D.3019
3019
/ 5 41

April 28 41.
List
of
publications

The Shanghai Press Censorship Office,
Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road.

Gentlemen,

I have to acknowledge receipt of your letter
dated April 25, 1941, and in reply regret to state that
in view of the magnitude of the task you ask, which
would involve the verification and tabulation of over
900 publications, the details of which are constantly
changing, this Force is unable to comply at present.

Should you desire details in respect of any
specific publication I shall be only too pleased to
oblige.

I am; Gentlemen,
Your obedient servant,

K.M.BOURNE
Commissioner of Police.

FILED BY
(S.S) REGISTRY
DATE / 5 / 41

CLK/.

3019

1941年4月28日。
出版物
清单

上海新闻检查办公室，
哈同大楼，
南京路。

诸位先生：

兹确认收到贵方1941年4月25日来信，并遗憾地回复称，鉴于贵方所要求的工作量巨大，涉及核实和编制900多种出版物的表格，且这些出版物的详情不断变化，本警务处目前无法照办。

如贵方希望获取任何特定出版物的详情，本人将非常乐意提供协助。

此致，
诸位先生，
你们顺从的仆人，

K.M. BOURNE
警务总监。

归档人
(S.S) 文书科
日期 / 5 / 41

CLK/.

page_data.en:
April 25, 1941.

Major K. M. Bourne,
Commissioner of Police,
S. M. C.

Sir,

We regret to trouble you at a time when you are
probably coping with a heavy pressure of work, but we
shall be much obliged if you will kindly make an
investigation and supply us with the following information:-

1. The names of newspapers, publishers and editors
together with the addresses and the S.M.C. Registration
numbers.

2. The names of magazines, publishers and editors
together with the addresses and the S.M.C. Registration
numbers.

3. The names of publishing offices and their responsible
persons together with the addresses and the principal
publications issued by these offices.

Yours sincerely,

(Sealed) Kato of the Shanghai
Press Censorship
Office, Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road.
page_data.zh:
1941年4月25日。

K. M. Bourne 少校，
警务总监，
上海公共租界工部局。

先生：

很抱歉在您可能正忙于繁重工作之时打扰您，但如蒙阁下进行调查并向我们提供以下信息，我们将不胜感激：-

1. 报纸名称、出版商及编辑姓名，连同地址及上海公共租界工部局注册号码。

2. 杂志名称、出版商及编辑姓名，连同地址及上海公共租界工部局注册号码。

3. 出版社名称及其负责人姓名，连同地址及这些出版社发行的主要出版物。

此致，

（盖章）加藤，上海
新闻检查
办公室，哈同大楼，
南京路。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTNo 3019
4th Floor, Nardo Building,
233 Nanking Road, Shanghai 41
February 27th, 1941.

re- Forwarding of extracts of anti-Japanese
articles from newspapers.

Sir,

With reference to undesirable anti-Japanese
articles appearing in Chinese language newspapers, we
have been forwarding extracts of such articles of an
important nature for your information; but this was dis-
continued towards the end of last year on account of
certain causes connected with this office. Commencing
from today the forwarding of extracts of important anti-
Japanese articles will be resumed.

It is respectfully requested that you will
utilize them for reference when censoring newspapers.

(Seal) Shanghai Press Censorship Office.
(Chop) Y. Sato.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 3019
January 31, 1941. 41

Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau - New chief appointed

Lieu Zah-keh (刘石克), Chief Editor of the
Central China Daily News (中華日報), Wang Ching-wei's
mouthpiece in Shanghai, No.59 North Honan Road, has been
authorized by Ling Pah-sen (林柏生), Minister of Publicity
of the Nanking Government, to act concurrently as Chief of
the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau, while his predecessor,
Kwang Hung-tsao (鄺鴻藻), an associate of Chen Fu-moo
(陈孚木), owner of the New China Daily News (新中國報),
308 Honan Road, and a member of the C.E.C. of the 'orthodox'
Kuomintang, has, on the recommendation of Mayor Chen Kung-po,
been appointed Magistrate of Feng Yen Hsien in Pootung.

Lieu Zah-keh has already assumbed his new post.
The expenditure of the Bureau is being covered with a sum of
$4,000 which has been issued monthly by the Ministry of
Publicity at Nanking.

The following are the staff of the Bureau :-
Senior Censor: Fu Tse-chen (符志成).
Censors in Chinese language: Do Pen-chen (杜本仁),
Li Ih (李一), Chen Pang (程鵬) and Oong Kan-chen (翁幹臣).
Censor in English language: Chen Kung (陈恭).
Censor in Japanese language: Chang Tsung-shao
(張忠孝).

In addition there are two assistant censors named
Chia Yung-sih (賈永) and Wu Kan-ziang (吳幹祥), who have
been detailed to the Bureau by the Shanghai City Government.

As no pro-Chungking morning and evening dailies
submit proofs to the Bureau for censorship, the work of the
censors is not particularly heavy.

1941年1月31日。 41

上海新闻检查局 - 新任局长任命

刘石克（Lieu Zah-keh），《中華日報》总编辑，该报为汪精卫在上海的喉舌，地址位于河南北路59号，已获南京政府宣传部长林柏生（Ling Pah-sen）授权，兼任上海新闻检查局局长；其前任鄺鴻藻（Kwang Hung-tsao）系河南路308号《新中國報》业主陈孚木（Chen Fu-moo）的亲信，也是“正统”国民党中执委成员，经市长陈公博推荐，已被任命为浦东奉贤县县长。

刘石克已就任新职。该局经费由南京宣传部每月拨付的4,000元款项支付。

该局职员如下：
高级检查员：符志成（Fu Tse-chen）。
中文检查员：杜本仁（Do Pen-chen）、李一（Li Ih）、程鵬（Chen Pang）和翁幹臣（Oong Kan-chen）。
英文检查员：陈恭（Chen Kung）。
日文检查员：張忠孝（Chang Tsung-shao）。

此外，还有两名助理检查员，名为賈永（Chia Yung-sih）和吳幹祥（Wu Kan-ziang），由上海市政府派往该局工作。

由于没有支持重庆方面的早报和晚报向该局提交校样以供审查，检查员的工作并不特别繁重。

Translation of Precis of Despatch No. T'e from S.C.G. Police Bureau.

January 11, 194 1.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

Instructional Order No. Pao Wu Hui 33 has been received from the Ministry of Policing Administration, which states inter alia:

"According to Letter No. Tao 41 from the Ministry of Propaganda, Shanghai Press Censorship Office was taken over by Japanese Military Authorities following their occupation of Shanghai in 1937, with an office in Hardoon Bldg., Nanking Road. With the return of the seat of the "National Government" to Nanking and the consent of Japanese Military Authorities, the Press Censorship Office has been put under the direct control of the "National Government". This Office having been taken over on December 16 and Kuang Hung Tsao having been appointed as Officer in Charge, the Ministry of Policing Administration is requested to detail an officer or two to jointly undertake the work of censorship in conformity with Article IV of the Regulations Governing Press Censorship, passed at the 27th Meeting of the "Administrative Yuan". Apart from an officer having been sent, the Ministry of Policing Administration is requested to take appropriate measures to accord protection".

The address of Shanghai Press Censorship Office being in the Settlement, I shall be greatly obliged you will kindly notify your subordinates to afford the Staff of that Office adequate protection.

(Signed): Loo Ying
Chief of the Bureau.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMM. 14 JAN. 1941）

上海市警察局第T'e号公函摘要译文。

1941年1月11日。

致 上海公共租界工部局警务处处长。

先生：

收到警政部指令第保武会33号，其中称：

“根据宣传部第陶41号函，上海新闻检查所于1937年日军占领上海后由日本军方接管，办公地点位于南京路哈同大楼。随着‘国民政府’还都南京以及日本军方的同意，新闻检查所已置于‘国民政府’的直接控制之下。该所已于12月16日接管，并任命鄺鴻藻为负责人，现请警政部依据‘行政院’第27次会议通过的《新闻检查条例》第四条，派遣一至两名官员共同承担检查工作。除派遣官员外，还请警政部采取适当措施予以保护。”

鉴于上海新闻检查所地址位于租界内，如蒙通知下属为该所职员提供充分保护，不胜感激。

Prior to the outbreak of the local hostilities on
August 13, 1937, the censorship of all Chinese language
newspapers and news agencies (except those of foreign
registered) was carried out by the Chinese Press Censorship
Bureau, Room 305 Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road,
under the control of Chen Kuh Zung (陳克成) and Chen Shun Ss
(陳訓慈). All manuscripts and proofs designated for the
local Chinese press were submitted to the Bureau for censor-
ship but no representatives of the Censorship Bureau were
detailed to the newspaper offices in the discharge of their
duties.

Following the retreat of the Chinese Forces from
Shanghai in November 1937, the Chinese Press Censorship
Bureau ceased functioning but the salaries of its staff
were secretly maintained on half-pay basis up until April 1939.

Shortly after the occupation of Shanghai by the
Japanese Forces, the Chinese Press Censorship Bureau was
instituted by the (Japanese) Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau,
located in Room 218, Hardoon Building, Nanking Road, which
was established jointly by the Japanese Expeditionary Forces
in Central China and the local Japanese Consulate-General.
Major S. Kaneko attached to the Headquarters of the Japanese
Expeditionary Forces in Central China and Mr. Y. Akita,
Consul and Chief of the Second Section of the Japanese
Consular Police were placed in charge, although the actual
functioning of the routine office work was carried out
under the directions of a Mr. Y. Kato. The censorship of
all local Chinese press and news agencies, however, actually

在1937年8月13日本地战事爆发前，所有中文报纸及通讯社（外国注册的除外）的检查工作均由位于南京路大陆商场305室的中华新闻检查局负责，受陈克成（Chen Kuh Zung）和陈训慈（Chen Shun Ss）控制。所有指定供本地中文报刊使用的稿件和校样均提交该局检查，但检查局并未派遣代表驻守报社执行职务。

1937年11月中国军队从上海撤退后，中华新闻检查局停止运作，但其职员的薪水以半薪形式秘密维持至1939年4月。

日军占领上海后不久，（日本）上海新闻检查局成立，该局位于南京路哈同大楼218室，由日本华中派遣军和日本驻上海总领事馆共同设立。隶属于日本华中派遣军司令部的 S. Kaneko 少校和日本领事警察第二科科长、领事 Y. Akita 先生负责主管，尽管日常办公工作的实际运作是在 Y. Kato 先生的指导下进行的。然而，对所有本地中文报刊和通讯社的检查实际上

lay in the hands of a number of Chinese assistants.
Because of the occasional appearance in publications
of articles criticising the Japanese sponsored Chinese
Municipal Authorities in Pootung, the Ta Tao Municipal
Government in May 1938 detailed one Sung Nyi(沈毅) to
the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau with specific instructions
to look after manuscripts unfavourable to the Ta Tao
Authorities.
In a similar manner the "Reformed Government" (then
located in Shanghai) following its inauguration in October,
1938, detailed one Lieu(刘 ), native of Hankow, to the
aforementioned Press Bureau for the purpose of examining
unfavourable references to the "Reformed Government" as
expressed in the manuscripts presented for censorship.
Commencing from February 1939 the two foregoing
representatives detailed by the Shanghai City Government
and the "Reformed Government" respectively, were placed
under the direct control of the Censorship Bureau.
With the intention of evading this press censorship,
a number of Chinese language pro-Chungking publications
registered their publications in the names of third Power
nationals and to a certain extent published articles of an
anti-Japanese nature and propaganda favourable to the
Chungking Regime, resultant from which the Shanghai Municipal
Council issued Notification No. 5092 dated 1-5-39 relative
to the dissemination of Political Propaganda, whilst due to
complaints re anti-Japanese propaganda from the Japanese
Consular Authorities, in July 1940 it was decreed by the
Shanghai Municipal Council that all political manifestos
should be submitted to the Special Branch of S.M. Police
before publication (Letter F.20/5 July 1940).
Commencing 7-8-40 it was decided that Police visits
should be made to newspaper offices for the purpose of
page_data.zh:
-2-

掌握在若干名华籍助理手中。
由于出版物中偶尔出现批评日本扶持的浦东中国市政当局的 articles，大道市政府于1938年5月特派一名沈毅（Sung Nyi）前往上海新闻检查局，并给予具体指示，要求其关注对大道当局不利的稿件。
同样地，“维新政府”（当时位于上海）在1938年10月成立后，也特派一名刘姓人士（Lieu，音译），汉口人，前往上述新闻局，目的是审查送审稿件中对“维新政府”的不利提及。
自1939年2月起，前述由上海市政府和“维新政府”分别派出的两名代表，被置于新闻检查局的直接管辖之下。
为了逃避这种新闻审查，一些支持重庆的中文刊物以第三国国民的名义注册其出版物，并在一定程度上刊登具有反日性质和支持重庆政权的宣传文章。因此，上海公共租界工部局发布了1939年5月1日的第5092号通告，涉及政治宣传的传播问题；同时，由于日本领事当局就反日宣传提出投诉，上海公共租界工部局于1940年7月颁布规定，所有政治宣言在出版前必须提交至上海公共租界警务处特务科（Letter F.20/5 July 1940）。
自1940年8月7日起，决定由警察走访报社，目的是

page_data.en:

examination of editorials, manifestoes, speeches and to
more generally supervise news items. This duty is being
carried out by members of the Special Branch, S.M.Police,
Chinese language publications being visited in rotation,
the pro-Chungking publications receiving the most attention
in respect to the publication of anti-Japanese and
political propaganda.

Following the inauguration of the National Government
of China in Nanking on November 30, 1940, on December 16, 1940,
the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau was handed over to the
jurisdiction of the National Government of China by the
Japanese Army Authorities.

In answer to the request of Mayor Chen Kung-po in
his despatch of 19-12-40, "that the Shanghai Municipal Council
urge newspapers in the International Settlement to send copies
to the Press Bureau for censorship", the Shanghai Municipal
Council have no power to enforce this request in respect to
newspapers under the registry of Third Power nationals with
extraterritorial rights.

Newspaper offices in the International Settlement
are under adequate Police protection.

审查社论、宣言、演讲，并更广泛地监督新闻项目。此项职责由上海公共租界警务处特务科成员执行，对中文出版物进行轮流走访，其中支持重庆的出版物因刊登反日及政治宣传内容而受到最多关注。

继1940年11月30日中华民国国民政府在南京成立之后，日本陆军当局于1940年12月16日将上海新闻检查局移交给中华民国国民政府管辖。

国际租界内的报社受到充分的警察保护。

Acting upon the instructions of the D.C.
(Special Branch), issued on the basis of the attached
letter from the Secretary and Commissioner-General,
and dated October 27, 1939, a visit was paid to the
offices of the "China Press" and the "Ta Mei Pao."

Interviewing Mr. Woo Kyatang in the former
case and Mr. M.C. Ford in the absence of Mr. Randall
Gould in the case of the "Ta Mei Pao," it was
explained to these gentlemen that the Consul-General
for Japan in Shanghai had completely denied the report
of "mutiny" among Japanese Troops in Hankow and desired
that a retraction be made.

Both undertook to publish the Japanese
denial and carried their undertaking into effect on
October 29th and 30th.

from the "Ta Mei Pao" attached (flagged).

Japanese
Protest
To S.M.C.

Groundless Allegations
In Press Are Subject
Of Two Notes

The Japanese Embassy spokesman told correspondents at yesterday's press conference that the Japanese Consul-General had made representations to the Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, Mr. C. S. Franklin, and to Mr. C. E. Gauss, the American Consul-General, protesting against the groundless allegation which appeared in several English language and Chinese language newspapers to the effect that a mutiny had broken out among the Japanese forces in Hankow.

The report, which purported to have been written by a person recently arrived from Hankow, was quite untrue, the spokesman said, and therefore Mr. Miura, the Japanese Consul-General, had requested Mr. Franklin to take suitable action in respect of these newspapers. The action of the Japanese Consul was based upon a memorandum from Mr. Franklin concerning anti-Japanese and other reports of a nature likely to endanger the peace.

The allegation was a groundless concoction spread by pro-Chungking groups and the Japanese authorities considered it a great insult to themselves. The attention of Mr. C. E. Gauss had been drawn to the matter with the request that he obtain a retraction of this allegation and an undertaking that no further reports of this kind would be published. Asked if by "suitable action" the Japanese meant suspension of publication, the spokesman replied that the Japanese had not been considering the question of the suspension of publication.

该指控是由支持重庆的团体散布的无端捏造，日本当局认为这是对他们的极大侮辱。此事已提请 C. E. Gauss 先生注意，并请他争取撤回这一指控，并保证不再刊登此类报道。当被问及日本方面所说的“适当行动”是否意味着停止出版时，发言人回答说，日本方面并未考虑停止出版的问题。

据日本大使馆发言人在昨日的记者招待会上透露，日本总领事三浦先生（Mr. Y. Miura）已请求上海公共租界工部局董事会主席C. S. 富兰克林先生（Mr. C. S. Franklin），就《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS）及数家美资中文报纸采取“适当行动”，因为这些报纸于10月21日刊登了关于日军在汉口发生兵变的报道。

此外，美国驻上海总领事高斯先生（Mr. Clarence E. Gauss）也注意到了该报道，他宣称，日本军方当局视此报道为“严重的侮辱和诽谤”。

发言人称，向富兰克林先生提出的请求是基于日本方面于4月29日收到其备忘录中的条款，该备忘录涉及控制反日文章及扰乱和平秩序文章的出版。

他断言：“不言而喻，所谓兵变的指控是毫无根据的捏造，显然是为了重庆政府的利益而散布的。”

发言人表示，已提请高斯先生注意此事，并请他运用其影响力，“以促使撤回这种毫无根据的指控，并防止此类事件再次发生”。

当被问及“适当行动”是否可能意味着暂停涉事报纸的出版时，发言人予以否认，称这仅意味着“撤回报道并提出警告”。

他补充说，目前尚未收到富兰克林先生或高斯先生的回复，因为关于该报道的通知及要求采取行动的请求刚刚发送给他们。

Sir,

At the request of the Japanese military authorities
I have the honour to refer you to my memoranda of April 12
and April 26 this year, and your memorandum of April 29 this
year, concerning the control of the publication of articles
which are anti-Japanese and/or disturb peace and order, and
to draw your attention to an article which appeared in the
China Press and some of the Chinese-language newspapers on
October 21, alleging that a mutiny had occurred in the Japan-
ese forces in Hankow.

In the first place, the allegation is groundless
concoction obviously circulated in the interest of the Chung-
king Government. The Japanese forces in China have special
requirements for the purpose of safeguarding their own
security, and have to suppress any such acts or causes as
will obstruct them or benefit their enemy. Moreover, any
unfounded allegations of such a character constitute a grave
insult and slander to the Imperial Japanese Army.

I have the honour, therefore, to request you to be
good enough to take suitable steps respecting the newspapers,
in accordance with the letter and spirit of the above-mentioned
memoranda, so that they will retract the article under reference
and refrain from any repetition of such a case in the future.

I have the honour to be,

Sir,

page_data.en:
OCT 21 1939
Ta Mei Pao :-

MUTINY AMONG JAPANESE TROOPS AT HANKOW

A rumour has been current to the effect that
a mutiny took place among the Japanese troops in Hankow
two days ago. At first the rumour gained no credence
at all, but confirmation of this report was received
yesterday by a reporter of this paper from a recent
foreign arrival from Hankow and from the officials of
a certain local foreign Consulate.
Briefly the facts are as follows :-
There are in all two Divisions of Japanese
troops in Hankow. Owing to the prolongation of the
hostilities and the lack of definite date for their
conclusion, the soldiers have felt dissatisfied with
their mission, with the result that a part of them
openly revolted and refused to take orders from their
superior officers. The trouble was not checked until
the execution of 13 ringleaders of the trouble-makers
and after strenuous efforts had been made by the Japanese
military officers in curbing the spreading of the trouble.
As a result, one of the two Divisions was immediately
transferred elsewhere, while the other Division was sent
to the front in North Hunan. The Japanese authorities
are maintaining strict secrecy as regards this incident
and are prohibiting any disclosure of the facts of this
affair. Owing to the adoption by the Japanese authorities
of a strict censorship of newspapers coupled with the
fact that they are being subjected to restrictions of
their movements, even the foreign residents at the place
were not in a position to gain any definite knowledge of
the incident. What is worthy of attention is that ever
since the Japanese occupation of the Wuhan area, never have
Japanese wounded soldiers been seen being transported to
warships, though Japanese transports have frequently been
noticed coming to and from Hankow. It is now learned that
the wounded Japanese soldiers are transported to warships
by trucks in the night.
page_data.zh:
1939年10月21日
《大美报》：

汉口日军士兵发生兵变

有谣言称，两天前汉口日军士兵中发生了兵变。起初该谣言完全无人相信，但本报记者昨日从一位刚从汉口抵达的外国人以及某当地外国领事馆官员处获得了证实。
简要事实如下：
汉口共有两个师团的日军。由于战事 prolonged（延长）且结束日期未定，士兵们对任务感到不满，导致部分士兵公开反抗，拒绝服从上级军官的命令。直到处决了13名肇事头目，且日本军官努力遏制事态蔓延后，骚乱才得以平息。
结果，其中一个师团立即被调往他处，另一个师团则被派往湘北前线。日本当局对此事严守秘密，禁止泄露任何相关事实。由于日本当局实行严格的新闻审查，加上人员流动受到限制，就连当地的外国居民也无法得知此事的确切情况。值得注意的是，自日军占领武汉地区以来，从未见过日军伤兵被运往军舰，尽管经常观察到日本运输船往返于汉口。现获悉，日军伤兵是在夜间通过卡车运往军舰的。

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 21 1938
Japanese Army
Revolt Report
Reaches Here
News Of Mutiny Two
Months Old Brought
From Hankow
Out of censor-sealed Hankow yesterday, leaked a story that spells dynamite—mutiny in the Japanese army.
The news is not from yesterday or last week. It is two months old at least and it has been coming in by the "bamboo telegraph" for some time, a route sufficient in itself to discredit any rumor. Yesterday, however, it was confirmed from two sources here, a prominent foreigner newly arrived from Hankow and a local consular official.
The facts of the matter, it was learned, were that two Japanese Army divisions garrisoned in Hankow since the beginning of the war became increasingly disaffected with the ineffectual prolongation of the conflict and several small units broke into open revolt, refusing to obey orders.
Execution for 12 of the men, it was declared, ended the mutiny. One of the divisions was immediately sent away from Hankow and the other is believed to have been assigned to take part in the recent Changsha campaign.
The arrival from Hankow said yesterday that even for foreigners living in that city news is most difficult to obtain as movement is restricted and the ring of censors is unrelenting. He gave as an example the fact that a Japanese wounded soldier is never seen being transported through the streets, and yet the number of hospital ships which enter the river port is apparently never ending. But all sick and wounded are taken aboard at night. The ships, too, invariably sail by night.
The spirit of the native Chinese of the city is almost openly patriotic, the same source declared. The most important topic of daily conversation is the "not distant" entry of Chinese troops into the city.
Del Fuh

1938年10月21日
日军
兵变报告
传抵此处
来自汉口的消息显示兵变发生于两个月前
昨日，从受新闻审查封锁的汉口泄露出一则如炸药般惊人的消息——日军发生兵变。
这则新闻并非来自昨天或上周。它至少已有两个月之久，并且一段时间以来一直通过“竹电”（指民间非正式渠道）传来，这种途径本身就足以让人对任何谣言产生怀疑。然而，昨天这里有两个来源证实了这一消息：一位刚从汉口抵达的知名外籍人士和一名当地领事馆官员。
据悉，事实真相是，自战争爆发以来驻守汉口的两个日本陆军师团，因冲突无效地 prolonged（延长/拖延）而日益不满，几个小部队发动公开叛乱，拒绝服从命令。
据称，处决了其中12名士兵后，兵变得以平息。其中一个师团立即被调离汉口，另一个师团据信已被指派参加最近的长沙战役。
这位从汉口来的人昨天说，即使对于居住在该城市的外国人来说，获取新闻也极为困难，因为行动受到限制，且新闻审查官的包围圈毫不放松。他举了一个例子：从未见过有日本伤兵在街道上被运送，然而进入江港的医院船只数量显然源源不断。但所有病患和伤员都是在夜间被送上船的。这些船只也总是在夜间航行。
该消息源还宣称，该市中国本土居民的爱国精神几乎是公开流露的。日常谈话中最重要的话题是中国军队“不远”将进入该市。
Del Fuh

Subject... Shanghai Press Censorship

Made by ... and ... Forwarded by ... D.S.I. Golder.

Prior to the outbreak of the local hostilities
on August 13, 1937, the censorship of all newspapers
and news agencies was carried out by the Chinese Press
Censorship Bureau, Room 306, Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road, under the control of Chen
Kuh-zung (陈克成) and Chen Shun-sz (陈訓慈). All
manuscripts and proofs designated for the local Chinese
press were submitted to the Bureau for censorship, but
no representatives of the Censorship Bureau were detailed
to the newspaper offices in the discharge of their
duties.

Following the retreat of the Chinese forces
from Shanghai in November 1937, the Chinese Press
Censorship Bureau ceased functioning, but the salaries
of its staff were secretly maintained on half-pay basis
up until April, of this year.

Shortly after the occupation of Shanghai by
the Japanese forces, the Chinese Press Censorship Bureau
was instituted by the (Japanese) Shanghai Press Censorship
Bureau, located in Room 218, Hardoon Building, Nanking
Road, which was established jointly by the Japanese
Expeditionary Forces in Central China and the local
Japanese Consulate-General. Major S. Kaneko attached
to the Headquarters of the Japanese Expeditionary Forces
in Central China and Mr. Y. Akiba, Consul and Chief of
the Second Section of the Japanese Consular Police were
placed in charge, although the actual functioning of
the routine office work was carried out under the

在1937年8月13日本地战事爆发之前，所有报纸和通讯社的新闻审查工作均由位于南京路大陆商场大楼306室的中国新闻检查局执行，该局由陈克成（Chen Kuh-zung）和陈训慈（Chen Shun-sz）控制。所有指定供本地中文报刊发表的手稿和校样均提交给该局进行审查，但新闻检查局并未派遣代表进驻各报社履行其职责。

随着1937年11月中国军队从上海撤退，中国新闻检查局停止运作，但其工作人员的薪水仍以半薪形式秘密维持至今年四月。

日军占领上海后不久，中国新闻检查局被（日本）上海新闻检查局所取代，后者位于南京路哈同大楼218室，由日本华中派遣军和当地日本总领事馆共同设立。隶属于日本华中派遣军司令部的金子（S. Kaneko）少佐和日本领事馆警察第二科科长、领事秋叶（Y. Akiba）先生负责主管，尽管日常办公工作的实际运作是在

Translation of the attached letter.

March 27, 1939.

To Major K.M. Bourne,
the Commissioner of Police, S.M.P.

Re. Request to prevent reissue of Hong Pao.

Sir,
The police action to suspend the Hong Pao
(紅報) was requested by letter dated March 22 and we have
to tender our deep appreciation for the prompt action taken
by the police.
However, according to information received by
this office the management of the Hong Pao is now contemplating
to reissue the newspaper by registering with the British or
American Consulate-General. Therefore we shall be much
obliged if the Municipal Police would refuse the re-registration
of this newspaper.

Yours Sincerely,

(Chop) Shanghai Press Censorship Office.

On the morning of March 25, Mr. S. Nishina, staff
member of the Japanese Press Censorship Office, Rooms 218-233,

Branch) regarding the request for action against the Hung Pao
(红报), the Soochow Kung Pao (苏州公报) and the Siao Tien Sz
(小天使). Mr. Nishina stated that the general complaint
against these three papers was that they had submitted their
articles to the Press Censorship Office, certain parts had
been deleted and the deletions had been ignored by the editors
who published the articles in their entirety.

A specific complaint was laid against the Soochow
Kung Pao namely that an article was published on March 22 on
the controversial subject of the flying of national flags
(translation attached) and this article was considered definitely
anti-Japanese.

The complaint against the Hung Pao was that on March 22,
an article was published (translation attached) which obviously
referred to the alleged oppressive activities of Japanese plain
clothes soldiers and was decidedly objectionable from the
Japanese point of view. Another complaint was that in the
same issue, a poem (translation attached) was inserted which
obviously referred in a derogatory manner to the Japanese and
was likely to instigate anti-Japanese sentiments.

The question of the third paper, the Siao Tien Sz, was
not discussed as the paper voluntarily suspended publication
on March 24, not for the reason contained in an item published
on March 24 to the effect that the S.M.P. had banned the
publication, as the editor was merely invited to Police

3月25日上午，日本新闻检查办公室职员西仁（S. Nishina，音译）先生（办公地点：南京路哈同大楼218-233室）拜访了特别分部副主管（D.C.），就请求对《红报》（Hung Pao）、《苏州公报》（Soochow Kung Pao）和《小天使》（Siao Tien Sz）采取行动一事进行交涉。西仁先生表示，对这三家报纸的一般性投诉是，它们已将文章提交给新闻检查办公室，某些部分被删除，但编辑无视这些删改，全文刊登了这些文章。

针对《苏州公报》的具体投诉是，该报于3月22日刊登了一篇关于悬挂国旗这一争议性话题的文章（附译文），该文章被认为具有明确的反日性质。

对《红报》的投诉是，该报于3月22日刊登了一篇文章（附译文），该文显然指的是据称日本便衣士兵的压迫活动，从日本方面的角度来看是绝对令人反感的。另一项投诉是，在同一期报纸中，插入了一首诗（附译文），该诗显然以贬低的方式提及日本人，并可能煽动反日情绪。

关于第三家报纸《小天使》的问题未予讨论，因为该报已于3月24日自愿停刊，其原因并非如3月24日刊登的一则消息所称系工部局警务处禁止出版，而仅仅是编辑被邀请至警察

page_data.en:
Soochow Kung Pao (苏州公报) published the following
article on March 22, 1939:

ANNIVERSARY OF THE ARRIVAL OF NATIONALIST ARMY
IN SHANGHAI

I observed with particular attention that the
anniversary of the arrival of the Nationalist Army in
Shanghai, which fell yesterday (March 21) passed off quietly
save for the flying of national flags from local shops and
public bodies. I think that the fellow townsmen of Soochow
must have also noticed the flying of national flags.

Flying of national flags is a spiritual expression.
By hoisting their national flags, the people of Shanghai
show that their spirit is not extinct.

Soochow naturally has a day of its own. Now I
ask my fellow townsmen to meditate that what will Soochow do
on such an occasion? Can she display national flags the
same as Shanghai? No, I fear even the occasion will be
abolished.

My heart feels hurt when the sight of the national
flag reminds me of my lost native place.
page_data.zh:
《苏州公报》于1939年3月22日刊登了以下文章：

国军抵沪周年纪念

我特别注意到，昨日（3月21日）适逢国军抵达上海周年纪念日，除当地商铺及公共机构悬挂国旗外，一切平静度过。我想苏州同乡想必也注意到了悬挂国旗之举。

悬挂国旗是一种精神表达。上海市民通过升起国旗，表明其精神并未泯灭。

苏州自然有它自己的日子。现在我请我的同乡们深思，苏州在此类场合会怎么做？她能像上海一样展示国旗吗？不，我担心甚至连这个场合都会被取消。

当看到国旗让我想起沦丧的故乡时，我的心感到伤痛。

page_data.en:
Hung Pao (红报) published on March 22 the following
article written by one Kwoh Fu Kwoh Jen (谷夫谷人):

On Christmas eve in 1928, the war clouds became
so black that after one night, an extensive area was converted
into the spoils of war of a foreign nation.
On the following morning, when he was getting up
from his bed, about 20 plainclothes soldiers of a foreign
nation came into his home arrogantly. One of these soldiers,
a very-sized one, without any cause, slapped him in the
face and made him faint.
Noise of the throwing articles and cries and reports
of firing were heard.
When the soldiers of the foreign nation had gone
away, he came to his senses and hurried back to the house,
finding that his mother and his sister had disappeared. On
taking a further look at the house, he cried loudly for he
found that his father and his brother were lying in a pool
of blood.

Hung Pao published on March 22 the following letter written
by one Shih Ying (时影):

TO A LATE FRIEND

Tseng (珍),
You have at last sacrificed your life under
brutal oppression,
In the struggle for liberty.
You have bravely assumed your dutiful mission.
Keep on your sentry duty,
You have done work not shameful towards your
country
Up to your death you have not compromised with
the robbers.
Nay, you have not yielded even for one minute.

Friend, you must have seen
That in the war of resistance you have fulfilled
your duty,
And that the other part of the work is for us
who will die later.

《红报》于3月22日刊登了一篇由谷夫谷人撰写的文章：

1928年圣诞前夕，战云密布，一夜之间，大片区域沦为某外国的战利品。
次日清晨，当他从床上起身时，约20名某外国便衣士兵傲慢地闯入他的家中。其中一名身材魁梧的士兵，无缘无故地扇了他一记耳光，致使他昏厥。
只听得投掷物品的声响、哭喊声以及枪声。
当那些外国士兵离去后，他苏醒过来，急忙返回屋内，发现母亲和妹妹已不见踪影。再仔细查看屋内，他放声大哭，因为发现父亲和兄弟倒在血泊之中。

《红报》于3月22日刊登了一封由时影撰写的信件：

致一位亡友

珍，
你终于在残酷的压迫下，
在争取自由的斗争中，
牺牲了你的生命。
你勇敢地承担了你的使命。
坚守你的哨位，
你做了无愧于国家的工作，
直至死亡，你都未与强盗妥协。
不，你甚至一分钟都没有屈服。

朋友，你一定看到了，
在抗战中你已尽到了你的职责，
而工作的另一部分，则留给我们这些稍后赴死的人。

The "Siao Tien Sz" (小天使), a three-day periodical,
publishes the following notice in its paper on March 24,
1939 :-

Acting on an order received from the Municipal
Police Headquarters, this paper will suspend publication
as from this date.

----------

At the same time, the paper publishes the
following article entitled "Farewell to Readers" :-

From its first appearance up to the present issue,
this paper has never submitted its proofs to the
Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau for examination. On
account of this point, the enemy in conjunction with the
Police authorities of the Settlement has warned us on
several occasions. On March 23, the S.M.P. sent
officers to the office of this paper for the purpose of
withdrawing our registration certificate.

When this paper was publishing its last issue,
our hot blood began to run swiftly. However, we will
not repent and will look for a chance at any time.

----------

从创刊至今期，本报从未将校样提交上海新闻检查局审查。因此点，敌人与租界警务当局曾多次警告我们。3月23日，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）派员至本报社，旨在吊销我们的注册证书。

SHANGHAI PRESS CENSORSHIP BUREAU 3019
January 12, 1939. 21 / 1 3

Major Bourne,
Commissioner of Police,
S. M. C.

Re--- a notice to the "Ta Ying Yeh Pao"

Sir,

We are informed that the S.M.C. has declared that it
has no authority to interfere with newspapers and magazines
published by foreigners enjoying extraterritoriality in China.
It seems that the S.M.C. has likewise acknowledged this to
be a fact. However, it is believed that the S.M.C. has a
right to approach the diplomatic authorities or the Consul
concerned when a newspaper or magazine of foreign registration
does something that destroys the neutrality of the
International Settlement or that obstructs the maintenance
of peace and order.

Since its formation this Bureau has been sending letters
to Chinese language newspapers of foreign registration
attention
drawing/to the fact that they were violating their neutrality
as nationals of a third Power when they criticise the
Japanese Empire or the Japanese Army and when they publish
anything which instigates anti-Japanese sentiment among the
Chinese people.

This notice is hereby sent to you to show how the foreign
owned newspapers are violating their neutrality and in the
hope that you will deal with the foreign owned newspapers
within your jurisdiction. This Bureau will hereafter send
a copy of such notices to you in the hope that the S.M.C.
will adopt suitable measures to deal with the offenders
according to Municipal authority.

A copy of the notice sent to the "Ta Ying Yeh Pao" on

工部局。

关于——致《大英夜报》的通知

先生，

据悉，工部局已声明其无权干涉在中国享有治外法权的外国人出版的报刊杂志。看来工部局也已承认此为事实。然而，据信，当注册为外国的报刊杂志做出破坏国际租界中立或阻碍维持和平与秩序的行为时，工部局有权接触外交当局或相关领事。

自本局成立以来，一直致函注册为外国的中文报纸，提请注意这样一个事实：即当它们批评日本帝国或日本军队，以及发表任何煽动中国人民反日情绪的内容时，它们作为第三国国民违反了其中立立场。

现发送此通知给您，以显示外商拥有的报纸如何违反其中立立场，并希望您能处理管辖范围内的外商报纸。此后，本局将把此类通知的副本发送给您，希望工部局能根据市政权限采取适当措施处理违规者。

To the editor of the Ta Ying Yeh Pao,

This Office has to inform you that the article
entitled "Anti-War Feeling Growing - Many suicides among
Japanese Soldiers in Nantao", which appeared on the second
page of your paper dated January 11, is evidently an
unfounded fabrication intended to defame the good name
of the Japanese army with the object of promoting an
anti-Japanese movement.

As your paper claims to belong to British interests,
you should maintain a neutral attitude. Since you are
now disregarding the personal stand of a newspaper and
are hostile towards Japan, this Office hereby issues a
warning that hereafter no article detrimental to the
Japanese army or of an anti-Japanese nature should be
published, otherwise this Office will regard your paper
as an organized anti-Japanese paper.

The Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau

page_data.en:
Ta Ying Yeh Pao (11-1) and Standard (12-1)

x File. D8039.5/12

SUICIDE AMONG JAPANESE SOLDIERS IN NANTAO

During the 18 months of military operations
in China, the Japanese have lost 800,000 men in killed and
wounded.
In order to check the growing activities of
Chinese mobile units in various guerrilla districts, the
Japanese are transferring to the front lines all the men
stationed in the rear for garrison duty. For example, a
detachment of Japanese soldiers at Nantao will be transferred
by the end of this month and will be replaced by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. It is learned that in future the
Japanese Naval Landing Party will replace all the Japanese
military forces in the districts surrounding Shanghai.
Considerable agitation was caused among
Japanese soldiers when they learned of their impending
transfer and many committed suicide. For instance, four
Japanese soldiers took their lives at the former site of
the Flour Exchange at Hsin Kai Ho (新闸河), Nantao Bund,
and 17 at the Van Tsoh Primary School (萬竹小學), Nantao.
The Pan Soong Yuen Garden (半淞園) in Nantao has become
a favourite place for suicides.
According to information received, there
have been about 300 suicide cases among the Japanese
garrison forces at Nantao during the past 15 months, amongst
whom were a number of officers.
page_data.zh:
《大英夜报》（1月11日）和《标准晚报》（1月12日）

x 档案. D8039.5/12

南市日军自杀事件

在中国军事行动进行的18个月期间，日军伤亡人数达80万。
为了遏制各游击区中国机动部队日益活跃的活动，日军正将所有驻守后方执行卫戍任务的人员调往前线。例如，南市的一支日军分队将在本月月底调离，并由日本海军陆战队接替。据悉，未来日本海军陆战队将接替上海周边地区的所有日军部队。
当日军士兵得知即将调防时，引起了相当大的骚动，许多人自杀。例如，四名日本士兵在南市新闸河码头的前面粉交易所旧址自杀，另有17人在南市萬竹小學自杀。南市的半淞園已成为自杀的热门地点。
据收到的消息，在过去15个月中，南市日军卫戍部队中约有300起自杀案件，其中包括多名军官。

CHUNGKING, Nov. 5 (Kuo-min)—The 7th regular meeting of the 2nd session of the National People's Political Assembly was held here yesterday. Mr. Wang Ching-wei, President of the Assembly, presided and 188 members were present.
After the meeting was called to order, Dr. Wang Shih-chieh, Secretary-General of the Assembly, read the minutes of the 6th meeting, and announced that Mr. Cheng Chen-yu, a member of the Assembly, was absent on account of urgent business.
The written replies of the Ministries of Economics and Education and the War-Time Relief Commission, to several questions raised at the 6th meeting, were then read.
Censorship To Be Abolished
An important proposal jointly made by Mr. Tsou Tao-fen and 73 other members—calling for abolition of the censorship on books, magazines and other publications, in order to safeguard the freedom of speech and press, was unanimously adopted.
Several other resolutions were also adopted, calling for:
Promotion of closer relations with the people in the outlying and frontier regions.
Acceleration of the enforcement of Local Autonomy.
Promulgation of the law governing the organization of District Governments.
Enlistment of the services of factory engineers and experts by the Government within a definite time-limit.
Allotment of foreign exchange for the purchase of minimum scientific equipment for schools of higher education (colleges and universities).
Assembly Members Wounded
Before adjournment Mr. Wang Ching-wei, President of the Assembly, announced that Mr. Liang Tung-lung, a member of the Assembly, who was recently dispatched to the war-front on an inspection trip, in the company of representatives of the Military Affairs Commission, Central Party Headquarters, and the Control Yuan, had been wounded during a Japanese air raid "somewhere at the front."
Another member of the Assembly, Mr. Chang Chiang, who was with Mr. Liang, was also wounded. Mr. Chang has now recovered from his wounds, but Mr. Liang's condition remains serious, his right arm having been amputated in order to save his life.
Following Mr. Wang's report, the meeting decided to send a telegram of confidence to Mr. Liang, commending him for his sacrifice for the sake of the state.

重庆，11月5日电（国民通讯社）——第二届国民参政会第七次定期会议昨日在此举行。参政会主席汪精卫先生主持会议，出席议员188人。
会议开始后，参政会秘书长王世杰博士宣读第六次会议记录，并宣布参政员程天放因急事缺席。
随后宣读了经济部、教育部及战时救济委员会对第六次会议所提若干问题的书面答复。
将废除审查制度
邹韬奋先生与其他73位议员联合提出的一项重要提案——呼吁废除对书籍、杂志及其他出版物的审查，以保障言论和出版自由——获得一致通过。
其他几项决议也获得通过，呼吁：
加强与边远及边疆地区人民的联系。
加速推行地方自治。
颁布区政府组织法。
政府在限期内征用工厂工程师及专家的服务。
拨给外汇，用于购买高等教育机构（学院和大学）所需的最低限度的科学设备。
参政员受伤
休会前，参政会主席汪精卫先生宣布，参政员梁寒操近期随军事委员会、中央党部及监察院代表前往前线视察，在“前线某地”遭遇日军空袭时受伤。
另一位与梁同行的参政员张江也受了伤。张先生现已伤愈，但梁先生情况仍然严重，为保命已截去右臂。
汪先生报告后，会议决定向梁先生发出慰问电，表彰其为国牺牲的精神。

The "Hwa Mei Chen Pao" publishes the following translation
of an article appearing in yesterday's issue of the "Shanghai
Mainichi," a local Japanese daily :-

Numerous articles have been published by this paper,
(the "Shanghai Mainichi,") regarding anti-Japanese Chinese
publications in both the International Settlement and the
French Concession in Shanghai in order to urge the authorities
to bring about their suppression. Yet no restrictions have
been placed upon them. Perhaps the authorities are tacitly
tolerating them or it may be that these anti-Japanese Chinese
newspapers have disregarded (?) their orders.

We are surprised to find that the contents of these
publications have been so outrageously anti-Japanese, especially
during the past few days. From the time of the outbreak of the
hostilities up to the fall of Shanghai, the attitude of Chinese
newspapers has been surprisingly anti-Japanese. Sometimes they
anger us, at other times they amuse us. The Chinese newspapers
which had remained silent after the fall of Shanghai have once
more become exceedingly active in the publication of anti-
Japanese articles. That anti-Japanese newspapers can still
be allowed publication in Shanghai, especially at this time
when Shanghai has been under Japanese occupation for more than
six months, is indeed an extraordinary phenomenon that should
never have been permitted in Shanghai.

We refuse to admit that we are inferior to Chinese
newspapers so far as love of justice and the personality of
newspapermen are concerned. We may be greatly displeased
with the views expressed by the anti-Japanese Chinese
publications, but we are not afraid to meet them in debate.
It is for this reason that we are in sympathy with and respect
the "Ta Kung Pao," the "Shun Pao," the "China Times," the "Lih
Pao" and other Chinese newspapers which had removed to the

《华美晨报》刊登了以下译文，译自当地日文日报《上海每日新闻》昨日发表的一篇文章：-

本报（《上海每日新闻》）已发表多篇文章，涉及上海公共租界和法租界内的反日中文出版物，旨在敦促当局予以取缔。然而，这些出版物并未受到限制。或许当局在默许容忍，又或者是这些反日中文报纸无视（？）其命令。

我们惊讶地发现，这些出版物的内容如此猖狂地反日，尤其是在过去几天里。从战事爆发到上海沦陷期间，中国报纸的态度令人惊讶地反日。有时令我们愤怒，有时又令我们觉得可笑。上海沦陷后曾保持沉默的中国报纸，如今再次变得极其活跃，刊登反日文章。在上海已被日本占领六个多月之际，反日报纸仍被允许在上海出版，这确实是一种本不应在上海出现的异常现象。

就正义感和报格而言，我们绝不承认自己逊色于中国报纸。我们可能非常不赞成反日中文出版物所表达的观点，但我们并不害怕与其辩论。正因如此，我们同情并尊重《大公报》、《申报》、《时事新报》、《立报》以及其他在上海沦陷后迁往

（印章：SHANGHAI MUNI... - 1938年5月7日 特别处）
（批注：FILE ... 9/5）

page_data.en:
- 2 -

interior after the fall of Shanghai.

Following their suspension, new publications,
such as the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao," the "Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning
Edition," the "Standard" and the "Morning Leader" made their
appearance in Shanghai. The publishers of all these papers
are foreigners and the papers are all registered with foreign
Consulates. Actually, however, they are run by anti-Japanese
elements.

Though we have nominally been in control of the
Chinese Newspaper Censorship Bureau since the fall of Shanghai,
actually we are still powerless. No satisfactory solution
can be brought about unless the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements adopt a sincere attitude. They should suppress
the publications, within their jurisdiction, of such newspapers,
irrespective of the fact whether they are of British or
American or Abyssinian registration, because not only are
these newspapers instigating the Chinese people to oppose
the "Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic" but they
are also inciting anti-Japanese feelings among the people.
The authorities of the Foreign Settlements should adopt
drastic and effective measures to suppress the publication
of these anti-Japanese Chinese newspapers within their
jurisdiction.

(Note by editor of the "Hwa Mei Chen Pao" :
Since September 16 last year our paper has been banned for
transmission to Japan. We were notified by Mr. Chapelain,
Commissioner of the Shanghai Postal Administration, that
according to a communication from the Tokyo Post Office,
the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" is now regarded as prohibited postal
matter and its copies are therefore detained and destroyed).

- 2 -

内地的中国报纸。

随着这些报纸的停刊，新的出版物如《华美晚报》、《大美晚报晨刊》、《文汇报》和《导报》在上海出现。所有这些报纸的发行人均为外国人，且均在外国领事馆注册。然而实际上，它们是由反日分子经营的。

尽管自上海沦陷以来，我们在名义上控制着中文报纸审查局，但实际上我们仍然无能为力。除非租界当局采取真诚的态度，否则无法达成令人满意的解决方案。他们应在其管辖范围内取缔此类报纸的出版，无论其是英国、美国还是阿比西尼亚注册，因为这些报纸不仅在煽动中国人民反对“中华民国维新政府”，还在民众中煽动反日情绪。租界当局应采取严厉有效的措施，在其管辖范围内取缔这些反日中文报纸的出版。

（《华美晨报》编辑注：
自去年9月16日起，本报被禁止寄往日本。上海邮政管理局局长Chapelain先生通知我们，根据东京邮局的来函，《华美晚报》现被视为禁寄邮件，因此其副本被扣留并销毁）。

March 21, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa l:ei Wan Pao Lorning Edition publishes the following
article written by one Wang Tseng-min (王正民) :-

WHICH DO YOU LIKE TO BE: A BONA-FIDE RESIDENT IN THE
OCCUPIED AREAS OR A LOYAL AND PATRIOTIC CITIZEN?

The expression "bona-fide resident"
has been bestowed upon us by the soldiers of our
friendly nation. With a view to distinguishing bona-
fide residents from others and as a measure of
precaution against untoward events, the Pacification
Section of the Special Affairs Department of the Army
undertakes the issue of "bona-fide residence" certificates
in conjunction with the autonomous committees. On
such permits, particulars as to age, sex, native place
and address are clearly indicated. If one intends
to take up one's residence in the areas wherein "kingly"
rights and heavenly bliss and happiness exist, one has
to take out such a permit, otherwise one is liable
to be suspected of being a member of the mobile unit
and come to an untimely end.

A large number of so-called bona-fide
residents have approached the autonomous committees
for registration and humbly and respectfully applied
to the Pacification Section of the Special Affairs
Department of the Army for certificates, so that they
can live a peaceful life in this paradise. However,
before applying for registration, one should reflect
carefully whether one has the necessary qualifications
required of a bona-fide resident.

What are the necessary qualifications
required of a bona-fide resident? What is the procedure
to be followed in applying for a bona-fide residence
certificate? All this can be easily ascertained by
a spineless applicant.

In the occupied areas, politeness
must be rigidly observed, especially when meeting with
members of the Imperial Army. Consequently, when a
bona-fide resident happens to be out on the streets,
he has to take off his hat many times in saluting
members of the Imperial Army. A slight attempt on his
part to evade the observance of this rule will bring
his head into contact with the butt of a rifle.

Moreover, to facilitate searches by
the Imperial Army, bona-fide residents must leave the
front gates of their houses open at night and when
searches are made, no matter how late at night, the
bona-fide resident must dress and get out from his bed
and stand by politely. Members of the Imperial Army
are not only mighty in war, but they are equally
familiar with affairs of love between men and women.
Therefore, in many instances, under the pretext of
conducting a search, the members of the Imperial Army
have intruded into the inner chambers of homes and
insisted on a pleasure trip with inmates. It would be
impolite for the female inmates to reject the kindly
offer of friendship extended to them by the members of
the Imperial Army, even though they cannot accept such
kindness without shame. Thus, the bona-fide residents
may one day have the experience of seeing their wives or
daughters or sisters being subjected to criminal assault
under their noses.

《华立晚报》晨刊刊登了一篇由王正民撰写的文章，内容如下：-

你愿做哪一种人：占领区的“良民”还是忠诚爱国的公民？

“良民”这一称呼是我们的友邦士兵赐予我们的。为了将良民与其他人区分开来，并作为预防不测事件的措施，陆军特务部绥靖科会同自治委员会负责签发“良民证”。此类证件上清楚注明了年龄、性别、籍贯和地址等详情。如果一个人打算在享有“王道”乐土和天赐幸福的地方居住，就必须申领此类证件，否则就会被怀疑是流动部队成员而招致杀身之祸。

大批所谓的良民已前往自治委员会登记，并谦卑恭敬地向陆军特务部绥靖科申请证件，以便在这个天堂里过上安宁的生活。然而，在申请登记之前，人们应当仔细反思自己是否具备良民所必需的条件。

良民必须具备哪些必要条件？申请良民证的程序又是怎样的？所有这些，一个没有骨气的申请者很容易就能弄清楚。

在占领区，必须严格遵守礼节，尤其是在遇到帝国军队成员时。因此，当良民外出上街时，必须多次脱帽向帝国军队成员致敬。如果他稍有试图逃避遵守这一规则的行为，他的头就会撞上步枪的枪托。

此外，为了方便帝国军队搜查，良民必须在夜间敞开家门，并且无论深夜何时进行搜查，良民都必须穿衣起床，礼貌地站在一旁。帝国军队成员不仅战功赫赫，而且对男女之间的情爱之事也同样熟悉。因此，在许多情况下，帝国军队成员以搜查为借口，闯入内室，强行要求与屋内人员寻欢作乐。女性住户若拒绝帝国军队成员伸出的友好橄榄枝，便是不礼貌的，尽管她们接受这种“好意”时会感到羞耻。因此，良民有一天可能会亲眼目睹自己的妻子、女儿或姐妹在眼皮底下遭受刑事侵犯。

The so-called paradise wherein "kingly"

should not go to live there. For the sake of our
personal happiness as well as for the independence of
our nation and the existence of the Chinese race, let
us not be bona-fide residents under oppression, but let
us become loyal and patriotic citizens by resisting
at personal sacrifices!

Standard and other local newspapers: 12-5-38 (A.M.)

JAPANESE TO CENSOR FOREIGN NEWS AGENCIES' REPORTS

Following the withdrawal of the Chinese forces
from Shanghai and Woosung, all Chinese owned newspapers
published in Shanghai, with the exception of those which
had suspended publication, had to submit to censorship
by the Newspaper Censorship Office established by the
Japanese authorities. With a view to extending the
sphere of its censorship, the Japanese Newspaper Censorship
Office yesterday notified all the local Chinese news
agencies to submit for censorship all news sheets before
they are sent out to local newspapers.
It is also learned that the Japanese newspaper
censorship authorities yesterday requested the local
foreign news agencies to submit two copies of their proof
sheets every day for censorship by the Japanese before
they are released for publication in local newspapers.
This request was also made at yesterday's press conference
with foreign journalists. In view of the fact that
the foreign news agencies, such as Reuter's, the United
Press, the Havas, etc., enjoy extraterritoriality, it is
not likely that they will comply with the request of the
Japanese authorities.

《标准报》及其他当地报纸：1938年5月12日（上午）*注：原文日期疑似OCR错误，结合上下文应为3月*

日本人将审查外国通讯社的报道

随着中国军队从上海和吴淞撤退，除停刊者外，所有在上海出版的华人_owned_报纸都必须服从日本当局设立的新闻检查所的审查。为了扩大其审查范围，日本新闻检查所于昨日通知所有当地中文通讯社，在将新闻稿发往当地报纸之前，必须送交审查。
另悉，日本新闻审查当局于昨日要求当地外国通讯社每天提交两份清样副本，在当地报纸刊登发布之前由日本人进行审查。在昨天与外国记者举行的新闻发布会上也提出了这一要求。鉴于路透社、合众社、哈瓦斯社等外国通讯社享有治外法权，它们不太可能遵从日本当局的要求。

After the fall of Nanking it was revealed

A record of discussions held at the 18th
meeting of the C.E.C. Standing Committee was discovered
at General Chiang's residence in the Military Academy.
According to the record, the meeting was held in the
conference hall of the Central Tangpu in Nanking at 8 a.m.
August 6, 1935. It is recorded that a sum of $4,000
is to be paid to the "Peiping Chronicle" every month,
and a sum of $10,000 a month to Reuter's.

Sir:

Re: Foreign Registered Newspapers
in the Chinese Language.

I have the honour to acknowledge
receipt of your letter of February 2, 1938,
and in reply to draw your attention to the
fact that the Municipal Police cannot exer-
cise summary jurisdiction over the property
or business of foreign nationals whose respec-
tive Governments possess extraterritorial rights
in China. Action along the lines you desire
can only be taken against such persons in the
judicial tribunals of their respective Govern-
ments or by appealing to the good offices of
their respective Consular Authorities.

Under these circumstances I would
suggest that you approach the Authorities concerned,
pointing out to them the specific matters to which
you take exception, who will no doubt be glad to
give careful consideration to your representations.

A careful check is maintained on all pub-
lications in Chinese over which the Municipal
Police can exercise control.

February 2, 1938,
The Shanghai Press Censorship Office.

Major Gerrard,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Re - The Suppression of Foreign Registered
Chinese Language Newspapers in the
Settlement.

Sir,

It might well be said that the publication of
anti-Japanese articles by foreign registered Chinese
language newspapers in the Settlement is prevalent because
they enjoy neutrality and have the right to exercise
impartiality in publishing every kind of news, no matter
what consequences such publication may have. Actually,
these papers are publishing anti-Japanese articles out of
ill-will and it is not a case of merely publishing any news
that comes to their knowledge. In some cases, they publish
anti-Japanese articles in order to increase circulation,
but whatever their motive may be, the publication of
anti-Japanese articles tends to encourage and stimulate
anti-Japanese feeling among the Chinese population of the
Settlement.

A close examination and analysis of the papers
in question will disclose that they harbour strong anti-
Japanese sentiments, and we fear that any leniency on
the part of the Settlement authorities in dealing with such
papers may be due to the fact that the authorities have
failed to detect the anti-Japanese feeling harboured by
the papers.

1938年2月2日，
致上海新闻检查处。

Gerrard少校，
警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局。

事由 - 取缔租界内外文注册之中文报纸。

先生，

可以说，租界内外文注册之中文报纸刊登反日文章之风盛行，是因为它们享有中立地位，并有权 impartially（公正地）发布各类新闻，无论此类发布可能产生何种后果。实际上，这些报纸是出于恶意刊登反日文章，而并非仅仅发布其所知悉的任何新闻。在某些情况下，它们刊登反日文章是为了增加发行量，但无论其动机如何，刊登反日文章往往会鼓励和刺激租界内华人的反日情绪。

对上述报纸进行仔细审查和分析后就会发现，它们怀有强烈的反日情绪，我们担心，租界当局在处理此类报纸时若有任何宽纵，可能是因为当局未能察觉这些报纸所隐藏的反日情绪。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

From our point of view, the attitude of the
Settlement authorities over such papers is quite strong.
We appreciate the fact that the Settlement
authorities have been sparing no efforts to restore peace
and order in the Settlement, and we think that the
Settlement authorities will recognize the fact that
we, the Press Censorship Office, are also doing our bit
in this respect through our work of censoring the
Chinese newspapers. The foreign registered Chinese
language newspapers, however, refuse to be censored by
us and deliberately publish anti-Japanese articles that
have been prohibited publication by purely Chinese papers
because they enjoy extraterritoriality. Their action
tends to stimulate anti-Japanese feeling among the
Chinese population of the International Settlement; it also
means that these foreign registered Chinese newspapers
have voluntarily abandoned their neutrality. If we
reflect what consequences the publication of anti-Japanese
articles may have on the peace and order of the
Settlement, we should not leave the matter neglected.
Whatever efforts you may make to effect the arrest of
the anti-Japanese terrorists, they will come to naught
if you do not take action against anti-Japanese papers.
We will not be far wrong if we say that the recent acts
of terrorism were partly due to encouragement and
stimulation from anti-Japanese articles published by
foreign registered Chinese language newspapers. We think
that the Police should take action against any paper
the existence of which detrimental to the peace and order
of the Settlement. We remember the case of the "China
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

从我们的角度来看，租界当局对这些报纸的态度相当强硬。
我们赞赏租界当局为恢复租界内的和平与秩序不遗余力，我们认为，租界当局会认识到，我们新闻检查处通过审查中文报纸的工作，也在此方面尽了一份力。然而，外文注册的中文报纸拒绝接受我们的审查，并故意刊登纯中文报纸已被禁止出版的反日文章，因为它们享有治外法权。它们的行径倾向于刺激国际租界内华人的反日情绪；这也意味着这些外文注册的中文报纸自愿放弃了其中立立场。如果我们反思刊登反日文章可能对租界的和平与秩序产生的后果，就不应忽视此事。无论你们为逮捕反日恐怖分子做出多大努力，如果不对反日报纸采取行动，这些努力都将付诸东流。如果说最近的恐怖主义行为部分是由于外文注册中文报纸刊登的反日文章的鼓励和刺激所致，这并不为过。我们认为，警方应对任何存在危害租界和平与秩序的报纸采取行动。我们记得《中国

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Forum," an American registered periodical, which was
suppressed by your authority. We think it is not
impossible to suppress the existing anti-Japanese
foreign registered Chinese language papers in a similar
manner.

We hereby request you to give consideration
to this matter and to take adequate steps against the
papers complained of.

Yours sincerely,

The Shanghai Press Censorship Office.

特此请求贵方考虑此事，并对被投诉的报纸采取适当措施。

page_data.en:
Responsibility

INQUIRIES are accumulating, both private and official, as to who owns the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, who owns its Chinese affiliate the Ta Mei Wan Pao, and what is the Ta Mei Wan Pao.
Unanswered questions in such times as these are unwholesome both for the community and for the newspapers concerned. The following statement seems necessary.
I am and have always been the controlling and responsible owner of both the Post Mercury Co. Federal Inc., U.S.A. and the Ta Mei Wan Pao. The Post Mercury Co. owns the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury. My associated shareholders are all American.
The Ta Mei Wan Pao is a Chinese language daily which until recently was my personal property and hobby. It has long been associated with the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, similar in editorial policy but separate as to editorial and executive control.
The rapidly growing circulation of the Ta Mei Wan Pao and the complexity of the problems now confronting Shanghai's Chinese community requires this Chinese newspaper to have the most experienced and responsible management and editing possible. From today, therefore, ownership, executive management and editorial control of the Evening Post and the Ta Mei Wan Pao are identical.
The Ta Mei Wan Pao is the Chinese edition of the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury.
Their combined circulation exceeds 80,000 copies daily.
The policies of the Evening Post and the Ta Mei are identical. Their substance is similar and in most particulars the same.
They collaborate with government authorities when they can do so with a clear conscience. They appreciate and strive to profit by constructive criticism and suggestions from all quarters.
They submit to censorship from nobody.
In general they follow the best American newspaper tradition of free speech, of fearless and hard hitting editorials, realistic and non-partisan, and of straight news presentation devoid of editorial bias.
Though American owned they appreciate and emphasize their responsibility to all of this international community, to serve which they possess a working personnel of many nationalities.
Today as never before, the times call for the type of newspaper thus evolved. I believe that Shanghai wants and needs honesty in editorial attitude and independent accuracy in news. These the Evening Post and the Ta Mei Wan Pao try to give.
Cornelius V. Starr.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 17 DEC 1937）
（批：S.S. / OBR 7/2   os. SB / OBR 7/2）
page_data.zh:
责任

关于谁拥有《上海晚邮报与信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury），谁拥有其中文附属报刊《大美晚报》，以及《大美晚报》究竟为何物，私人及官方的查询正日益增多。在此类时局下，此类未获解答的问题无论对社区还是对相关报纸而言均无裨益。因此，似乎有必要发表如下声明。
我过去是、现在依然是美国联邦注册的后邮报公司（Post Mercury Co. Federal Inc., U.S.A.）及《大美晚报》的控股及责任所有人。后邮报公司拥有《上海晚邮报与信使报》。我的关联股东均为美国人。
《大美晚报》是一份中文日报，直到最近仍是我的个人财产及业余爱好。它长期以来与《上海晚邮报与信使报》保持关联，编辑方针相似，但在编辑及行政管控方面相互独立。
鉴于《大美晚报》发行量迅速增长，以及目前上海华人社区所面临问题的复杂性，这份中文报纸需要尽可能由最具经验且负责任的人员进行管理和编辑。因此，从今天起，《晚邮报》与《大美晚报》的所有权、行政管理及编辑控制权归于一体。
《大美晚报》即《上海晚邮报与信使报》的中文版。
两报合计日发行量超过 80,000 份。
《晚邮报》与《大美报》的方针一致。其内容实质相似，且在大多数细节上相同。
它们在问心无愧的前提下与政府当局合作。它们感激并努力从各方的建设性批评与建议中获益。
它们不接受任何人的审查。
总体而言，它们遵循美国报纸的最佳传统，即言论自由、社论无畏且犀利、现实且不偏不倚，以及不带编辑偏见的直率新闻报道。
虽为美资所有，它们珍视并强调其对整个国际社区的责任，为此它们拥有一支由多国国籍人员组成的工作团队。
今时不同往日，时代呼唤由此演变而成的报纸类型。我相信上海渴望并需要在编辑态度上的诚实以及在新闻上的独立准确性。《晚邮报》与《大美晚报》正致力于提供这些。
科尼利厄斯·V·斯塔爾 (Cornelius V. Starr)。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1937年12月17日）

December 21, 1937. Morning Translation.

Lieh Pao (力報), a mosquito paper :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK'S ELDER SON APPOINTED
COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF OF OUTER MONGOLIAN FORCES

According to information secured by our reporter
from a reliable source, Chiang Ching-kuo (蒋经国), the
elder son of General Chiang Kai-shek, who had studied
abroad and later entered the "Au-s" University (奥断大学)
in Moscow to undergo a special military course, has been
appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Outer Mongolian Army.
These Mongolian forces are assisted by a number of
Russian military advisors and aviators and are equipped
with 500 tanks, 300 heavy field pieces, 1,000 Soviet
aeroplanes and numerous mechanized units. One hundred
of the aeroplanes have made flights to various parts of
China, such as Hankow, Canton and Loyang.
Chiang Ching-kuo is now watching the develop-
ments in the Sino-Japanese hostilities. He will move
his troops to the Great Wall where he will effect a
junction with the 8th Route Army under the command of
General Chu Teh. Before long the well-equipped Outer
Mongolian Army will appear on the Western Front.

Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition :-

50,000 CHINESE KILLED AFTER JAPANESE OCCUPATION OF NANKING

During the first four days after the occupation
of Nanking, about 50,000 Chinese including Chinese
civilians and unarmed soldiers were killed. Foreign
observers, however, do not believe this report can be
true.
Japanese soldiers entered the safety zone and
arrested all men of strong physique whom they suspect
to be Chinese soldiers. The men were then escorted to
an execution ground in batches of 300 and shot. Five
or six men were shot at one time with the others standing
by. Chinese policemen who had not withdrawn were also
killed.
A foreign reporter who passed through
Shingchungmeng (兴中门), Nanking, in a motor car
noticed heaps of corpses "as high as hills". According
to observers, the object of these executions is to
make Chinese respect and fear Japanese, but the reaction
has been the contrary for the executions have increased
the Chinese hatred of Japanese and have aroused a
desire for revenge.
Prior to the entry of Nanking by Japanese
soldiers, large numbers of Chinese soldiers remained
in the city. Some committed robbery. It is a matter
of regret that many fine buildings have been levelled.
After entering Nanking, the Japanese soldiers committed
extensive looting and all monies in Chinese and foreign
houses and in the homes of refugees in the safety zone
were carried away. Women were raped. The residence
of the American Ambassador was not robbed as two
foreigners were still there. The Japanese soldiers

《力报》，一家小型报纸：-

蒋介石将军长子被任命为外蒙古军队总司令

据本报记者从可靠消息来源获悉，蒋介石将军的长子蒋经国，曾留学海外，后进入莫斯科“奥断大学”(Au-s University) 修习特别军事课程，已被任命为外蒙古军队总司令。这支蒙古军队由数名俄国军事顾问和飞行员协助，装备有 500 辆坦克、300 门重型野战炮、1,000 架苏联飞机以及众多机械化部队。其中一百架飞机已飞往中国各地，如汉口、广州和洛阳。
蒋经国目前正在关注中日战事的发展。他将把部队调往长城，在那里与朱德将军指挥的八路军会师。不久，装备精良的外蒙古军队将出现在西线战场。

《大美晚报》晨版：-

日军占领南京后 50,000 名中国人遇害

在南京沦陷后的头四天里，约有 50,000 名中国人，包括中国平民和手无寸铁的士兵，被杀害。然而，外国观察家认为这一报道不可能是真的。
日本士兵进入安全区，逮捕了所有体格强壮、被怀疑是中国士兵的男子。这些人随后被分批每批 300 人押往刑场枪决。每次枪决五或六人，其他人则在旁等候。尚未撤离的中国警察也被杀害。
一名外国记者驾车经过南京兴中门 (Shingchungmeng) 时，注意到尸体堆积“如山”。据观察家称，这些处决的目的是为了让中国人尊重并畏惧日本人，但反应却恰恰相反，因为处决增加了中国人对日本人的仇恨，并激起了复仇的欲望。
在日本士兵进入南京之前，大量中国士兵留在城内。有些人实施了抢劫。令人遗憾的是，许多精美的建筑物被夷为平地。进入南京后，日本士兵进行了大规模的掠夺，中国和外国家庭以及安全区内难民家中的所有钱财均被掠走。妇女遭到强奸。美国大使的寓所未遭抢劫，因为当时仍有两名外国人在那里。日本士兵

After the Japanese soldiers had completed
their extensive looting, General Matsui, Commander-in-
Chief of the Japanese army, issued a notice instructing
Nanking residents to return immediately and to live
peacefully under Japanese control.

Ta Mei Wen Pao Morning Edition (Tokyo telegram) :-

SINKING OF BATTLESHIP MUTSU CONFIRMED

Admiral Nagano, Commander-in-Chief of the
Japanese Fleet, who was reported to have been lost in
the Yangtse River when the battleship Nagato was sunk,
received American and Japanese journalists on December
19 and made the following statement :- "It was not the
battleship Nagato that was sunk by the Chinese, but the
battleship Mutsu. The battleship Nagato has been in
Japanese waters since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities."
(Editor's notes The battleship Mutsu was one of the
largest Japanese warships; its fighting value was equal
to that of the battleship Nagato. Both battleships are
of 32,720 tons. The Mutsu was built during the European
War. At the Washington Conference, the United States
suggested the scrapping of the battleship. In 1934,
it was overhauled. She carried 10 16-inch guns. It
cost about Yen 200,000,000.)

Hwa Lei Wen Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

THE OPERATIONS NEAR HANGCHOW

According to information from Hangchow, the
Japanese forces delivered a furious attack on Tsingshan
Shih (青山市) on the night of December 18 under heavy
gunfire. The Chinese forces put up a very stiff resistance,
but were forced to retreat to their new lines near the
bus station and vicinity because of a flanking movement
by the Japanese against their rear.
On the morning of December 19, a fierce battle
took place at this latter place. At 4 p.m. the same day,
Chinese reinforcements arrived and delivered an unexpected
attack on Tsingshan Shih from Si Da Kiao (西大桥) and
surrounded the 800 Japanese. In the course of the fierce
fighting, more than 50 Japanese soldiers were killed,
while six big field pieces and a number of trench mortars
and other military weapons were seized. Consequently,
the Japanese withdrew and Tsingshan Shih was retaken by
the Chinese. The retreating Japanese are being surrounded
by the Chinese.

Ta Lei Wen Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

MANY JAPANESE TRANSPORTS GATHER OUTSIDE WOOSUNG

Yesterday some 80 Japanese transports were
noticed outside Woosung. They were carrying a large number
of soldiers to some unknown destination. On December 20,
the transport "Dairen" arrived in Shanghai.

1937年12月21日。晨间译稿。

被拒之门外，他们显得非常羞愧。
在日本士兵完成大规模掠夺后，日军总司令松井将军发布通告，指示南京居民立即返回，并在日本控制下和平生活。

《大美晚报》晨版（东京电报）：-

确认战列舰“陆奥”号沉没

日本舰队总司令长野海军上将，此前据报道在战列舰“长门”号沉没时于长江失踪，于 12 月 19 日接见了美国和日本记者，并发表如下声明：“被中国人击沉的不是战列舰‘长门’号，而是战列舰‘陆奥’号。自中日敌对行动爆发以来，战列舰‘长门’号一直停泊在日本水域。”
（编者注：战列舰“陆奥”号是日本最大的军舰之一；其作战价值相当于战列舰“长门”号。两艘战列舰均为 32,720 吨。“陆奥”号建于欧洲大战期间。在华盛顿会议上，美国建议将该战列舰报废。1934 年，该舰进行了大修。它装有 10 门 16 英寸火炮。造价约为 2 亿日元。）

《华雷文报》(Hwa Lei Wen Pao) 晨版及其他本地报纸：-

杭州附近的战斗

据来自杭州的消息，12 月 18 日晚，日军在猛烈炮火下对青山市 (Tsingshan Shih) 发动了猛烈攻击。中国军队进行了非常顽强的抵抗，但由于日军对其后方实施侧翼机动，被迫撤退至汽车站附近及其周边的新防线。
12 月 19 日上午，在该地发生了激烈的战斗。同日下午 4 时，中国援军抵达，并从西大桥 (Si Da Kiao) 对青山市发动了出其不意的攻击，包围了 800 名日军。在激烈的战斗中，50 多名日本士兵被击毙，缴获了 6 门大型野战炮以及若干迫击炮和其他军事武器。随后，日军撤退，青山市被中国军队收复。撤退的日军正被中国军队包围。

《大雷文报》(Ta Lei Wen Pao) 晨版及其他本地报纸：-

大量日本运输船聚集在吴淞口外

昨天，有人在吴淞口外发现约 80 艘日本运输船。它们正载着大量士兵前往某个未知的目的地。12 月 20 日，运输船“大连”号抵达上海。

page_data.en:
Japanese Censor
Offices Opening

Influential Takungpao
Ceases Publication
In Defiance

The Japanese controlled
"Shanghai Censorship Office" has
announced that censorship of
Chinese newspapers will begin to-
morrow at its offices in the Bar-
goon building on Nanking Road.
Upon being notified of the de-
cision, the Ta Kung-Pao, one of
the leading Chinese dailies, this
morning announced that it will
suspend publication tomorrow in-
stead of yielding to the Japanese
censorship.

Circulars were delivered at the
offices of various Chinese news-
papers yesterday demanding that
all of them submit two proofs of
all news items to the censorship
office for examination before pub-
lication as from tomorrow. While
the Ta Kung Pao decided to sus-
pend publication, the reaction of
the other Chinese newspapers
could not be ascertained this
morning, although rumors were
current that the Shun Pao, an-
other leading daily here, may fol-
low suit.

"Isolated Island"

The Ta Kung Pao, which will
continue to publish its Hankow
edition, has been outstanding
among the Chinese newspapers in
its continued allegiance to the
Chinese government and defiance
to the Japanese. Its editorials
have been describing Shanghai as
an "isolated island" and criticiz-
ing a certain section of Chinese
who frequent amusement resorts
as if no "struggle for life" was
going on in the interior. Last
week, the Ta Kung Pao authori-
ties made it clear that it would
not "cooperate" with the Jap-
anese by refusing to be repre-
sented at a tea party given by
a Japanese vice-consul in charge
of the censorship office.

During the tea reception, it was
revealed this morning, the Japan-
ese official discussed the censor-
ship and is alleged to have dis-
tributed among the represented
newspapers a copy of an adver-
tisement for insertion. The "ad"
turned out to be an official pro-
clamation of the formation of the
"Ta Tao Municipal Government."
The newspapers, however, reject-
ed the "business."

Never Submit

Bidding farewell to its readers
in its last edition today, the Ta
Kung Pao, in a stirring editorial,
reminded the Chinese people in
the "Isolated Island" surrounded
by Japanese troops never to "lose
the soul of a Chinese" and never
to submit to their "powerful
neighbor."

Simultaneously, the paper's
weekly supplement, Kuo Wen
Tsou Pao, or the "National News
Weekly," also announced discon-
tinuation.

The closure of the Ta Kung
Pao, Eastern Times, the Hwa Mei
Wan Pao and the American-
owned Ta Mei Wan Pao, affiliate
of the Shanghai Evening Post.

日本审查官
办事处开设

有影响力的《大公报》
以示抗议停止出版

受日本控制的“上海新闻检查处”宣布，将从明天起在其位于南京路巴公大楼 (Bargoon building) 的办事处开始对中文报纸进行审查。
得知这一决定后，主要中文日报之一的《大公报》今早宣布，它将于明天停刊，而不是屈服于日本的审查制度。

昨天，各种中文报纸的办事处都收到了传单，要求所有报纸从明天起在出版前将所有新闻项目的两份校样提交给审查办公室进行检查。虽然《大公报》决定停刊，但其他中文报纸的反应今早尚无法确定，尽管有谣言称这里的另一家主要日报《申报》可能会效仿。

“孤岛”

《大公报》将继续出版其汉口版，它在中文报纸中因其继续效忠中国政府并反抗日本而脱颖而出。其社论将上海描述为“孤岛”，并批评某些经常光顾娱乐场所的中国人，仿佛内地没有发生“生存斗争”一样。上周，《大公报》当局明确表示，通过拒绝派代表参加负责审查办公室的日本副领事举办的茶话会，它不会与日本人“合作”。

今早透露，在这次茶话招待会上，这位日本官员讨论了审查事宜，据称向出席的报纸分发了一份待刊登的广告副本。这份“广告”原来是成立“大道市政府”的官方公告。然而，各报纸拒绝了这笔“生意”。

绝不屈服

《大公报》在今日的最后一版中向读者告别，在一篇激动人心的社论中，提醒被日军包围的“孤岛”上的中国人民永远不要“失去中国人的灵魂”，永远不要向他们的“强邻”屈服。

同时，该报的周刊副刊《国闻周报》(Kuo Wen Tsou Pao) 也宣布停刊。

《大公报》、《时事新报》(Eastern Times)、《华美晚报》以及美资《上海晚邮报》附属刊物《大美晚报》的关闭。

Subject Opposition of leading Chinese newspapers to
Japanese interference
Made by C.A. Loh Sih-kya Forwarded by N.I.I. Logan

With reference to the attached cuttings
from local foreign newspapers relating to the Japanese
interference with the leading Chinese daily newspapers,
enquiries made by the undersigned show that upon receipt
of a circular notice issued by the Japanese authorities
announcing that they have assumed control of the Shanghai
Newspaper Censorship Office, the Chinese Daily Newspapers
Association held an urgent meeting on the evening of
November 29, at which it was resolved that the "Sin Wan
Pao," the "Shun Pao," the "Eastern Times" and the "Ta Kung
Pao", the only members of the Association, should cease
publication should the Japanese insist on censoring these
papers before publication. It was also resolved that the
Association detail a representative to pay a call on
Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C., on the
morning of November 30 to ask for the assistance of the
Council in this matter.

On November 30 these four newspapers received
another circular notice from the Shanghai Newspaper
Censorship Office announcing its removal from the Continental
Emporium Building to Room No. 218 of the Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road. The notice also requested the recipients to
send two copies of every issue of their respective papers
to its new office for purposes of censorship.

The managers of the four papers held a
meeting on the evening of November 30, at which the
interview with Mr. Fessenden was reported to those present.

page_data.en:
Ta Kei Wan Pao dated November 29 :-

THE CHINESE NEWSPAPER CENSORSHIP BUREAU

The Chinese Newspaper Censorship Bureau ceased
to function on November 23 after receiving a notice from
the Shanghai Municipal Council.
At 3 p.m. November 28, Japanese Consular
Police and gendarmes, accompanied by members of the
Shanghai Municipal Police called at the Bureau, Room 306
Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road. As there
was then only a coolie present in the office, the Japanese
officials, after asking him several questions, posted up
a notice bearing the inscription "The Shanghai Newspaper
Censorship Bureau" outside the office. Several of the
officers remained in the place until 7 p.m., at which
hour they left the premises, leaving a note to the coolie
stating that they would be back at 8 the next morning,
November 29.
It seems that the Japanese officials are
about to commence the censorship of newspapers.
page_data.zh:
11月29日《大基晚报》(Ta Kei Wan Pao) 报道：-

中国新闻检查局

中国新闻检查局在收到上海工部局的通知后，于11月23日停止运作。
11月28日下午3时，日本领事警察和宪兵，在上海公共租界工部局巡捕的陪同下，前往位于南京路大陆商场大楼306室的该局。由于当时办公室内只有一名苦力，日本官员在问了他几个问题后，在办公室外张贴了一张写有“上海新闻检查局”字样的告示。几名官员留在该处直至晚上7时，随后离开，并给苦力留下一张便条，称他们将于次日（11月29日）上午8时返回。
看来日本官员即将开始对报纸进行检查。

page_data.en:
28284

Chinese Papers
Oppose Nippon
Censor Demand

Four Leading S'hai
Dailies Wilt Suspend
If Necessary

AMERICAN-OWNED
SHEETS INVOLVED

Council Gets Request
To Urge Exemption
From Japanese

All Chinese-owned Chinese
newspapers in Shanghai, already
reduced to four leading ones since
the withdrawal of the Chinese
troops on November 12, would sus-
pend publication tomorrow if the
Japanese insisted on instituting a
censorship system.

This decision was understood to
have been reached in an emerg-
ency meeting of the Daily News-
paper Publishers' Association last
night following the receipt of
notifications from the Japanese
controlled Shanghai Censorship
Office that they must submit all
news items for censorship before
publication. The Japanese autho-
rities took over the censorship
office of the City Government of
Greater Shanghai Sunday and
began to function last night when
the notifications were sent around
the Chinese-owned newspapers.

Meetings Called

The Publishers' Association, of
which the two American-owned
evening newspapers are not mem-
bers, immediately convened the
emergency meeting and decided to
close their doors unless the Japan-
ese change their mind. A repre-
sentative was to call on Mr. Stir-
ling Fessenden, secretary-general
of the Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil, to submit a petition requesting
the Council to negotiate with the
Japanese for exemption of the
Chinese newspapers from censor-
ship. The outcome of the nego-
tiations, upon which the fate of
four leading Chinese dailies de-
pend, could not be ascertained this
morning.

The four newspapers directly
affected by the Japanese ruling
are the Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao,
Eastern Times and Ta Kung Pao.
The last named paper has a Han-
kow edition while the Shun Pao
is known to have been making
preparations to publish a paper in
that up-river city. A fifth news-
paper, the National Herald, would
not be affected by the Japanese
ruling as it has announced its
decision to suspend publication
from tomorrow. The Central
China Daily News, in which Mr.
Wang Ching-wei, chairman of the
Central Political Council, is report-
ed to be interested, suspended
Sunday.

Complications Seen

Diplomatic complications would
loom in the case of the two
American-owned evening news-
papers, the Ta Mei Wan Pao
(Great American Evening News-
paper) and the Hwa Men Wan
Pao (China-American Evening
Newspaper). Both of the papers
have not yet received notification
for censorship from the Japanese
censorship office, but asked to
send copies of their paper free.
The Hwa Mei Wan Pao is also
publishing a morning edition
while the Ta Men Wan Pao will
begin its morning edition tomor-
row.

As far as could be ascertained,
the Ta Mei Wan Pao stopped its
"cooperation" with the Chinese
censorship system some time be-
fore the withdrawal of the Chin-
ese troops from Shanghai.

28284

中文报纸
反对日本
检查要求

上海四大日报
必要时将停刊

涉及美资
报纸

工部局接到请求
敦促免除
日本检查

上海所有的中资中文报纸，自11月12日中国军队撤离后已减少至四家主要报纸，如果日本坚持实行检查制度，它们将于明天停刊。

据悉，这一决定是在昨晚日报出版商协会紧急会议上作出的，此前该协会收到了受日本控制的上海检查所的通知，要求所有新闻项目在出版前必须提交检查。日本当局于周日接管了大上海市政府的检查办公室，并于昨晚开始运作，当时通知已发送给各中资报纸。

召开会议

出版商协会（两家美资晚报并非其成员）立即召开紧急会议，并决定除非日本改变主意，否则将关闭报社。一名代表将拜访上海工部局总办斯特林·费森登 (Stirling Fessenden) 先生，提交请愿书，请求工部局与日本谈判，使中文报纸免除检查。今早尚无法确定谈判结果，而这关系到四家主要中文日报的命运。

直接受日本规定影响的四家报纸是《申报》、《新闻报》、《时事新报》和《大公报》。最后提到的这份报纸有汉口版，而据悉《申报》一直在准备在那座上游城市出版报纸。第五家报纸《国民日报》(National Herald) 不会受到日本规定的影响，因为它已宣布从明天起停刊。据报道，中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生感兴趣的《华中日报》(Central China Daily News) 已于周日停刊。

预见复杂情况

两家美资晚报，《大美晚报》(Ta Mei Wan Pao / Great American Evening Newspaper) 和《华美晚报》(Hwa Men Wan Pao / China-American Evening Newspaper)，将面临外交上的复杂局面。这两家报纸尚未收到日本检查所的检查通知，但被要求免费寄送报纸副本。《华美晚报》也在出版早报，而《大美晚报》将于明天开始出版早报。

据查，《大美晚报》在中国军队撤离上海之前的一段时间，已停止与中文检查系统的“合作”。

4 Chinese Dailies To Close If
Japanese Insist On Censorship

The four remaining Chinese-
owned Chinese newspapers in
Shanghai would suspend publication
if the Japanese authorities here
insist on instituting a censorship.
It was revealed yesterday following
an emergency meeting Monday
evening of the Shanghai Daily
Newspaper Publishers' Association.
Up to last night, no request has
been made to the editors to submit
their papers to censorship, although
all of them have been asked by
the Japanese Censorship Bureau to
deliver copies of their journals to
that office.
The four papers which are mem-
bers of the Publishers' Association
are the Ta Kung Pao, the Shun
Pao, the Sin Wan Pao and the
Eastern Times. The National
Herald (Sheng Chou Jih Pao),
which was one of the five leading
dailies that received the Shanghai
Municipal Council's "unofficial ad-
vice," will suspend publication today.
The farewell edition of the journal
was published yesterday.

若日本坚持检查
四家中文日报将关闭

如果驻沪日本当局坚持实行检查，上海仅存的四家中资中文报纸将停刊。这是在上海日报出版商协会周一晚召开紧急会议后，于昨日披露的消息。
截至昨晚，虽日本检查局要求所有编辑向其办公室递交期刊副本，但并未要求编辑们将报纸提交检查。
出版商协会的四家成员报纸是《大公报》、《申报》、《新闻报》和《时事新报》。《国民日报》(Sheng Chou Jih Pao) 曾是收到上海工部局“非正式建议”的五家主要日报之一，将于今天停刊。该报的告别版于昨日出版。

当地日文日报《上海联合新闻》(Shanghai United News) 昨日预测，上海工部局在镇压国际租界内的反日活动时，最终将取缔市内所有中文报纸。
该日本报纸认为，只有注册为美资的《华美晚报》这一家中文日报将被允许在租界内出版。
该报在进一步报道本地报纸局势时指出，双语出版物《中国每日先驱报》(China Daily Herald) 已在不久前被租界当局关闭，而《舰队新闻》(Fleet News) 据称已收到工部局的停刊通知。

June 5, 1937.                                      Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

REGISTRATION OF NEWSPAPER OFFICES AND NEWS AGENCIES

    The local Tangou publishes the following
notification in the advertisement columns of the "Min
Pao" and other local newspapers:-

    "We are in receipt of the following despatch
from the Central Publicity Department of the Kuomintang:-

    'Many newspaper offices and news
agencies in various parts of China have sent their
news matter either to the Collection and Examination
Section or to the Registration Section of the
Journalistic Enterprise Control Office of this
Department for censorship; this has caused us much
unnecessary labour.    In an effort to
readjust the delivery of news matter for censorship,
all newspapers and reports of news agencies which
are to be submitted for censorship should hereafter
be sent to the Registration Section of the
Journalistic Enterprise Control Office alone.  We
hereby request you to instruct all newspaper offices
and news agencies to observe this order and act
upon it accordingly."

    "In view of the foregoing, we therefore
publish this notification for public information and hope
that newspaper offices and news agencies throughout this
city will observe this order and act upon it accordingly."

Public Opinion To Receive
Protection In China

Important Circular Order Is Issued By C.E.C. For
Promotion Of Mass Movements And Freedom
Of Speech; Chance For Expression

NANKING, May 15.—The Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang has issued an important circular order (No. 4848) regarding the promotion of mass movements and protection of the freedom of speech. The order is addressed to the various Provincial and Municipal Party headquarters and is as follows:

It is the traditional policy of this Party to promote the mass movement and protect legitimate public opinion, since the Revolutionary aim of this Party is to arouse the people and seek the freedom and equality of China in the family of nations.

All actions and opinions of the people in so far as they are within the bounds of law (the Party) should be only too eager to promote and protect. How can we suppress them?

In recent years, the national emergency has become daily more serious. Danger lurks on every hand. In order to suppress disturbances and consolidate the national foundation, this traditional policy is even more indispensable. Public opinion must be given ample opportunity of expression, and mass movements must be actively promoted, so that the will of the people throughout the country may be unified under the direction of this Party for the achievement of the difficult task of national regeneration, reconstruction and salvation.

Within Legal Bounds

As to the small minority of people who, through ignorance or prejudice, exceed the limits of law in their actions and utterances—in certain cases, even to the extent of plotting the overthrow of the Government under the pretext of patriotism, thereby endangering the Republic—their actions cannot but be restricted or restrained by law.

However, in order to enforce the above-mentioned policy, the masses must be actively trained; social education promoted; local autonomy instituted; and the co-operative movement promoted, so as to elevate the cultural level of the people, strengthen their organization, and assure them security in their livelihood. Each individual must be made a productive unit of society. Each must perform his duties efficiently, so that he may successfully serve the State. Only thus can public opinion harmonize with the policy of consolidating the people's strength and concentrating the national resources; and only thus can the policy of this Party to promote mass movements and protect legitimate public opinion be enforced.

Besides dispatching a communication to this effect to the National Government for transmission to its various subordinate organs, this Order is hereby issued to the various grades of local Party headquarters for transmission to their subordinate organs for strict observance.

(Signed). Chiang Chung-cheng (Chiang Kai-shek), Wang Chao-ming (Wang Ching-wei) Chu Cheng, Feng Yu-hsiang, Ting Wei-fen, Yeh Chu-tsang, Kung Hsiang-hsj (H. H. Kung) Tsou Lu, and Chen Li-fu members of the Standing Committee of the C.E.C.—Kuo Min.

中国将保护舆论

国民党中央执行委员会发布重要通令，以促进群众运动及言论自由；提供表达机会

南京，5月15日电。——国民党中央执行委员会已就促进群众运动及保护言论自由一事，发布一项重要通令（第4848号）。该通令发往各省市党部，内容如下：

本党之一贯政策，在于促进群众运动并保护正当之舆论，盖本党之革命宗旨，旨在唤醒民众，谋求中国在各国大家庭中之自由与平等。

凡人民之行动与意见，只要处于法律（及党纪）范围以内，本党自当竭力促进与保护，岂可加以压制？

近年来，国难日益严重，危机四伏。为平息骚乱、巩固国本，此项传统政策更属不可或缺。必须给予舆论充分的表达机会，并积极促进群众运动，以便在全国民众中统一意志，在本党指导下，完成民族复兴、重建与救亡这一艰巨任务。

在法律范围内

至于极少数人因无知或偏见，在行动与言论上超越法律界限——在某些情况下，甚至假借爱国之名策划推翻政府，从而危害民国——对其行为不得不依法加以限制或约束。

然而，为贯彻上述政策，必须积极训练民众；推广社会教育；实行地方自治；并推动合作运动，以提高人民文化水平，加强其组织性，并保障其生计安全。必须使每个人成为社会的一个生产单位。每个人均须有效履行其职责，以便成功服务于国家。唯有如此，舆论方能与巩固民力、集中全国资源的政策相协调；也唯有如此，本党促进群众运动及保护正当舆论的政策方能得以贯彻。

除就此事项致函国民政府，由其转达各下属机关外，现特将此令发给各级地方党部，由其转达下属机关，严加遵照执行。

（签名）。中央执行委员会常务委员会委员：蒋中正（蒋介石）、汪兆铭（汪精卫）、朱家骅、冯玉祥、丁惟芬、叶楚伧、孔祥熙（H. H. Kung）、邹鲁及陈立夫。——《国民新闻》

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, April 2, 1937

New Censor Enforces
Rules On Newspapers
Taking over the Central Censorship Bureau, the Central Publicity Department of the Central Kuomintang, headed by Mr. Shao Lih-tsz, a veteran newspaperman and until recently chairman of the Shensi provincial government, enforced a universal censorship system in Shanghai yesterday.
Threatening to withdraw the Central News services, which also supply Chinese translations of Reuters' and Havas messages from abroad, the department succeeded in making the Chinese language newspapers published by firms registered with foreign nations submit to censorship. The Chinese edition of a Japanese daily however is not affected.
Until yesterday, one American registered Chinese evening newspaper was published without any form of censorship while another had special arrangements under which the censorship bureau sent censors to their offices. Yesterday, galley proofs were sent to the bureau offices.

新新闻检查官执行
报纸管制条例
昨日，由资深报人、前陕西省政府主席邵力子先生领导的国民党中央宣传部接管中央新闻检查局后，在上海实施全面新闻检查制度。
该部以停止提供中央通讯社服务相威胁（该社亦提供路透社及哈瓦斯社海外消息的中文译稿），成功迫使在外商注册机构出版之中文报纸接受检查。然而，某家日文日报的中文版不受此影响。
直至昨日，一家在美商注册的中文晚报仍无需接受任何形式的检查，而另一家则另有特别安排，即由新闻检查局派遣检查员驻其报社办公。昨日，各报已将清样送至检查局办公室。
