Morning Translation

Shun Pae and other local newspapers:-

BOOKSELLERS' ASSOCIATION ISSUES NOTICE.

The Shanghai Booksellers' Association has
issued the following notice to all its members:-
"On March 16, the Social Bureau called a
meeting of managers of various book-stores, at which
Commissioner Pan of the Bureau stated that many books
dealing both in art and socialism and published by
various local book-stores had been found to contain
reactionary literature. As the manuscripts of these
books were not sent to the Central Censorship Board for
investigation before their publication, they were often
prohibited by official organs after printing, thus
causing serious loss to the bookstores concerned.
Hereafter, before the publication of any book, careful
investigation should be made by the managements, and if
anything suspicious is found, the manuscripts or drafts
should be sent to the Propaganda Department of the
Central Tangpu at Nanking for investigation. Mr. Pan
promised to request the Central Propaganda Department to
pay special attention to any drafts sent in by the book-
stores. This notice is hereby issued for the information
of the various bookstores."

Subject Censorship of Foreign-Registered Chinese Evening Papers.

Made by G.A. Loh Sih Kya. Forwarded by (签名)

There is no truth that the Chinese Newspaper
Censorship Bureau is unable to deal with those evening
newspapers which are under foreign protection. It will be
remembered that in 1935 when Mr. T.O. Thackrey, publisher of
the "Ta Mei Wan Pao" (大美晚報), refused to send the proofs
of articles to the Chinese Newspaper Censorship Bureau for
examination, the Shanghai City Government ordered the Postal
Censors to detain all copies of the paper in question until
the publisher complied with the instructions of the Bureau.
At present the "Ta Mei Wan Pao" is published by
Mr. C.V. Starr, an American citizen, but in reality the paper
is managed by Mr. Chang Ming Wei (張明煒), who is closely
connected with General Chiang Kai Shek and was once Principal
of the Ching Chi School (錦溪學校), which was established
by General Chiang at his native place at Chikow (溪口) in
Fenghua District. The paper is financially supported by
the Shanghai City Government. However, in accordance with
instructions from the Newspaper Censorship Board of the
National Government, the paper was detained for seven days i.e.
from January 3 to 9, 1937, for failing to comply with the order
of the Shanghai Newspaper Censorship Bureau to delete certain
reading matters which were regarded as objectionable.
The cause is due to the fact that the Shanghai
Newspaper Censorship Bureau has to submit to Nanking daily a
report containing the headings of all articles deleted by
the Bureau.
As regards the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" (華美晚報), it is
registered in the State of Delware by Mr. H.P. Mills, who has
been engaged by Mr. Chu Tao Dong (朱作同) as publisher

主题 对外商注册中文晚报的审查。

由 G.A. Loh Sih Kya 撰写。呈报人 (签名)

所谓中国新闻检查局无法处理那些受外国保护的晚报，这种说法并不属实。人们应当记得，1935年，《大美晚报》(Ta Mei Wan Pao) 出版人 T.O. Thackrey 先生拒绝将文章校样送交中国新闻检查局审查时，上海市政府命令邮政检查员扣留该报的所有刊物，直到出版人遵从该局指令为止。
目前，《大美晚报》由美国公民 C.V. Starr 先生出版，但实际上该报由张明煒 (Chang Ming Wei) 先生管理，他与蒋介石将军关系密切，并曾担任溪口锦溪学校 (Ching Chi School) 的校长，该校是蒋介石将军在其奉化县溪口 (Chikow) 老家创办的。该报在财政上得到上海市政府的支持。然而，根据国民政府新闻检查委员会的指令，该报因未遵行上海新闻检查局关于删除某些被视为不妥的阅读内容的命令，被扣留七天，即从1937年1月3日至9日。
其原因在于，上海新闻检查局必须每天向南京提交一份报告，其中包含该局删除的所有文章的标题。
至于《华美晚报》(Hwa Mei Wan Pao)，它由 H.P. Mills 先生在特拉华州 (Delware) 注册，Mills 先生受朱作同 (Chu Tao Dong) 先生聘请担任该报出版人

June 11, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao published the following editorial on June 10:-

HOW MAY RESTRICTIONS BE IMPOSED ON FOREIGN NEWS AGENCIES?

Hardly had the amalgamation of the Domei and Rengo News Agencies been effected by order of the Japanese Government when Domei published a sensational and false report that the two Kwangs had raised the standard of revolt against Nanking. The foreign newspapers of Shanghai did not fail to publish this false information so that a panic was created in financial circles. It was not until the following day that the trick of the Japanese news agency was understood. It is clear that this was an act of bad faith on the part of the Japanese, but this state of affairs is also due to the discrimination exercised by our government in the censorship of the Chinese and foreign newspapers. In fact, there is no need to hide the fact that foreign newspapers are at liberty to create false rumours without running the slightest risk.

Since the enforcement of the censorship of the Press, people interested in the situation in our country have frequently found it impossible to learn the truth in regard to events taking place. To satisfy their desire, they are obliged to read the foreign newspapers towards which our government has adopted an attitude of laissez-faire. It is for this reason that the advertisements of a certain paper are always increasing.

Chinese readers are often misled by believing the sensational news published by the foreign press. They pay no heed to the source of the reports and the political inclinations of the agency issuing these reports. When these reports are published in a different form in Chinese newspapers, people will say that they have been censored. Therefore, we hope the government will restore to the Chinese newspapers their freedom.

Censorship of the Press is not an absolutely superfluous measure in abnormal times. The question which arises is: how restrictions may be imposed simultaneously on foreign and Chinese newspapers. It is regrettable to state that our government accords the foreign press certain facilities which are not enjoyed by the Chinese press. The telegrams dispatched by Japanese news agencies are never submitted for censorship by our government. The same happens in the case of Reuter, Havas etc. all of which enjoy so much freedom that our government cannot place the slightest control upon them. The foreign press is most audacious, especially the Japanese press which publishes tendentious reports without fear of being censored by our government.

Recently the Peiping correspondent of the "Manchester Guardian" wrote in a review called "Pacific Affairs" an article on the question of the censorship of the press, criticising the censorship system of our government. He, however, emphasized that the reports of the foreign news agencies in China, especially the Japanese, but also the Havas, Reuter's, Tass, are far from being without blemish.

Such criticism coming from a foreign newspaper correspondent reveals to us that censorship of the foreign press is indispensable. Consequently we hope the Government will, on the one hand, restore to the Chinese newspapers their freedom of publication, and on the other, place restrictions on the foreign newspapers and news agencies. This is the only means to remedy the present state of affairs.

1936年6月11日。下午译件。

《申报》于6月10日发表以下社论：-

如何对外国通讯社施加限制？

日本政府下令合并同盟社与联合社后不久，同盟社便发布了一则耸人听闻且虚假的报道，称两广举起了反叛南京的旗帜。上海的外国报纸无不刊登这一虚假信息，导致金融界陷入恐慌。直到第二天，日本通讯社的诡计才被识破。显然，这是日本方面的背信行为，但这种局面也归咎于我国政府在审查中外报纸时实行的歧视政策。事实上，无需隐瞒的是，外国报纸可以随意制造谣言，而无需承担丝毫风险。

自从实施新闻审查以来，关心我国局势的人们经常发现无法了解正在发生事件的真相。为了满足他们的求知欲，他们不得不阅读我国政府采取放任态度对待的外国报纸。这正是某家报纸广告收入不断增加的原因。

中国读者往往因相信外国媒体发布的耸人听闻的新闻而受到误导。他们不注意报道的来源以及发布这些报道的机构的政治倾向。当这些报道以不同形式出现在中文报纸上时，人们会说它们受到了审查。因此，我们希望政府恢复中文报纸的自由。

在非常时期，新闻审查并非绝对多余的举措。出现的问题是：如何同时对外国和中国报纸施加限制。令人遗憾的是，我国政府给予外国媒体某些中国媒体所没有享有的便利。日本通讯社发出的电报从未提交给我国政府审查。路透社、哈瓦斯社等也是如此，它们享有如此多的自由，以至于我国政府无法对它们施加丝毫控制。外国媒体最为大胆，尤其是日本媒体，它们在发布带有倾向性的报道时无需担心受到我国政府的审查。

最近，《曼彻斯特卫报》驻北平记者在一篇名为《太平洋事务》的评论中写了一篇关于新闻审查问题的文章，批评我国政府的审查制度。然而，他强调，在华外国通讯社，特别是日本通讯社，以及哈瓦斯社、路透社、塔斯社的报道，远非完美无缺。

来自外国报社记者的这种批评向我们表明，对外国媒体进行审查是必不可少的。因此，我们希望政府一方面恢复中文报纸的出版自由，另一方面对外国报纸和通讯社施加限制。这是纠正当前局势的唯一途径。

February 23, 1936.
Morning Translation,

Star Evening News (星夜報) published the following article
on February 21:-

TWO CHINESE POLICEMEN AND A BEGGAR WOMAN

One evening while passing Shantung Road, I
saw a crowd gathered in front of the Shantung Road
Cemetery. I approached and found two Chinese policemen
arresting an aged female beggar who was rolling herself
on the ground.
During the struggle, the woman cried out
for mercy: "Lords, release me. I will not beg again".
But each of the two Chinese policemen took
her by the hand and would not show her any mercy. The
woman was very strong and continued to roll herself on
the ground and refused to get up.
The two Chinese policemen used all their
strength in an effort to pull her up, but it only caused
the woman to roll the more. The struggle lasted about
five minutes.
A foreign policeman standing behind the crowd
told the Chinese policemen to let the woman go. Whether
he did this out of kindness or from some other motive,
it is not known. The two Chinese policemen smiled.
The beggar woman then crawled away after making a kotow
to each of the three officers.

《星夜报》于2月21日发表以下文章：-

两名中国警察与一名女乞丐

一天晚上，当我经过山东路时，
看见一群人聚集在山东路公墓前。我走近一看，发现两名中国警察
正在逮捕一名在地上打滚的老女乞丐。
在挣扎过程中，这名妇女哭喊求饶：“老爷们，放了我吧。我再也不乞讨了”。
但这两名中国警察各抓住她的一只手，
对她毫不留情。这名妇女力气很大，继续在地上打滚，
拒绝起身。
两名中国警察使出全身力气试图将她拉起，但这只导致
这名妇女翻滚得更厉害。这场争斗持续了大约
五分钟。
站在人群后面的一名外国警察告诉中国警察放开这名妇女。不知他是出于善意还是其他动机。两名中国警察笑了。
随后，这名女乞丐向这三名警官逐一磕头后爬走了。

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

MURDER IN CHAPEI

At 7.40 a.m. yesterday three persons entered
House No. 5, Zung Shing Li (仁兴里), Tsin Yuen Road,
Chapei, the residence of Loh Shih Kong (陸士康), owner
of the Kong Hwa (康華) Silk Weaving Factory, and fired
several shots at Loh Shih Kong, wounding him in the head
and the right waist and made good their escape.
Loh Shih Kong was rushed by his family to
the Paulun Hospital for treatment where he died at 3 p.m.

Chen Pao (official organ of General Chiang Kai Shek) publishes
the following editorials:-

THE SITUATION IN NORTH CHINA

Following the inauguration of the Hopei-
Charhar Political Council, a section of the people thought
that the critical situation in North China would improve,
and the East Charhar question be settled without more
difficulty. This view has been proved to be wrong. Up
to the present, no measures have been drawn up to solve
the East Charhar question and the position of traitor Yin
Ju Keng has become more firm. Furthermore, Yin recently
sent his Peace Preservation Corps to occupy Tangku and to
take over the various organizations there. According
to information received, there is a possibility that Yin
Ju Keng will be appointed by the Hopei-Charhar Political
Council as a senior administrative officer in the demilitarized
zone. If this report be true, a rebel will have been
promoted to a high position and this will encourage people
to rebel.

Japanese militarists have constructed
aerodromes in Peiping and Tientsin, increased the number of
their soldiers in these two cities, freely conducted
military movements inside the Great Wall, bribed traitors
and formed plain clothes groups, but the Hopei-Charhar
Political Council has paid no attention to these activities.
The situation in the North has now become
more grave. The calls paid by the Japanese militarists
on General Yen Shih San and General Han Fu Chu indicate an
intention on the part of the Japanese to induce Shantung
and Shansi to join the Hopei-Charhar Council so as to
complete their plan for the creation of an autonomy of
the five provinces in North China.

The National Government should realize that
the Hopei-Charhar Council has no power to negotiate external
affairs independently. The activities of Doihara and
other Japanese in the North should be carefully watched.

《晨报》（蒋介石将军的官方喉舌）刊登以下社论：

华北局势

继冀察政务委员会成立后，部分民众认为华北危急局势将会好转，东察哈尔问题也将不难解决。事实证明这种观点是错误的。截至目前，尚未制定解决东察哈尔问题的措施，而汉奸殷汝耕的地位反而更加稳固。此外，殷最近派遣其保安队占领塘沽，并接管当地各机构。据收到的消息，殷汝耕有可能被冀察政务委员会任命为非武装地带的高级行政官员。如果此报道属实，则意味着叛徒被提拔至高位，这将鼓励人们从事反叛活动。

目前北方局势已变得更加严峻。日本军国主义者拜访阎锡山将军和韩复榘将军，表明日本方面有意诱使山东和山西加入冀察政务委员会，以完成其建立华北五省自治的计划。

国民政府应认识到，冀察政务委员会无权独立交涉外交事务。应密切监视土肥原（Doihara）及其他日本人在北方的活动。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 28, 1935

Petition For Improvement
Of Press Censorship

Six Colleges And Universities Of Journalism
Submit Joint Plea To Nanking Government;
Alleged Discrimination

NANKING, Dec. 27. — That measures be adopted for the improvement or immediate abolition of the present system of press censorship, is urged by a colleges and universities of journalism in a joint petition to the Central authorities.

The schools include the Departments of Journalism of the Central Political Training Institute, Fuhtan University, Yenching University, University of Shanghai, the Peiping School of Journalism, and the Canton School of Journalism.

After referring to the resolution for the protection of legitimate public opinion, adopted by the recent 1st Plenary Session of the 5th Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, the petition says that the Government at last realizes the unwisdom of oppressing public opinion and the necessity of remedying the situation.

Undue Interference

Pointing out the abuse of the power of press censorship by certain local authorities, the petition states that the press is often unnecessarily interfered with by local officials, who often attempt to suppress news merely because they are not favourable to themselves personally.

Such unwarranted interference with legitimate public opinion can only be regarded as despotic, the petition observes.

In order that press censorship may become effective and intelligent, the petition suggests, it must be applied to Chinese and foreign journals alike; its control must be concentrated; and it must follow definite standards.

The petition deplores that, under the present system of press censorship, only the Chinese newspapers are censored, while the foreign press are exempt. Consequently, news which are prohibited in the Chinese press are published by the foreign press. Such discrimination against the Chinese press is incomprehensible, the petition adds.

Continuing, the petition points out that if control over the press is not concentrated, or if no definite standards of censorship are established and followed, not only will press censorship be ineffective, but it may also be abused by the local authorities.

Abolition Urged

If these recommendations cannot be adopted and enforced by the Government, the petition says in conclusion, the latter should immediately abolish the present system of press censorship, and order all cases of violation of the Press Law to be dealt with by the competent judicial authorities. Only thus can public opinion in this country be genuinely emancipated and national solidarity promoted.—Kuo Min.

《字林西报》，1935年12月28日，星期六

请求改进
新闻检查

六所新闻院校
向南京政府提交联合请愿；
指称存在歧视

南京，12月27日电。——各新闻院校在致中央当局的联合请愿书中，敦促采取措施改进或立即废除现行的新闻检查制度。

这些学校包括中央政治训练班新闻系、复旦大学、燕京大学、上海大学、北平新闻学院和广州新闻学院。

请愿书提及国民党第五届中央执行委员会第一次全体会议最近通过的关于保护正当舆论的决议，并称政府终于意识到压制舆论的不明智以及纠正局势的必要性。

不当干涉

请愿书指出某些地方当局滥用新闻检查权力，称媒体经常受到地方官员不必要的干涉，这些官员往往仅仅因为新闻对其个人不利就试图压制新闻。

请愿书指出，这种对正当舆论的无理干涉只能被视为专制。

请愿书建议，为了使新闻检查有效且明智，必须同等适用于中外刊物；其控制权必须集中；并且必须遵循明确的标准。

请愿书对现行新闻检查制度下仅检查中文报纸而外文报刊豁免的情况表示遗憾。因此，中文报纸被禁止刊登的新闻却由外文报刊发表。请愿书补充说，这种对华文报纸的歧视令人费解。

请愿书接着指出，如果对媒体的控制不集中，或者不建立并遵循明确的检查标准，不仅新闻检查将无效，还可能被地方当局滥用。

敦促废除

请愿书最后称，如果政府不能采纳并执行这些建议，则应立即废除现行的新闻检查制度，并命令所有违反《出版法》的案件由主管司法机关处理。只有这样，本国的舆论才能真正得到解放，并促进民族团结。——《国民新闻》

December 27, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

IMPROVEMENT IN PRESS CENSORSHIP DESIRED

On December 26, the Journalism Course Departments of the Central Political School, Futan University, the Yen Chin University and the University of Shanghai, the Peiping News College and the Canton News School sent the following joint petition to the National Government:-
"We understand that the 6th Plenary Congress passed a resolution that the National Government be requested to afford every protection to bona fide comments and to improve the Press censorship. This shows that the government leaders realize the impropriety of suppressing comments and speeches. If a country desires consolidation, the views of the people must be sought. The freedom of the Press is the only important way by which this can be attained.
"When Press censorship was first enforced, its object was to guard against propaganda by reactionary elements. The censorship was subsequently extended, and even bona fide news that was disliked by censors or by the district senior officers was also banned. Thus, the censorship has become tyrannical and newspapers are allowed to publish unimportant and uninteresting reports.
"The Press censorship should observe the following principles:-
1) Chinese and foreign newspapers throughout the country should all be subjected to censorship.
2) The system of censorship must be uniform.
3) Press censorship must have a certain fixed standard.
"Newspapers organized by foreigners in China are not subjected to censorship. People who do not read foreign newspapers will thus be unable to understand the actual situation in the country.
"In connection with the recent students movement in Peiping, Chinese newspapers were not permitted to publish reports regarding the movement, but foreign newspapers published what they liked. We are at a loss to understand why the treatment of Chinese and foreign newspapers is so different.
"If the government is unable to observe the abovementioned three principles, the system of Press censorship should be abolished immediately. Newspapers which publish improper matters should be dealt with by the Courts.
"We hope that the government will lose no time in adopting our views".

1935年12月27日。下午译文。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：

期望改进新闻检查

12月26日，中央政治学校、复旦大学、燕京大学和上海大学的新闻系课程部门，以及北平新闻学院和广州新闻学校，向国民政府提交了以下联合请愿书：
“据悉，第六届全会通过决议，请求国民政府充分保护真诚评论并改进新闻检查。这表明政府领导人意识到压制评论和言论的不当。如果一个国家希望巩固团结，必须倾听民众的观点。新闻自由是实现这一目标的重要途径。
“新闻检查最初实施时，其目的是防范反动分子的宣传。随后检查范围扩大，甚至审查员或地区高级官员不喜欢的真诚新闻也被禁止。因此，检查变得专横，报纸只被允许刊登不重要和无趣的报道。
“新闻检查应遵循以下原则：
1) 全国的中外报纸均应接受检查。
2) 检查制度必须统一。
3) 新闻检查必须有固定的标准。
“在华由外国人创办的报纸不受检查。因此，不读外文报纸的人将无法了解国家的实际情况。
“关于最近北平的学生运动，中文报纸不被允许刊登有关该运动的报道，但外文报纸则随意刊登。我们不解为何对待中外报纸如此不同。
“如果政府无法遵守上述三项原则，应立即废除新闻检查制度。刊登不当内容的报纸应由法院处理。
“我们希望政府尽快采纳我们的观点”。

Subject (in full) Chinese Journalists' Association - meeting.

Made by D. S. McKeown Forwarded by [Signature] 97

The Chinese Journalists' Association, with an office at
Room 630, the Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road, held
a general meeting of members at 6 p.m. December 22 in the Dah
Ya Lou (大雅樓) Restaurant, 580 Foochow Road. One hundred

were passed including the following :-

2) That an employment department for the benefit of unemployed
members be established.

Subject Censorship of Newspapers.

Made by C.A. Loh Sih Kya Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
Chen Ko Zung (陳克成), Chief of the Chinese Newspaper
Censorship Bureau, gives the following explanation:-
"The Government has no intention to abolish the
censorship of newspapers but in order to pacify certain
Kuomintang leaders who are strongly demanding the freedom
of the Press, the Government will adopt a more moderate
attitude. But my Bureau can do nothing to improve the
situation so long as the rules governing the censorship
of newspapers are in force.
"The Shanghai City Government recently made a
suggestion that the registration of mosquito papers be
undertaken by the Shanghai City Government in lieu of the
Ministry of Home Affairs and the Central Propaganda Department
of the Kuomintang at Nanking, and that in order to prevent
bad characters from publishing mosquito papers, every applicant
for registration be ordered to furnish $500 cash as security.
This suggestion has not yet been approved.
"Since the dissolution of the Magazines and Periodicals
Censorship Bureau in Shanghai by the Central Propaganda Depart-
ment on account of the "New Life" Weekly Magazine case, all the
magazines, periodicals, pictorials, etc., published in Shanghai
are not being censored at present."

Loh Sih Kya
Clerical Assistant

December 7, 1935. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

MOTOR HORNS REDUCE THE NUMBER OF ACCIDENTS.

The Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the International Settlement sent a letter to the S.M.C. yesterday stating that accidents will be bound to occur in congested areas if motor-car drivers do not make good use of their horns. It alleges that the S.M.C. has not actually considered the stipulations of Article 30 of the Traffic Regulations, revised this year, regarding the restrictions of the frequent use of motor-car horns, and states that an amendment to this Article is necessitated. The letter concludes by requesting the S.M.C. to immediately instruct the Traffic Office to conduct an investigation and then to make a change.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of General Chiang Kai Shek) published the following editorial on December 5:-

THE POLICY TOWARDS THE PRESS SHOULD BE AMENDED

The autonomous movement in North China was not started to-day, but the Chinese Press published reports of the movement only on November 25. The revolt of the traitor Ying Zu Keng was thus unexpected by a majority of Chinese readers. The Central Government has ordered the arrest of Ying but the complicated situation in North China renders this order ineffective.
Who then is responsible for this sorry state of affairs? Nothing more nor less than the present policy towards the Press.
For several years now, the condition of the country has been becoming more and more critical, but the Press is muzzled and has authority to publish optimistic reports only. Chinese readers are thus uninformed of what is taking place and are astonished when any grave incidents are exposed. If the general public had been informed of it, they would perhaps have made their views known earlier; traitors would not have dared to brave this opinion while those persons connected with the traitors would have reflected more carefully before acting; the position of the Government would have been more strengthened and incidents of this nature might have been averted.
The present policy towards the Press is solely responsible for the present situation. Was it not announced that Dr. Hu Shih was in favour of this autonomous movement? Dr. Hu has since declared that he will energetically oppose any movement tending to partition China. Did not the Japanese newspapers and news agencies announce that General Han Fu Chu was the soul of these seditious movements? The categorical denials issued by General Han have revealed the truth.
If the Press had not been muzzled by this erroneous policy, many of these traitorous movements might not have taken place.
Military and diplomatic affairs are generally regarded as things which should be carefully concealed,

《晨报》（蒋介石将军的官方机关报）于12月5日发表以下社论：

应修改对新闻界的政策

华北自治运动并非今日才开始，但中国新闻界直到11月25日才刊登有关该运动的报道。因此，大多数中国读者对汉奸殷汝耕（Ying Zu Keng）的叛乱感到意外。中央政府已下令逮捕殷，但华北复杂的局势使得这一命令无效。
那么，谁应对这种糟糕的局面负责呢？无非就是当前对新闻界的政策。
几年来，国家局势日益危急，但新闻界被钳制，仅有权发布乐观的报道。中国读者因此对正在发生的事情一无所知，当任何重大事件曝光时便感到震惊。如果公众早已知情，他们或许会更早表达观点；汉奸们就不敢无视这种舆论，而与汉奸有关联的人在行动前也会更加慎重考虑；政府的地位本可得到加强，此类事件或许本可避免。
当前的新闻政策对目前的局势负有全部责任。此前不是宣布胡适博士支持这一自治运动吗？胡博士此后声明，他将大力反对任何旨在分裂中国的运动。日本报纸和通讯社不是曾宣称韩复榘将军是这些煽动性运动的灵魂人物吗？韩将军发布的断然否认揭示了真相。
如果新闻界没有被这一错误政策所钳制，许多此类叛国运动或许根本不会发生。
军事和外交事务通常被视为应严加保密的事项，

但我们是否必须走到隐藏那些寻求损害国家利益的汉奸活动的地步？
秘密外交可能对强国有益，但对弱国的利益有害。我们不应让民众处于无知状态。
此外，不受这种荒谬审查约束的外国报纸，从未试图向读者隐瞒真相。由此得出的结论是，只有中国人民不了解事实以及在其土地上发生的事件。
这种审查导致人民对中国新闻界失去信心，因此人们不得不求助于外国报纸，以获取正在发生的重大事件的信息。
这种令人遗憾的局面使无耻之徒得以利用它谋取私利。至于那些对中国新闻界失去信心且无法阅读外文报纸的人，他们则满足于散布谣言。
为了国家利益，应迅速修改这种对新闻界的荒谬政策。
应允许报纸：
1) 刊登任何可能证明对国家及人民利益有害的事件的报道。
2) 让民众了解所有外交谈判的情况。
3) 揭露不诚实和腐败官员犯下的罪行和过错。
如此，新闻界方可重获公众信任，国家亦可免于危险。

November 30, 1935. Morning Translation.

China Evening News (comment):

GOVERNMENT SHOULD ALTER NEWSPAPER POLICY

The "Central Daily News" at Nanking published a comment in its paper on November 28, pointing out the mistakes of the newspaper policy of the National Government. It states:- "The situation of China is so grave to-day that the National Government should, without delay, alter its newspaper policy. The Kuomintang organ or the superior newspaper organ of the Government should consult with newspapermen about a set of simple measures regarding the censorship of newspapers. While laying down certain restrictions on the publication of news by newspapers, they should allow Chinese newspapers to publish news regarding any plot or any person that is liable to endanger China, news regarding facts or actions bearing on the political administration of China and news concerning patriotic movements of the people, and they should also be allowed to reproduce comments or any article of fact published in foreign newspapers".

Since the enforcement of the newspaper censorship policy by the Government, Chinese newspapers throughout the country have acted according to these regulations. What is the result? All news that Chinese newspapers are not allowed to publish appears in foreign newspapers as well as Chinese newspapers under the management of foreigners. Chinese newspapers by now are considered mere rubbish. Although Chinese readers know well of the difficulties of Chinese newspapers, yet they have to read foreign newspapers or Chinese newspapers under the management of foreigners in order to obtain fresh and reliable news. They think all news even rumours, guesses, and exaggerated reports, published in foreign newspapers or Chinese newspapers under foreign management, are reliable and trustworthy. For this reason, certain foreign newspapers which have particular motives wilfully publish rumours to deceive the public.

The present newspaper policy of the Government has caused a section of the Chinese people to refrain from reading Chinese newspapers. The people are becoming submissive and foreign aggression is becoming more evident. The Government newspaper policy can be, at least, partly held responsible. It is a very unwise policy.

The Government should alter its newspaper policy without delay as is suggested by the "Central Daily News".

《中国晚邮报》（评论）：

政府应改变报纸政策

南京《中央日报》于11月28日在该报发表评论，指出国民政府报纸政策的错误。文章指出：“中国目前的局势如此严峻，国民政府应立即改变其报纸政策。国民党机关报或政府的高级新闻机构应与新闻从业者协商，制定一套关于报纸审查的简单措施。在对报纸新闻发布施加一定限制的同时，应允许中国报纸刊登有关任何可能危及中国的阴谋或人物的新闻、有关涉及中国政治行政的事实或行动的新闻，以及有关人民爱国运动的新闻；还应允许转载外国报纸发表的评论或任何事实性文章”。

自从政府实施报纸审查政策以来，全国各地的中国报纸均依照这些规定行事。结果如何？所有中国报纸不被允许刊登的新闻，都出现在外国报纸以及由外国人管理的中文报纸上。中国报纸如今被视为纯粹的垃圾。虽然中国读者深知中国报纸的困难，但他们为了获得新鲜可靠的新闻，不得不阅读外国报纸或由外国人管理的中文报纸。他们认为，刊登在外国报纸或由外国人管理的中文报纸上的所有新闻，甚至是谣言、猜测和夸张的报道，都是可靠和值得信赖的。因此，某些带有特定动机的外国报纸故意发布谣言以欺骗公众。

政府目前的报纸政策导致一部分中国人不再阅读中文报纸。民众变得顺从，外国侵略变得更加明显。政府的报纸政策至少应承担部分责任。这是一个非常不明智的政策。

正如《中央日报》所建议的那样，政府应立即改变其报纸政策。

the demilitarized zone. Although the National Government has ordered the dismissal and the arrest of this traitor immediately after learning of the news of his revolt, no effective measures have as yet been adopted. This affair is at present receiving great concern from the public, many of whom have even despatched telegrams urging the Government to take immediately measures to quell this movement. There are, however, large numbers of Chinese people who are still ignorant of the seriousness of this development and who are taking a very cool and indifferent view towards it. It is indeed a deep regret that our national spirit has sunkun to . such a depth at the present time of national crisis.

As our newspapers are the chief means of conveying news to the public, they ought to prove a beneficial institution for assisting pro-Government and patriotic propaganda. This constitutes the principal reason why the various nations of the world are all adopting the policy of centralizing the control of newspapers. Although such a system also prevails in this country, it is, however, carried out in a totally different manner from that followed in other countries.

In this country newspapers are not allowed to disclose important Government and political news. There is , therefore, no doubt that the weakness of our national spirit is principally due to the adoption of this "dumb" newspaper policy.

Our nation is at present facing a great crisis. The trouble in North China will gradually spread and the troops of our enemies are daily concentrating around Tientsin and Peiping. They have taken control of the Peiping-Tientsin Line and have occupied our railway stations. Under such conditions, ought we (the pressmen) to still remain in silence and not endeavour to stimulate the patriotic feeling of our nation, thereby assisting the activities of our enemies?

非军事区。虽然国民政府在获悉其叛变消息后立即下令将其免职并逮捕，但迄今尚未采取有效措施。此事目前引起公众极大关注，许多人甚至发电报敦促政府立即采取措施平息这一运动。然而，仍有大量中国人对这一事态的严重性一无所知，并采取非常冷淡和漠不关心的态度。在国家危机的当前时刻，我们的民族精神竟沉沦至如此地步，实为深憾。

由于我们的报纸是向公众传递新闻的主要手段，它们本应成为协助亲政府和爱国宣传的有益机构。这就是世界各国均采取集中控制报纸政策的主要原因。虽然这种制度在本国也盛行，但其执行方式与其他国家完全不同。

在本国，报纸不被允许披露重要的政府和政治新闻。因此，毫无疑问，我们民族精神的软弱主要是由于采取了这种“哑巴”报纸政策。

我国目前正面临巨大危机。华北的麻烦将逐渐蔓延，敌军的部队每天都在天津和北平周围集结。他们已控制了北宁线（平津线），并占领了我们的火车站。在这种情况下，我们（新闻界人士）难道还应保持沉默，不努力激发我国的爱国情感，从而助长敌人的活动吗？

November 29, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) of November 28 publishes the following comment :-

THE COMMENT OF THE "CENTRAL CHINA DAILY NEWS" ON PRESS CENSORSHIP AGREED.

The "Central China Daily News" at Nanking has published a comment regarding the new policy, presenting many good views to the Authorities. What is said in the comment is very precise and sincere. We can say that every word in the comment represents the opinion of the press circles throughout the country. The utterance of this opinion is made for the good of the general situation of the country and the newspaper enterprises themselves as well.

The important points in the comment stress "The Government organs which supervise the publication of newspapers should consult with the newspaper concerns on a simple measure governing news; besides fixing a few explicit restrictions, all reports of facts should be allowed to be printed in Chinese press.... It is believed that three months hence, civil administrations and diplomatic developments will reach a new status." We are of the opinion that, if our wise Authorities, especially the officials of the press censorship organs of the Government, are willing to consider this sincere proposal broad mindedly, they will have to accept the opinion in good part.

During the present time and grave situation, the Government should naturally direct, control, and sometimes restrict the publication of certain news; but the so-called "direction", "control" and "restriction" should not be unreasonable. That is to say, for the benefit of the country, all measures for the control and restriction of news publication should be clear and simple. Suppose the censorship rules are too complicated and confused, those in the capacity of pressmen will find it hard to comply with them. Thus, speaking on the principle of new policy, the rules will cause more confusion in the newspaper system.

Take the present facts for instance, all diplomatic and military news are to be kept confidential. Newspaper reporters should have some common knowledge and understanding or at least they should have a thought for the nation. When they see things which should not be reported or published, they should not publish them imprudently even if the Government has not placed a restriction on such news. As to what is mentioned in the comment of the "Central China Daily News", all acts which tend to endanger the country or are destructive to rules and principles, if confirmed, should be disclosed to the public as early as possible so that the Government and the people may know to take precautionary measures. Speaking positively, patriotic movements of the people and the foreign opinion or criticisms should be allowed to appear in the newspapers as much as possible in order to encourage our people. By so doing, the newspaper concerns can then find an effective means to serve their country, and the latter will obtain assistance and cooperation from newspapers. If severe restrictions are further continued and all the facts are not allowed to be reported in either a positive or negative way, then what is to be reported in the newspapers? As newspapers have lost their real value, the Government authorities will also lose their opportunity to co-operate with the press.

11月28日出版的《辛晚报》（晚刊）发表如下评论：

赞同《华中日报》关于新闻审查的评论。

南京《华中日报》就新政策发表评论，向当局提出了许多良好见解。该评论言辞精准且诚恳。可以说，评论中的每一句话都代表了全国新闻界的意见。发表这一意见既是为了国家大局的利益，也是为了报业自身的利益。

评论的重点强调：“监管报纸出版的政府机关应与报馆协商，制定简单的新闻管理办法；除了规定几项明确的限制外，应允许中文报刊刊登所有事实报道……相信三个月后，内政和外交局势将达到一个新的状态。”我们认为，如果我们明智的当局，特别是政府新闻审查机构的官员，能够以宽广的胸怀考虑这一真诚的建议，他们就应当欣然接受这一意见。

在当前严峻的形势下，政府自然应当指导、控制，有时限制某些新闻的发布；但所谓的“指导”、“控制”和“限制”不应不合理。也就是说，为了国家利益，所有控制和限制新闻发布的措施都应清晰简单。假如审查规则过于复杂和混乱，身为新闻工作者的人将难以遵守。因此，从新政策的原则来看，这些规则将在报纸体系中造成更多的混乱。

以当前事实为例，所有外交和军事新闻均需保密。报纸记者应具备一定的常识和理解力，或者至少应有为国着想之心。当他们看到不应报道或发布的事情时，即使政府未对此类新闻加以限制，也不应轻率发布。至于《华中日报》评论中提到的内容，所有危害国家或破坏规章原则的行为，一经证实，应尽早向公众披露，以便政府和人民知道采取预防措施。从积极方面来说，应允许人民的爱国运动和外国舆论或批评尽可能多地见诸报端，以激励我国人民。通过这样做，报馆才能找到服务国家的有效途径，而国家也将获得报纸的协助与合作。如果继续实行严厉的限制，不允许以任何正面或负面的方式报道事实，那么报纸还能报道什么呢？既然报纸失去了其真正价值，政府当局也将失去与新闻界合作的机会。

SHANGHAI BUREAU OF EDUCATION TO CENSOR ILLUSTRATED
LITERATURE TO BE PUBLISHED BY LOCAL BOOKSTORES

Since the Pictures, Books and Magazines
Censorship Committee of the Central Propaganda Depart-
ment (in Shanghai) ceased its operations, no one is
responsible for the censorship of illustrated literature
and as a result local bookstores have again started
to publish literature dealing with spiritualism as well
as suggestive and immoral pictures.

The Shanghai Bureau of Education has
therefore, decided to undertake the censoring of such
literature and pictures, in conjunction with the
Bureau of Social Affairs and the Bureau of Public Safety ,
prior to the re-establishment of the Central Censorship

procedure, while the various local bookstores have been
instructed to observe this rule.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 29, 1935

Censorship
System Has
Evil Effects

Government Being Urged
To Co-operate With
National Press

SHARP EDITORIAL IN
CHINESE PAPER

“How Can Deaf And Dumb
Nation Organize State And
Exist On Earth?”

NANKING, Nov. 28.—The recent developments in North China have brought about a significant change in the attitude of the Chinese press, which is every day showing signs of defiance of the rigid censorship now in force. The Chinese newspapers are accustomed to publish only such news as is permitted by the Government’s Bureau of Censors, and violation of its regulations has hitherto brought severe disciplinary measures.

In the past few days, however, all the Chinese newspapers here have been openly criticizing the Government’s press censorship policy which, they state, has placed the Chinese people completely in the dark concerning vital developments in their country’s affairs.

Public ignorance at such a critical time is, in their opinion, “most dangerous,” and they are agitating for a change in the Government’s policy in the matter.

“Irrational” System

The “Central China Daily News,” which rarely prints editorials, to-day devotes half a page to an editorial on the question of censorship, urging that the present “irrational” system of news censoring be greatly relaxed. The journal begins by deploring the lack of public interest in State affairs despite the present extremely critical developments in North China, and explains that this is due to the fact that the authorities have hitherto chosen to withhold from the public news of important diplomatic developments.

Continuing, the journal says: “Such an irrational system of censorship is completely demoralizing, and if continued, the Chinese will become a nation of deaf and dumb people. How can a deaf and dumb nation organize a State and exist on earth?”

The journal urges the authorities to co-operate with the press and formulate simple regulations covering news which may be printed and that which may not. It advocates that, apart from a few explicit restrictions, all news concerning diplomatic developments, intrigues against the State, personalities involved in foreign comments, trustworthy news carried by foreign agencies, and reports on economic actions on the part of the people should be allowed to appear freely in the Chinese newspapers.—Reuter.

《字林西报》，1935年11月29日，星期五

审查制度
产生
恶劣影响

政府被敦促
与全国新闻界
合作

中文报纸发表
尖锐社论

“聋哑之民族如何组织国家并立于地球之上？”

南京，11月28日电。——华北近期的事态发展使中国新闻界的态度发生了显著变化，每天都显示出对目前实施的严格审查制度的蔑视迹象。中国报纸习惯于只刊登政府新闻检查局允许的新闻，违反其规定迄今会招致严厉的纪律处分。

然而，在过去几天里，这里的所有中国报纸都公开批评政府的新闻审查政策，称该政策使中国民众对国家事务的重要发展完全处于无知状态。

他们认为，在如此关键的时刻让公众处于无知状态是“最危险的”，他们正在鼓动改变政府在此事上的政策。

“非理性”的制度

很少刊登社论的《中央日报》今天用半个版面刊登了一篇关于审查问题的社论，敦促大幅放宽目前这种“非理性”的新闻审查制度。该报开篇对尽管华北局势极度危急但公众对国家事务缺乏兴趣表示惋惜，并解释说，这是由于当局迄今为止选择向公众隐瞒重要外交发展的消息所致。

该报接着说：“这种非理性的审查制度完全使人意志消沉，如果继续下去，中国人将成为一个聋哑的民族。一个聋哑的民族如何组织国家并立于地球之上？”

该报敦促当局与新闻界合作，制定简单的规章，规定哪些新闻可以刊登，哪些不可以。它主张，除了少数明确的限制外，所有有关外交发展、危害国家的阴谋、涉及外国评论的人物、外国通讯社发布的可靠新闻以及民众经济行动的报道，都应允许在中国报纸上自由刊登。——路透社。

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of General Chiang Kai Shek) published the following editorial on December 5:-

THE POLICY TOWARDS THE PRESS SHOULD BE AMENDED

The autonomous movement in North China was not started to-day, but the Chinese Press published reports of the movement only on November 25. The revolt of the traitor Ying Zu Keng was thus unexpected by a majority of Chinese readers. The Central Government has ordered the arrest of Ying but the complicated situation in North China renders this order ineffective.
Who then is responsible for this sorry state of affairs? Nothing more nor less than the present policy towards the Press.
For several years now, the condition of the country has been becoming more and more critical, but the Press is muzzled and has authority to publish optimistic reports only. Chinese readers are thus uninformed of what is taking place and are astonished when any grave incidents are exposed. If the general public had been informed of it, they would perhaps have made their views known earlier; traitors would not have dared to brave this opinion while those persons connected with the traitors would have reflected more carefully before acting; the position of the Government would have been more strengthened and incidents of this nature might have been averted.
The present policy towards the Press is solely responsible for the present situation. Was it not announced that Dr. Hu Shih was in favour of this autonomous movement? Dr. Hu has since declared that he will energetically oppose any movement tending to partition China. Did not the Japanese newspapers and news agencies announce that General Han Fu Chu was the soul of these seditious movements? The categorical denials issued by General Han have revealed the truth.
If the Press had not been muzzled by this erroneous policy, many of these traitorous movements might not have taken place.

《晨报》（上海《晨报》，蒋介石将军的官方喉舌）于12月5日发表了以下社论：

应修改对新闻界的政策

华北的自治运动并非今日才开始，但中国新闻界直到11月25日才刊登有关该运动的报道。因此，大多数中国读者对汉奸殷汝耕（Ying Zu Keng，音译）的叛乱感到意外。中央政府已下令逮捕殷，但华北复杂的局势使这一命令无效。
那么，谁应对这种可悲的局面负责呢？无非就是目前的对新闻界政策。
几年来，国家局势日益危急，但新闻界被封住嘴巴，仅有权刊登乐观的报道。中国读者因此对正在发生的事情一无所知，当任何重大事件被揭露时便感到震惊。如果公众早已知情，他们或许会更早表达观点；汉奸就不敢无视这种舆论，而与汉奸有关联的人在行动前也会更慎重地思考；政府的地位会更加稳固，此类事件或许可以避免。
目前的对新闻界政策应对当前局势负全部责任。此前不是宣布胡适博士支持这一自治运动吗？胡博士随后声明，他将大力反对任何旨在分裂中国的运动。日本报纸和新闻机构不是曾宣布韩复榘将军是这些煽动性运动的灵魂人物吗？韩将军发出的断然否认揭示了真相。
如果新闻界没有被这一错误政策封住嘴巴，许多此类叛国运动可能不会发生。
军事和外交事务通常被视为应仔细保密的事项，

Secret diplomacy may be good for a strong nation, but

In the interests of the country, this ridiculous

Newspapers should be allowed:

秘密外交可能对强国有益，但

让民众处于无知状态。
此外，不受这种荒谬审查约束的外国报纸，
从不试图向读者隐瞒真相。由此得出的结论是，
只有中国人民不了解事实以及在其国土上
发生的事件。
这种审查导致人民对中国新闻界失去
信心，因此人们不得不求助于外国报纸以获取
正在发生的重要事件的信息。

为了国家利益，这种对新闻界的荒谬

应允许报纸：
1) 刊登任何可能证明对国家

2) 让民众了解所有外交

3) 揭露不诚实和腐败官员所犯的

只有这样，新闻界才能重新赢得公众的

November 29, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) of November 28 publishes the following comment :-

THE COMMENT OF THE "CENTRAL CHINA DAILY NEWS" ON PRESS CENSORSHIP AGREED.

The "Central China Daily News" at Nanking has published a comment regarding the new policy, presenting many good views to the Authorities. What is said in the comment is very precise and sincere. We can say that every word in the comment represents the opinion of the press circles throughout the country. The utterance of this opinion is made for the good of the general situation of the country and the newspaper enterprises themselves as well.

The important points in the comment stress "The Government organs which supervise the publication of newspapers should consult with the newspaper concerns on a simple measure governing news; besides fixing a few explicit restrictions, all reports of facts should be allowed to be printed in Chinese press.... It is believed that three months hence, civil administrations and diplomatic developments will reach a new status." We are of the opinion that, if our wise Authorities, especially the officials of the press censorship organs of the Government, are willing to consider this sincere proposal broad mindedly, they will have to accept the opinion in good part.

During the present time and grave situation, the Government should naturally direct, control, and sometimes restrict the publication of certain news; but the so-called "direction", "control" and "restriction" should not be unreasonable. That is to say, for the benefit of the country, all measures for the control and restriction of news publication should be clear and simple. Suppose the censorship rules are too complicated and confused, those in the capacity of pressmen will find it hard to comply with them. Thus, speaking on the principle of new policy, the rules will cause more confusion in the newspaper system.

Take the present facts for instance, all diplomatic and military news are to be kept confidential. Newspaper reporters should have some common knowledge and understanding or at least they should have a thought for the nation. When they see things which should not be reported or published, they should not publish them imprudently even if the Government has not placed a restriction on such news. As to what is mentioned in the comment of the "Central China Daily News", all acts which tend to endanger the country or are destructive to rules and principles, if confirmed, should be disclosed to the public as early as possible so that the Government and the people may know to take precautionary measures. Speaking positively, patriotic movements of the people and the foreign opinion or criticisms should be allowed to appear in the newspapers as much as possible in order to encourage our people. By so doing, the newspaper concerns can then find an effective means to serve their country, and the latter will obtain assistance and cooperation from newspapers. If severe restrictions are further continued and all the facts are not allowed to be reported in either a positive or negative way, then what is to be reported in the newspapers? As newspapers have lost their real value, the Government authorities will also lose their opportunity to co-operate with the press.

1935年11月29日。下午译文。

11月28日的《新闻报》（晚刊）刊登了以下评论：

赞同《中央日报》对新闻审查的评论。

南京《中央日报》就新政策发表了一篇评论，向当局提出了许多良好的观点。评论中的言论非常精辟和真诚。可以说，评论中的每一句话都代表了全国新闻界的意见。发表这一意见既是为了国家大局的利益，也是为了报业自身的利益。

评论的重点强调：“监管报纸出版的政府机关应与报业公司协商，制定管理新闻的简单措施；除了规定少数明确的限制外，应允许所有事实报道在中国报刊上刊登……相信三个月后，民政管理和外交发展将达到一个新的阶段。”我们认为，如果我们明智的当局，特别是政府新闻审查机构的官员，愿意以宽广的胸怀考虑这一真诚的建议，他们就应当欣然接受这一意见。

在当前严峻的局势下，政府自然应该指导、控制，有时限制某些新闻的出版；但所谓的“指导”、“控制”和“限制”不应是不合理的。也就是说，为了国家的利益，所有控制和限制新闻出版的措施都应清晰简单。假如审查规则过于复杂和混乱，身为新闻工作者的人将发现很难遵守。因此，从新政策的原则来讲，这些规则将在报纸体系中造成更多的混乱。

以当前的事实为例，所有外交和军事新闻都要保密。新闻记者应具备一定的常识和理解力，或者至少应有为国着想之心。当他们看到不应报道或出版的事情时，即使政府未对此类新闻加以限制，也不应轻率地予以刊登。至于《中央日报》评论中提到的内容，所有危及国家或破坏规则原则的行为，一经证实，应尽早向公众披露，以便政府和人民知道采取预防措施。从积极方面来说，应尽可能允许人民的爱国运动和外国舆论或批评在报纸上出现，以激励我国人民。通过这样做，报业公司就能找到为国家服务的有效途径，而国家也将获得报纸的协助与合作。如果继续实行严厉的限制，不允许以任何正面或负面的方式报道所有事实，那么报纸还能报道什么呢？既然报纸失去了其真正价值，政府当局也将失去与新闻界合作的机会。

尽管如此，在中国报纸上不能刊登的新闻，在我们境内却可以在外国报刊上不受限制地自由报道。新闻的秘密无论如何都无法保持。此外，外商拥有的报纸经常刊登偏离事实的夸张报道，从而导致虚假新闻的传播。因此，允许中国报纸刊登此类新闻以纠正误解，从而大大减少当地的紧张情绪，同时遏制所有对我们不利的恶意宣传，将是权宜之计。这一建议基于我们的经验；我们特此将其奉献给我们的政府。

November 30, 1935. Morning Translation.

China Evening News (comment):

GOVERNMENT SHOULD ALTER NEWSPAPER POLICY

The "Central Daily News" at Nanking published a comment in its paper on November 28, pointing out the mistakes of the newspaper policy of the National Government. It states:- "The situation of China is so grave to-day that the National Government should, without delay, alter its newspaper policy. The Kuomintang organ or the superior newspaper organ of the Government should consult with newspapermen about a set of simple measures regarding the censorship of newspapers. While laying down certain restrictions on the publication of news by newspapers, they should allow Chinese newspapers to publish news regarding any plot or any person that is liable to endanger China, news regarding facts or actions bearing on the political administration of China and news concerning patriotic movements of the people, and they should also be allowed to reproduce comments or any article of fact published in foreign newspapers".

Since the enforcement of the newspaper censorship policy by the Government, Chinese newspapers throughout the country have acted according to these regulations. What is the result? All news that Chinese newspapers are not allowed to publish appears in foreign newspapers as well as Chinese newspapers under the management of foreigners. Chinese newspapers by now are considered mere rubbish. Although Chinese readers know well of the difficulties of Chinese newspapers, yet they have to read foreign newspapers or Chinese newspapers under the management of foreigners in order to obtain fresh and reliable news. They think all news even rumours, guesses, and exaggerated reports, published in foreign newspapers or Chinese newspapers under foreign management, are reliable and trustworthy. For this reason, certain foreign newspapers which have particular motives wilfully publish rumours to deceive the public.

The present newspaper policy of the Government has caused a section of the Chinese people to refrain from reading Chinese newspapers. The people are becoming submissive and foreign aggression is becoming more evident. The Government newspaper policy can be, at least, partly held responsible. It is a very unwise policy.

The Government should alter its newspaper policy without delay as is suggested by the "Central Daily News".

1935年11月30日。晨间译件。

《中国晚报》（评论）：

政府应改变新闻政策

南京《中央日报》于11月28日在该报发表一篇评论，指出国民政府新闻政策的错误。该文称：“今日中国局势如此严峻，国民政府应立即改变其新闻政策。国民党机关报或政府上级新闻机构应与新闻界人士商讨一套关于新闻审查的简单措施。在对报纸新闻报道施加一定限制的同时，应允许中国报纸刊登有关任何可能危害中国的阴谋或人物的消息，刊登与中国政治管理有关的事实或行动的消息，以及有关民众爱国运动的消息，并应允许转载外国报纸发表的评论或任何事实性文章”。

自政府实施新闻审查政策以来，全国各地的中国报纸均依此规定行事。结果如何？凡是中国报纸不准刊登的消息，都出现在外国报纸以及由外国人管理的中文报纸上。中国报纸如今被视为毫无价值的废纸。虽然中国读者深知中国报纸的困难，但为了获得新鲜可靠的消息，他们不得不阅读外国报纸或由外国人管理的中文报纸。他们认为，即使是在外国报纸或由外国人管理的中文报纸上刊登的谣言、猜测和夸张报道，也是可靠和可信的。因此，某些怀有特定动机的外国报纸故意发布谣言以欺骗公众。

政府目前的新闻政策导致一部分中国人不再阅读中文报纸。民众变得顺从，而外国侵略日益明显。政府的新闻政策至少应承担部分责任。这是一个非常不明智的政策。

正如《中央日报》所建议，政府应立即改变其新闻政策。

11月30日《大美晚报》（短评）：

民族精神与新闻集中管制

过去一个月华北局势非常复杂，似乎华北目前面临四面楚歌的危险。汉奸殷汝耕在非军事区内的二十多个县建立了“傀儡”自治政府。虽然国民政府在得知其叛乱消息后立即下令将其免职并逮捕，但迄今尚未采取有效措施。此事目前受到公众极大关注，许多人甚至发电报敦促政府立即采取措施平息这一运动。然而，仍有大量中国人对这一事态的严重性一无所知，并采取非常冷淡和漠不关心的态度。在国家危机的当前时刻，我们的民族精神竟沉沦至如此地步，实为深憾。

由于我们的报纸是向公众传递消息的主要手段，它们应当成为协助亲政府和爱国宣传的有益机构。这就是世界各国均采用新闻集中管制政策的主要原因。虽然这种制度在我国也盛行，但其执行方式与其他国家完全不同。

在我国，报纸不允许披露重要的政府和政治新闻。因此，毫无疑问，我们民族精神的软弱主要是由于采用了这种“哑巴”新闻政策。

我国目前正面临巨大危机。华北的麻烦将逐渐蔓延，敌军的部队每日在天津和北平周围集结。他们已控制平津线并占领了我们的火车站。在这种情况下，我们（新闻界人士）难道还应保持沉默，不努力激发我国的爱国情感，从而助长敌人的活动吗？

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 6, 1935 S. I RE...
S. B. D. 3019
7-12-35

CENSORSHIP POLICY
CRITICIZED

“Chen Pao” Points Out
Three Points To Be
Kept In Mind

Strong but constructive criticisms were made yesterday in an editorial published by the “Chen Pao,” a semi-official organ, of the Government’s censorship policy, which was blamed for the ignorance of the Chinese public of China’s international relations. The journal urged that the Government should be frank with its people and to this end three things were mentioned that the Government censors ought to do.

Although the recent developments on North China, the paper said, could be attributed the many factors, the present newspaper censorship policy adopted by the Government was to be blamed. It was alleged that the censors forbade the publication of news of the autonomous movement led by Mr. Yin Ju-keng in East Hopei until he issued a public statement to that effect and, as a result, the people received the news with much surprise.

The publication of such news before it was too late, the paper continued, would at least gave time for those plotting against the Government to reflect and for the people to know it beforehand so as to enable them to adopt preventive measure. The issuance of a warrant for Mr. Yin’s arrest was said to be useless, for Mr. Yin “was riding on a tiger” and had to go ahead with his programme. The journal insisted that the publication of news, even when unconfirmed, would do good to the public and mentioned Dr. Hu Shih’s denial of his sympathy with the autonomists as an example. Dr. Hu was once reported to have expressed sympathy with the separatist movement.

While not belittling the importance of preserving the military secrets of the country, the paper was sceptical about the efforts made by officials to keep the country’s diplomatic negotiations secret. No matter how humiliating the results of diplomatic negotiations might be, the people should be informed, the paper said.

Concluding, the paper outlined three policies that the censors should follow, namely, the publication of all news about actions detrimental to the country and people, full knowledge to be given to the public so as to enlighten the people in general in regard to facts being discussed by diplomatic officials, and fearless revelation of corruption among officials as a warning, to others.

新闻审查政策
受批评

《晨报》指出
需注意的三点

半官方机关报《晨报》昨日在一篇社论中对政府的新闻审查政策提出了强烈但具有建设性的批评，该政策被指责导致中国公众对中国国际关系无知。该报敦促政府应对人民坦诚，为此提到了新闻检查官应做的三件事。

该报称，虽然华北最近的 developments（原文不清/事态发展）可归因于多种因素，但应归咎于政府目前采用的新闻审查政策。据称，检查官禁止刊登殷汝庚先生在冀东领导的自治运动的消息，直到他公开发表声明为止，结果，民众得知此消息时大为惊讶。

该报继续称，趁为时未晚刊登此类消息，至少能让那些策划反对政府的人有所反思，并让民众事先知晓，以便他们采取预防措施。据说签发逮捕殷先生的令状是无用的，因为殷先生“骑虎难下”，不得不继续推行其计划。该报坚持认为，刊登消息，即使是未经证实的消息，也对公众有益，并举胡适博士否认同情自治派为例。胡博士曾被报道表示同情分离主义运动。

该报虽不贬低保守国家军事秘密的重要性，但对官员们保守国家外交谈判秘密的努力表示怀疑。该报称，无论外交谈判的结果多么屈辱，都应告知民众。

最后，该报概述了检查官应遵循的三项政策，即：刊登所有有关损害国家和人民行动的消息；让公众充分了解情况，以便就外交官员正在讨论的事实启迪广大民众；无畏地揭露官员中的腐败行为，以警示他人。

SI，
供您在编制
月度报告中关于此主题
的段落时使用。

November 2, 1935 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY 289
How Japanese Pressure and Chinese Censorship Are
Killing the Chinese Press

IN the issue of The Review for Oct. 19 there appeared an editorial discussion of the censorship situation in China wherein Prof: Hubert S. Liang of the School of Journalism of Yenching University told of the deplorable conditions now prevailing and urged that the censorship should either be made efficient or abolished entirely. Prof. Liang referred to several recent cases where the Chinese newspapers were not permitted to publish important news for periods ranging up to ten days and longer after the news had already appeared in the foreign newspapers in the port cities. One case referred to the detention of a high Chinese official within the Japanese Embassy compound in Peiping, an incident of far-reaching significance in that it was the first instance of Japan's asserted right to arrest and punish Chinese officials in North China who do not carry out the dictates of the Imperial Japanese army. No Chinese newspaper was permitted to print a line about this case despite the fact it received prominence in the foreign papers in China and also abroad. Another recent case was the Japanese ultimatum at Hankow compelling the Chinese authorities to dismiss the local garrison commander. The Japanese sent a half dozen gunboats to Hankow and threatened to bombard the Chinese city but the readers of the Chinese newspapers knew nothing about these stirring developments due to suppression of the news. The first knowledge that the people of Shanghai had of the incident was the receipt here of a brief message through a foreign news agency from Tokyo telling of the dispatch of Japanese warships to Hankow. The Japanese demands for the dismissal of Chinese officials at Hankow had been presented nearly three weeks prior to the publication of the news in Shanghai but had been suppressed by the censors.

Since the most important political and military developments in China, covering the period from the Japanese seizure of Manchuria in the fall of 1931 to the present have had to do with Japanese aggression, it is obvious that the chief inspiration behind the censorship is the Imperial Japanese Army which desires to keep its activities on the Continent shrouded in secrecy. One of Japan's latest demands concerning the suppression of all "anti-Japanese" activities is concerned with this important element of publicity and if the Nanking Government should consent to this it would result in the complete suppression not only of all publications regarded as antagonistic to Japanese aggression, but also would prevent the public utterance of any statement regarded as critical of Japanese policy.

There are few Chinese who realize the extent to which this Japanese-inspired Chinese censorship has already been established in this country. Last summer when Nanking was compelled to agree to the closing of all Kuomintang branches in Hopei, Chahar, and Suiyuan Provinces this carried with it the immediate closure of the Kuomin Jih Pao newspapers in all of the leading cities in these territories, including Kalgan, Peiping, Tientsin, Suiyuan-Kweihwa and Paotow. In many instances the Kuomin papers, being official organs of the Party, had become the leading papers of the cities where they were published, having circulations ranging from 5,000 to 8,000 depending on the size of the cities and towns where published. But they were suppressed, in accordance with the demands of the Japanese warlords and no other paper has been permitted to start up in their places. The situation in Shantung Province is almost as serious, although the Kuomintang party still functions in a limited manner. Several months ago a mob of Japanese reservists and rowdies in Tsingtao raided and smashed up the office of the Kuomintang paper in that city. The paper never resumed publication and recently the Kuomin paper in Tsinan, capital of the province, was discontinued as a result of Japanese objection to articles published in its columns. In some places new papers with outright pro-Japanese editorial policies have been started, edited nominally by some aged literati, but, one may be assured, with a Japanese loitering somewhere in the background, who pays the bills. The editors of two papers of this type, published within the Japanese concession at Tientsin, were murdered last summer by Chinese students. In some places such as Foochow in Fukien provinces the local paper Min Pao entirely owned by Japanese, but published in the Chinese language, has become the leading newspaper in the port.

At Shanghai, the Japanese have not attempted, in recent years at least, to publish papers in the Chinese language, confining their activities to the English-language press where they control the policy of one daily and two periodicals, one a monthly and the other a weekly. But recently there have been rumors of negotiations for the purchase of a leading Chinese daily. Sometime ago the Japanese newspapers in Shanghai began publishing sections or supplements in the Chinese language. These Chinese sections were subsidized by the Manchukuo government through the medium of the Kwantung army's representative stationed in Shanghai. They generally specialize in news and editorials depicting the glories of the puppet state under Japanese army rule.

Considering the censorship situation generally over the entire country the Japanese have had admirable success in suppressing the publication of news unfavorable to themselves. The Japanese consulates maintain staffs of translators who watch the Chinese papers and magazines for articles and editorial comment regarded as detrimental to "Sino-Japanese friendship," and a protest to the local Chinese officials is usually sufficient to bring

日本施压与中国审查制度如何扼杀中国报业

在10月19日出版的《评论报》中，刊登了一篇关于中国审查制度状况的社论讨论，燕京大学新闻学院的梁士纯（Hubert S. Liang）教授讲述了当前普遍存在的令人痛心的状况，并敦促要么使审查制度变得高效，要么将其彻底废除。梁教授提到了最近的几个案例，其中中国报纸在港口城市的外国报纸已经刊登重要新闻长达十天甚至更长时间后，仍不被允许发布这些新闻。其中一个案例涉及一名中国高官在北平日本大使馆馆区内被扣留，这一事件具有深远意义，因为这是日本首次声称有权逮捕和惩罚华北地区不执行大日本帝国军队指令的中国官员。尽管此事在中国及国外的外国报纸上占据了显著位置，但没有任何一家中国报纸被允许刊登关于此案的一行字。另一个最近的案例是日本在汉口发出最后通牒，强迫中国当局撤换当地驻军司令。日本派遣了半打炮舰前往汉口，并威胁要轰炸中国城市，但由于新闻遭到封锁，中国报纸的读者对这些激动人心的事态发展一无所知。上海民众得知此事的第一消息，是通过一家外国通讯社从东京发来的一条简短讯息，告知日本军舰已派往汉口。日本要求撤换汉口中国官员的要求，在上海刊登该新闻前近三周就已提出，但被审查官扣押。

鉴于自1931年秋季日本夺取满洲以来至今，中国最重要的政治和军事发展都与日本侵略有关，显而易见，审查制度背后的主要推动力是大日本帝国陆军，它希望将其在大陆的活动笼罩在秘密之中。日本最近关于镇压所有“反日”活动的要求之一，就涉及宣传这一重要因素，如果南京政府同意这一点，将导致不仅所有被视为反对日本侵略的出版物被完全压制，而且还会阻止公众发表任何被视为批评日本政策的言论。

很少有中国人意识到这种由日本煽动的中国审查制度在该国已经建立到了何种程度。去年夏天，当南京被迫同意关闭河北、察哈尔和绥远三省的所有国民党分部时，这也伴随着立即关闭这些地区所有主要城市（包括张家口、北平、天津、绥远-归化和包头）的《国民日报》。在许多情况下，《国民日报》作为党的官方机关报，已成为其出版城市的主要报纸，发行量根据出版地城镇的大小在5,000至8,000份之间。但它们按照日本军阀的要求被查封，且不允许有其他报纸取而代之。山东省的情况几乎同样严重，尽管国民党在那里仍以有限的方式运作。几个月前，青岛的一群日本后备役军人和流氓袭击并捣毁了该市国民党报纸的报社。该报从未复刊，最近，由于日本反对该报栏目中发表的文章，位于省会济南的《国民日报》也停刊了。在一些地方，出现了具有公然亲日编辑方针的新报纸，名义上由一些年老的文人编辑，但可以肯定的是，背后有某个日本人游荡并支付费用。去年夏天，在天津日本租界内出版的两家此类报纸的编辑被中国学生谋杀。在福建福州等一些地方，完全由日本人拥有但以中文出版的当地报纸《闽报》，已成为该港口的主要报纸。

至少近年来，日本人在上海并未尝试出版中文报纸，而是将活动局限于英文报业，他们控制着一家日报和两家期刊（一家月刊，一家周刊）的政策。但最近有传闻称，日本方面正在谈判收购一家主要的中文日报。不久前，上海的日本报纸开始出版中文版块或增刊。这些中文版块由伪满洲国政府通过驻扎在上海的关东军代表提供补贴。它们通常专门刊登描绘在日本陆军统治下傀儡国家荣耀的新闻和社论。

纵观全国范围内的审查制度情况，日本人在压制不利于自己的新闻发布方面取得了令人瞩目的成功。日本领事馆维持着翻译人员队伍，监视中国报纸和杂志中那些被视为损害“中日友好”的文章和社论评论，而向当地中国官员提出抗议通常足以带来

报纸代表团
请求制定新新闻法

南京，7月25日.—（国民社）.—中央政治委员会昨日在第467次会议上通过了监管出版物的标准。该标准规定：—
1. 出版物审查的标准应符合新闻法。
2. 记录历史事件的出版物不受国民政府6月10日关于培养与外国友好关系的命令所施加的限制。（例如，记录济南惨案或二十一条的出版物不应被禁止。）
3. 上述国民政府命令对命令发布前出版的出版物不具有追溯效力。
行政院和司法院应受命通知其各自下属机构上述内容。

July 6, 1935. Morning Tribune

Journal de Shanghai :-

DISADVANTAGES OF THE CENSORSHIP.

The Chinese Government, which has established an extremely severe censorship over the Press, to-day realizes the disadvantages of such a measure.

Some days ago, the "New Life Weekly" published an article entitled "Gossip about the Emperor of Japan" (? Gossip about Emperors) which was considered by the Japanese as offensive to their sovereign. As the person of the Emperor, to the Japanese Nation, is sacred and semi-divine, the Japanese Authorities have made representations to the Chinese Authorities and demanded an apology for the insult.

The offence of lese majeste is not to be found in the Criminal Code of the Republic of China. Nevertheless, in every country throughout the world, an Ambassador or a Minister can draw the attention of the Authorities to any attacks on their sovereign by a publication. But the affair is never permitted to go far in any country which enjoys freedom of the press.

For many years, the French Republic was allied with the Czar. Our revolutionary newspapers were not always very courteous towards the Czar of Russia. If our memory serves us well, several prosecutions were instituted against some of the pamphleteers whose vehemence went so far as to border on instigation to murder.

In a country where the freedom of the Press is considered an essential right, the publications and the authors of articles can only be prosecuted according to the conditions laid down by the law. All that the Government can do when a writer offends a foreign sovereign is to bring him before the Court and if the offence is proved the legal penalties will be imposed.

But the situation is not the same in a country where there is no freedom of the Press, for, every article which appears is censored in order to be given the approval of the censorship, that is to say, of the Government.

The Japanese Authorities have not failed to take advantage of the existence of the censorship in China to give a political aspect to the affair and to demand an explanation from the Chinese Government of the offence committed against their sovereign.

An official spokesman in Tokyo declares that the incident constitutes fresh proof of the duplicity of the Nanking Government which, on the one hand, is turning a friendly face towards Japan, and on the other, is instigating Press campaigns against the Mikado and his people.

On the day following Mr. Ishii's protest, the Chinese Authorities did everything they could to give satisfaction to Japan.

General Wu Teh Chen, the Mayor of Shanghai, who is not responsible for the follies of the censorship for it is not placed under his control,

（批：Reg. Please let me see what we have on file on this subject. J.K. 8 JULY 1935）

1935年7月6日。《晨报》

《上海日报》:-

审查制度的弊端。

中国政府对报业实施了极其严厉的审查制度，如今意识到了这种措施的弊端。

几天前，《新生活周刊》发表了一篇题为《关于日本皇帝的闲话》（？关于皇帝的闲话）的文章，被日本人认为是对其君主的冒犯。由于天皇对日本民族而言是神圣且半神性的存在，日本当局已向中国当局提出交涉，并要求为这一侮辱行为道歉。

中华民国刑法典中并没有亵渎君主罪。尽管如此，在世界各国，大使或公使都可以提请当局注意任何出版物对其君主的攻击。但在任何享有新闻自由的国家，此事绝不会被允许扩大化。

多年来，法兰西共和国与沙皇结盟。我们的革命报纸对俄国沙皇并不总是很有礼貌。如果记忆无误，曾对一些 pamphleteers（小册子作者/政论作家）提起过诉讼，他们的激烈言辞甚至达到了煽动谋杀的边缘。

在一个将新闻自由视为基本权利的国家，出版物和文章作者只能根据法律规定的条件被起诉。当一名作家冒犯外国君主时，政府所能做的只是将其送上法庭，如果罪名成立，将施加法律惩罚。

但在一个没有新闻自由的国家，情况则不同，因为出现的每一篇文章都要经过审查，以获得审查机构即政府的批准。

日本当局毫不利用中国存在审查制度这一事实，赋予此事政治色彩，并要求中国政府就对其君主的冒犯行为作出解释。

东京的一位官方发言人宣称，这一事件构成了南京政府两面派手法的新证据，该政府一方面对日本摆出友好面孔，另一方面却煽动针对天皇及其人民的报业运动。

在石井先生提出抗议的第二天，中国当局尽其所能以满足日本的要求。

上海市市长吴铁城将军，他对审查制度的愚蠢行为不负责任，因为审查制度并不受其控制，

（批注：长官，附件档案 A.A.D. 7月8日。[签名] 1935年7月7日）

July 6, 1935. Morning Translation.

has seized all the seditious copies of the "New Life Weekly" and charged Doo Zoong Yuen, the manager of the periodical, before the Chinese Court. Doo was unable to give the name of the author of the article and has been released on security.
But the Japanese are not interested in any satisfaction to be given by the Courts. They are insisting on the political aspect of the affair, that is to say, on the fact that the censorship had authorized the publication of the offending article and are demanding political reparation. Nothing official has been revealed regarding Japan's demands. Well-informed Japanese circles would simply say that the affair will be easily settled.
In the meantime, we learn that the Central Committee of the Kuomintang has resolved to dismiss the Chief and the staff of the Censorship Bureau in Shanghai.
For the Japanese investigation has unearthed the secret. This notorious censorship directed against the correspondents of the foreign newspapers is not a Government censorship but a Kuomintang censorship! We were right when we qualified the censorship as illegal.
It was already illegal because it was being imposed by the official Chinese Authorities on foreigners who enjoy extraterritoriality; it is doubly so because of the fact that the censorship is established in the Foreign Settlements.
But what makes matters worse is that the censorship is not the doing of the regular Chinese Authorities but of members of the Kuomintang. It is the same as if the Executive Committee of the Radical-Socialist Party in Paris had sent its representatives to the Exchange Bureau to supervise the messages of the British, American, Italian, German, Russian and other correspondents to their newspapers. In such a case, the Diplomatic Corps would have lodged a protest with the French Government which would hastily put an end to the illegal censorship established by the Radical-Socialist Party.
But in China, it is the Kuomintang which is exercising the right of censorship. One can only regret that the foreign Ministers in China have not yet found a collective formula of protest which would have created respect for the rights of the foreign Press.
We know that the Japanese have demanded that Nanking give a guarantee that such an incident would not occur again.
In that event, will the censorship be reinforced or will it be abolished? Or will other measures be taken?
In any case, if there had been no censorship in existence, the incident would have been a simple case of private rights. As it is, the arbitrary existence of this censorship has permitted Japan to make out a case of International Law.

G. M.

已查获所有煽动性的《新生》周刊副本，并将该期刊经理杜重远（Doo Zoong Yuen）移送中国法院起诉。杜未能提供文章作者的姓名，已获保释。
但日本人对法院给予的任何补救措施并不感兴趣。他们坚持此事的政治层面，即审查机构曾批准发表那篇冒犯性文章这一事实，并要求政治赔偿。关于日本的要求，官方尚未透露任何消息。消息灵通的日本圈子仅表示，此事将轻易解决。
与此同时，我们获悉国民党中常会已决定撤换上海图书杂志审查委员会的主任及职员。
因为日本的调查揭开了秘密。这种针对外国报纸通讯员的臭名昭著的审查，并非政府审查，而是国民党审查！当我们认定该审查为非法时，我们是正确的。
它之所以非法，是因为它是由中国官方当局强加于享有治外法权的外国人身上的；而由于该审查设立在外国租界内，其非法性更是加倍。
但使事态更加恶化的是，实施审查的并非正规的中国当局，而是国民党成员。这就好比巴黎的激进社会党执行委员会派遣其代表前往电报局，监督英国、美国、意大利、德国、俄国及其他各国通讯员向其报社发送的消息。在这种情况下，外交团本应向法国政府提出抗议，而法国政府则会迅速终止由激进社会党设立的非法审查。
但在中国，行使审查权的是国民党。人们只能遗憾地看到，在华外国公使们尚未找到一种集体抗议的方式，以确立对外国报业权利的尊重。
我们知道，日本人已要求南京方面保证此类事件不再发生。
在此情况下，审查制度是会加强还是会被废除？或者会采取其他措施？
无论如何，如果此前不存在审查制度，这起事件本将是一起简单的私权案件。正因这种任意存在的审查制度，使得日本得以援引国际法提出主张。

G. M.

Sin Jan Pao and other local newspapers

ORDER FOR THE PROTECTION OF NEWSPAPERS

During the 5th Plenary Congress held at
Nanking in 1934, the Shanghai Newspapermen's Association
and various newspapers at Tientsin and Peiping sent
many telegrams to the Congress with a request that
vigilance should be exercised in the censorship of
the press. The Congress referred the matter to
the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang,
the Military Affairs Commission and the Executive
Yuan to be dealt with.
The Military Affairs Commission and the
Executive Yuan have issued the following joint
circular order to various Provincial and City
Governments:-
"The newspapers at Tientsin and Shanghai
sent telegrams to the 5th Plenary Congress held in
1934 containing the following demands:-
1) That the censorship of the press be carried out
in accordance with the measures promulgated by
the Government and with strict vigilance.
2) That punishment on newspapers or newspaper-reporters
be not carried out with abnormal procedure.
3) That newspapers which have been banned or ordered
to close down by the Government Authorities or
reporters who have been given certain punishment,
be allowed to resume business provided that they were
not reactionary.
"The censorship of the press must be carried
out in compliance with the revised measures of the
Government as well as with the Press Law. Item 1
of the Appendix to the measures for the censorship
of the press contains clear stipulations and Articles
36, 37, 39, 40 and 41 of the Press Law point out
that newspapers violating the Press Law may be
prohibited from publication and the publishers,
editors etc. of these newspapers may be sentenced
to a term of imprisonment of less than a year.
Therefore, newspapers which have been banned or
ordered to close down by the Government or reporters
who have been given certain punishment should be
allowed freedom.
"With reference to the protection of freedom
of speech, the Government has ordered on several
occasions the various organs concerned to act in
accordance with Government orders. There are many
newspaper organs in the country conducted lawfully,
yet there are also unsound organs. These latter
organs are liable to commit crimes for they are in
the habit of disclosing military or diplomatic secrets
of the Government, or disseminating rumours wilfully
for the purpose of disturbing the public, or utilizing
the position of a newspaper to impair the reputation
of others in order to pay off a grudge. The Government,
of course, should make every effort to render support
to excellent newspapers, but it must take action
against those whose motives are beyond the law.

（批：Dang）

《申报》及其他本地报纸

保护报纸令

在1934年于南京举行的第五届全会上，上海记者协会以及天津和北平的各家报纸向大会发送了许多电报，请求对新闻审查保持警惕。大会将此事项移交国民党中央执行委员会、军事委员会和行政院处理。
军事委员会和行政院已向各省市政府发出以下联合通令：
“天津和上海的报纸向1934年举行的第五届全会发送电报，提出以下要求：
1) 新闻审查应按照政府颁布的措施严格执行，并保持高度警惕。
2) 对报纸或新闻记者的处罚不得采用异常程序。
3) 被政府当局禁止或勒令停业的报纸，或受到某种处罚的记者，若非反动分子，应允许其恢复营业。
“新闻审查必须依照政府修订后的措施以及《出版法》进行。新闻审查措施附录第1项中有明确规定，《出版法》第36、37、39、40和41条指出，违反《出版法》的报纸可能被禁止出版，这些报纸的出版人、编辑等可能被判处一年以下有期徒刑。因此，被政府禁止或勒令停业的报纸或受到某种处罚的记者应获得自由。
“关于保护言论自由，政府已多次命令各有关机关遵照政府命令行事。国内有许多依法经营的报纸机构，但也存在不良机构。后者容易犯罪，因为他们习惯泄露政府的军事或外交秘密，或故意散布谣言以扰乱公众，或利用报纸地位损害他人声誉以泄私愤。政府当然应全力支持优秀报纸，但必须对那些动机违法的报纸采取行动。

（批注：Dang）

THE BASIC PRINCIPLE OF PRESS CENSORSHIP.

The National Government has instructed
the various official organs to enforce the following
order :-
"At the 155th regular session of the
Central Kuomintang, a resolution relating to the

allowed."

Journal de Shanghai.

THE FREEDOM OF THE PRESS
(From our Special Correspondent)
Nanking, January 25.

Yesterday morning the Central Political Council
examined one of the most interesting questions of the present
time : the censorship of the press.

As the result of a petition submitted by the "Ta
Kung Pao" ("The Impartial") of Tientsin and of the Newspaper-
men's Association of Shanghai, demanding greater freedom
for the Chinese Press - a petition which was presented to
the recent Plenary Congress of the members of the Kuomintang -
the Central Political Council yesterday fixed the two
following principles regarding the freedom of the Press:-
1. The Press will henceforth be authorized to publish
"mild criticisms" of joint acts of the Government and
of the Party.
They will not be allowed to publish reports touching
on military or diplomatic questions held to be secret
or which may be prejudicial to the national interests
of China.
2. Newspapers may not publish information relating to
propaganda if such information is contrary to the Three
Principles of the People.

Detailed regulations relating to this censorship
have already been drafted by the Executive Yuan and by the
National Military Commission.

It is common knowledge that the opposition, at the
head of which stands Hu Han Min, had insisted on this freedom
of the Press in the three fundamental conditions and
preliminary conditions which it had submitted for a
rapprochement between Nanking and the South-West. It is

新闻自由
（本报特约通讯员）
南京，1月25日。

昨日上午，中央政治委员会审议了当前最有趣的问题之一：新闻审查。

鉴于天津《大公报》（“The Impartial”）及上海新闻记者协会向最近召开的国民党全体代表大会提交了一份请愿书，要求给予中国新闻界更大的自由，中央政治委员会昨日就新闻自由问题确定了以下两项原则：-
1. 今后，新闻界将被授权刊登对政府和党联合行动的“温和批评”。
不得刊登涉及被视为机密或可能损害中国国家利益的军事或外交问题的报道。
2. 报纸不得刊登与三民主义相悖的宣传信息。

行政院和全国军事委员会已起草了有关此项审查的详细规定。

众所周知，以胡汉民为首的反对派在提交用于南京与西南方面和解的三项基本条件及先决条件中，曾坚持要求实现新闻自由。这是

page_data.en:
2
perhaps to please the Opposition that the Central Political
Council yesterday adopted this decision.
It would be interesting, without doubt, to make
a rapid survey of the manner in which the various censorship
organs in the cities controlled by the Nanking Government carry
out their work.
At Nanking, every publication, under pain of
being banned or confiscated, must be submitted to the
censorship prior to being printed.
At Shanghai, apart from a so-called censorship
bureau to which all Chinese newspapers must submit their
proofs before publication, there is in existence a Supervisory
Committee for all other periodical publications, drawings,
pamphlets or books of any kind whatever. The editors
were bound, and are still bound, to submit to this
Commission proofs of their publications and to secure their
approval before printing.
----, w the practice of censorship in foreign
countries, Chinese censorship requires editors to replace
with proper words or phrases the words or phrases which
had been deleted by the censors. Apparently, the Chinese
authorities do not desire the public to be aware of the
existence of this censorship, for the "white spaces" would
have revealed too conspicuously the passage of the blue
pencil over the original "copy". The Bureau of Supervision
of Publications in Shanghai frequently compel editors to
retouch cartoons.
In principle, one must not criticise Fascism.
It is, above all, forbidden to say openly that the competent
authorities are favourable to Fascism. One must above all
abstain from publishing any declaration emanating from the
Opposition which criticises, even so slightly, acts of the
Government. In order to avoid the fate which has befallen
page_data.zh:
2
或许是为了取悦反对派，中央政治委员会昨日通过了这项决定。
毫无疑问，快速调查一下南京政府控制下的各城市审查机构如何开展工作将是很有趣的。
在南京，所有出版物在印刷前必须送交审查，否则将面临被禁或没收的风险。
在上海，除了一个所谓的审查局（所有中文报纸必须在出版前向其提交校样）外，还存在一个针对所有其他期刊、图画、小册子或各类书籍的监督委员会。编辑们过去有义务，现在仍有义务，将该委员会所需的出版物校样提交审批，并在获得批准后方可印刷。
----, w 与外国的审查做法不同，中国的审查制度要求编辑用适当的词语或短语替换被审查员删除的词语或短语。显然，中国当局不希望公众意识到这种审查的存在，因为“空白处”会过于明显地暴露出蓝铅笔在原“稿件”上划过的痕迹。上海出版物监督局经常强迫编辑修改漫画。
原则上，不得批评法西斯主义。
尤其禁止公开声称主管当局倾向于法西斯主义。最重要的是，必须避免刊登任何来自反对派的、即使只是轻微批评政府行为的声明。为了避免遭受上海一家大型日报数月前的遭遇——该报因刊登了一则关于韩复榘将军、阎锡山将军及北方其他几位将军发出呼吁要求“国家统一”的无害报道而被剥夺邮政服务——人们不得刊登任何可能伤害领导人敏感神经的报道。然而，人们可以自由刊登任何关于社会事务的内容，但条件是不包含任何涉及军事当局的内容。人们可以谨慎地表达对政府行为的看法，但必须做得圆滑得体：例如，可以说中国的行政机构总体而言是可以改变的，但目前的行政机构是无懈可击的！

J. Fentos。

审查与“审查”。
（社论）

读者们还记得，不久前，西南方面的政治领袖胡汉民在接受本报采访时宣布，他已提出与南京和解的三项条件。其中第一项条件是废除新闻审查。

中央执行委员会常务委员会采取这一举措，究竟是为了安抚广州的反对派并促进西南方面与中央政府结盟，从而并非废除审查，而是界定此项审查所依据的原则？

命令中的一节写道：“凡涉及党和行政事务的所有报道，以及出于善意发表的所有意见，均允许

3

a large daily newspaper in Shanghai which has found itself
deprived of postal facilities for having published, several
months ago, a harmless report that General Han Fu Chu,
General Yen Sih San and certain other Generals of the North
had issued an appeal demanding "national unification", one
must not publish any report that is liable to wound the

to publish anything it likes regarding social matters but

J. Fentos.

Censorship and CENSORSHIP.
(Leading Article)

Readers will recollect that recently Hu Han Min,
the political leader of the South-West, in the course of
an interview granted to this paper, declared that he had
submitted three conditions for his reconciliation with
Nanking. The first of these conditions was the suppression
of the censorship of the Press.

Is it to appease the Opposition in Canton and to
facilitate an alliance between the South-West and the
Central Government that the Permanent Committee of the
Central Executive Committee has taken this step, not to
abolish the censorship but to define the principles on
which this censorship is based?

One section of the order reads: "All reports
relating to the Party and to administrative affairs and
all opinions expressed in good faith are allowed to be

上海一家大型日报因在数月前刊登了一则无害的报道，称韩复榘将军、阎锡山将军及北方其他几位将军曾发表呼吁要求“国家统一”，从而导致该报被剥夺邮政便利；鉴于此，人们不得刊登任何可能伤害领导人敏感神经的报道。然而，人们可以自由刊登关于社会事务的任何内容，但条件是不涉及军事当局。人们可以谨慎地表达对政府行为的意见，但必须采取外交辞令：例如，可以说中国的行政机构总体而言是可以更迭的，但现任行政机构是无懈可击的！

J. Fentos。

新闻检查与新闻检查。
（社论）

读者们会记得，西南政治领袖胡汉民近期在接受本报采访时宣称，他已提出三项条件以谋求与南京和解。其中第一项条件便是废除新闻检查制度。

中央执行委员会常务委员会采取这一举措，究竟是为了安抚广州的反对派，并促进西南方面与中央政府之间的联盟，而并非废除新闻检查，只是界定该检查制度所依据的原则？

命令中的某一部分写道：“所有涉及党务和行政事务的报道，以及出于善意发表的意见，均允许

page_data.en:
4
published on the condition that they do not betray diplomatic
and military secrets and they do not harm the policy of the
Party or of the government. The newspapers must refrain
from expressing opinions that are contrary to those of the
Kuomintang."

In the first place, for an opinion on any affairs
concerning the Kuomintang and the government to be printed
in the Press, the author must be of good faith. This
anxiety is reasonable.

In the second place, no military or diplomatic
secrets are to be disclosed. In principle, this prohibition
need not trouble anybody for we do not believe that journalists
possess as many secrets as badly informed people suppose they
do. Most of the military or diplomatic information which
they may possess are furnished by the authorities themselves,
consequently what they know is what the government wants them
to know, especially so in China. Real diplomatic or military
secrets are procured by spies and these people do not work for
newspapers.

In the third place, a newspaperman must not write
anything that is harmful to the policy of the Kuomintang
or the Government. This is something more severe and it
will be interesting to learn if this will please the South-
West.

As for us, we will confine ourselves to a criticism
of the decision of the Central Executive Committee. In our
opinion the question of the censorship of Chinese newspapers
concerns the Chinese only. We would, however, like to make
this remark: Most of the large Chinese newspapers in Shanghai
and in North China are located in foreign settlements; they
have submitted to government censorship because a very large
number of their subscribers live outside the settlements as
well as in the interior provinces. In order to be able to
reach them, it is necessary for papers to be in agreement
page_data.zh:
4
刊登，条件是不泄露外交和军事秘密，且不损害党或政府的政策。报纸必须避免表达与国民党观点相左的意见。”

首先，要在报刊上刊登任何有关国民党和政府事务的意见，作者必须出于善意。这种顾虑是合理的。

其次，不得泄露任何军事或外交秘密。原则上，这项禁令无需困扰任何人，因为我们不相信记者拥有消息不灵通人士所臆测的那样多的秘密。他们可能掌握的大多数军事或外交信息均由当局本身提供，因此他们所知道的正是政府希望他们知道的，在中国尤其如此。真正的外交或军事秘密是由间谍获取的，而这些人为报纸工作。

第三，新闻工作者不得撰写任何有害于国民党或政府政策的内容。这一点更为严厉，了解这是否会让西南方面感到满意将是很有趣的。

至于我们，我们将仅限于批评中央执行委员会的决定。在我们看来，中国报纸的审查问题仅关乎中国人。然而，我们要提出如下评论：上海和华北的大部分大型中文报纸位于外国租界内；它们之所以服从政府审查，是因为其大量订户居住在租界外以及内地省份。为了能够触达这些读者，报纸必须与当局保持一致

page_data.en:
5
with the authorities.
We would like to voice a strong protest against the
illegal as well as absurd censorship which the Chinese
authorities are exercising in an international settlement
on telegrams which the correspondents of foreign newspapers
are daily sending to Europe and America.
This censorship is illegal on several counts. Above
all it is being exercised in an international settlement
when the right of censorship in the settlement belongs to
the authorities of the settlement. In establishing their
Avenue
censors on Edward VII, the Chinese Authorities have taken
the place of the authorities of the International Settlement
without having first consulted with them as well as without
having been authorised to do so by the Consular Body.
The censorship of telegrams sent out by foreign
newspaper correspondents to European and American newspapers,
is, in our view, illegal because it is contrary to the
principle of extraterritoriality, a right which most of
the correspondents enjoy.
The Chinese authorities realize fully that censorship
is not defensible so much so that they are keeping it a secret.
They have overlooked, however, that foreign newspapers are
sent out to China and that each correspondent can easily
ascertain whether his telegrams have been mutilated, delayed
or even falsified. They also seem to have overlooked the
fact that the editors of the newspapers in foreign countries
will be surprised that a telegram sent from Shanghai at 1 a.m.
on January 1 does not reach Paris until noon January 1, that
is to say, much too late for the news to be useful. The editors
are also surprised to learn that a telegram handed in by the
correspondent in Shanghai at 1 a.m. January 1 is not despatched
until 10 a.m. because the illegal censorship bureau had held
up the telegram for 9 hours. Perhaps the bureau had been
page_data.zh:
5
我们希望对中国当局在国际租界内对外国报纸通讯员每日发往欧美电报实施的非法且荒谬的审查提出强烈抗议。
这种审查在多方面是非法的。首先，它是在国际租界内实施的，而租界内的审查权属于租界当局。中国当局在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）设立审查员，取代了国际租界当局的职权，既未事先与其协商，也未获得领事团的授权。
我们认为，对外国报纸通讯员发往欧美报纸的电报进行审查是非法的，因为它违背了治外法权原则，而大多数通讯员享有这一权利。
中国当局充分意识到审查是站不住脚的，以至于他们将其保密。然而，他们忽略了外国报纸是发往中国的，且每位通讯员都能轻易查明其电报是否被删改、延误甚至伪造。他们似乎还忽略了一个事实，即外国报纸的编辑会感到惊讶，为何1月1日凌晨1点从上海发出的电报直到1月1日中午才抵达巴黎，也就是说，太晚了，新闻已失去效用。编辑们还会惊讶地发现，通讯员于1月1日凌晨1点在上海提交的电报直到上午10点才发出，因为非法审查局将电报扣留了9个小时。也许该局当时正在

page_data.en:
6
asleep. This delay in the despatch of telegrams frequently
renders them useless and results in serious loss for the
foreign newspapers which have to pay for the telegrams. They
would therefore be perfectly within their rights to demand
compensation from the Chinese authorities.
We have said that the censorship on foreign telegrams
is illegal, we now add that it is absurd. It will be sufficient
to publish the parts deleted by the censors in order to convince
the public of our assertion and perhaps to amuse them.
This is a second time that we have had to deal with
these abuses on the part of the Chinese authorities. We hope
that they will examine the objections we have written in regard
to the censorship of foreign telegrams and that they will take
a necessary action to put an end to these mistakes which are
more harmful to the prestige of the Chinese government than
the phrases which the censors often delete.

Georges Moresthe.
page_data.zh:
6
睡觉。这种电报发送的延误经常使其失去价值，并导致必须支付电报费的外国报纸遭受严重损失。因此，他们完全有权向中国当局要求赔偿。
我们说过，对外国电报的审查是非法的，现在我们补充说，它是荒谬的。只需公布被审查员删除的部分，就足以让公众相信我们的断言，或许还能逗乐他们。
这是我们第二次不得不处理中国当局的这些滥用职权行为。我们希望他们审视我们就外国电报审查所提出的异议，并采取必要行动终止这些错误，这些错误对中国政府声誉的损害，往往比审查员经常删除的词句更为严重。

Georges Moresthe。
