The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, January 20, 1933.    5360

New Rules On Press
Censorship Adopted
After Long Struggle

Years Of Agitation By Chinese Editors Brings
Change To Situation Which Caused Endless
Inconveniences; Many Improvements

PAPERS MAY EXPRESS VIEWS

(Reuter's Agency)
NANKING, Jan. 20.—After several years of persistent agitation on the part of the Chinese press in regard to press censorship, which in the past has caused endless inconveniences to the press, the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang has finally adopted a set of regulations concerning press censorship.
It is learned that five press censorship bureaux will be established immediately at Nanking, Shanghai, Peiping, Tientsin and Hankow.

Many Improvements
The improvements of the new ruling over the old press censorship system are many. Among the most conspicuous features of the new system are:
(1) The press knows definitely what type of news may be published and what may not be published.
(2) The censors will be competent representatives of the highest local political, military and Kuomintang offices.

Press Represented On Bureau
(3) The Press will be represented on the censorship bureau.
(4) Any disciplinary measures taken against the press must be in accordance with the Press Laws promulgated by the National Government.

Central Government Policy
(5) The press censorship work is unified as the general policy will be laid down by the Central Government. And no serious interferences are expected from local authorities.
Perhaps the most important of all is the provision that the local press may be represented on the censorship bureau. This is something which has never been done before. It gives the press an opportunity to put their views directly before the censors, and what is more important, the press can express their opinion before censors pass any judgment in regard to news publication.

Certain News Censored
The Government takes the attitude that only news affecting military affairs, foreign policy and local peace and order, should be considered by the censors.
In regard to news concerning other matters, the Press Law can take care of them.

Military News Tabooed
Military news which is tabooed by the Government has to do with secret military plans, movements and disposition of troops, transportation of ammunition, inaccurate or groundless military news.
The Government also desires non-publication of news concerning foreign affairs which are not yet announced by the Government or which may prejudice the progress of diplomatic negotiations.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1933年1月20日，星期五。    5360

经过长期斗争
通过新闻审查新规

中国编辑多年的抗争使造成无尽不便的局势发生改变；诸多改进

报纸可表达观点

（路透社）
南京，1月20日电。——鉴于中国报界多年来就新闻审查问题持续进行抗争，而过去的审查制度给报界造成了无尽的麻烦，国民党中央执行委员会最终通过了一套关于新闻审查的规章。
据悉，南京、上海、北平、天津和汉口将立即设立五个新闻审查局。

诸多改进
新规章相较于旧的新闻审查制度有许多改进之处。新制度最显著的特点包括：
(1) 报界明确知晓哪些类型的新闻可以刊登，哪些不可以刊登。
(2) 审查员将是当地最高政治、军事及国民党机构的称职代表。

报界在审查局中有代表
(3) 报界将在审查局中拥有代表。
(4) 对报界采取的任何纪律措施必须符合国民政府颁布的《出版法》。

中央政府政策
(5) 新闻审查工作实行统一，因为总体政策将由中央政府制定。预计地方当局不会进行严重干涉。
或许其中最重要的是规定地方报界可在审查局中拥有代表。这是以前从未有过的事情。这使报界有机会直接向审查员陈述其观点，更为重要的是，在审查员对新闻发布作出任何裁决之前，报界可以表达其意见。

某些新闻受审查
政府的态度是，只有涉及军事事务、外交政策以及地方治安与秩序的新闻才应由审查员审议。
至于涉及其他事项的新闻，《出版法》足以加以规范。

军事新闻被列为禁忌
政府列为禁忌的军事新闻涉及秘密军事计划、部队调动和部署、弹药运输，以及不准确或毫无根据的军事消息。
政府还希望不刊登有关尚未由政府公布的外交事务的新闻，或可能损害外交谈判进程的新闻。

October 7, 1932.
Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

Min Pao and other local newspapers:
ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS GOVERNING REGISTRATION OF NEWSPAPERS

A large number of local news agencies have already registered with the Newspapers & Magazines Examination Committee organised by the Municipality of Greater Shanghai. Of late, news agencies have demanded that the Examination Committee alter the conditions of its registration. As the Press Laws do not provide for any alterations, the Municipality has sent a petition to the Ministry of Interior requesting instructions to deal with the matter.

The Municipality has received the following dispatch from the Ministry of Interior:-
"Hereafter when matter arise regarding alterations in the registration of newspapers or magazines, the names of the newspapers or magazines to be changed as also of those persons responsible for the publications must be inserted in a registration form which must be sent to the Ministry together with their original registration certificates when application is made for new ones.
When a news agency wishes to change either its address, name of publication, names of editors and staff members, address of printing office, etc., a petition containing the alterations must be sent to the Municipal Government in the province in which the news agency is situate and this latter in turn will submit the petition to the Ministry to serve as a record."

The Municipality of Greater Shanghai yesterday notified its Bureaux of Public Safety and Education and the Newspapers & Magazines Examination Committee of the above instructions.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

PUBLIC SAFETY BUREAU TIGHTENS UP ON EXTORTIONISTS.

The Public Safety Bureau issued the following notice yesterday:-
"It has frequently happened that bad characters and loafers in the various districts under the jurisdiction of the Bureau distribute invitation cards bearing their own names or the names of their relatives for the purpose of obtaining money by extortion. Cases of assault which often result in persons being killed or wounded occur when their demand is refused. Acts of this description engaged in by local bad characters and loafers constitute a menace to the public safety and must be strictly prohibited.
"In addition to instructing the various subordinate organs to act accordingly, the Bureau hereby notifies the public to arrest the ringleaders who will be severely punished."

杂项

《民报》及其他本地报纸：
报刊注册附加规章

大量本地通讯社已向大上海市政府组织的报刊审查委员会注册。近来，各通讯社要求审查委员会修改其注册条件。由于《出版法》未规定任何变更程序，市政府已向内政部呈请指示以处理此事。

市政府收到内政部如下来电：
“此后，若出现报刊注册变更事宜，须将拟变更的报刊名称及出版负责人姓名填入注册表，并在申请新证时连同原注册证书一并送交内政部。
当通讯社希望变更其地址、出版物名称、编辑及职员姓名、印刷所地址等时，须向该通讯社所在省份的市政府提交包含变更内容的申请书，后者再将申请书转呈内政部备案。”

大上海市政府昨日已将上述指示通知其公安局、教育局及报刊审查委员会。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：

公安局严厉打击勒索者。

公安局昨日发布如下通告：
“本局辖区各区内，不良分子和游手好闲之徒经常分发印有自己或其亲属姓名的请柬，以此进行勒索钱财。若其要求被拒，常发生袭击案件，往往导致人员伤亡。此类由本地不良分子和游手好闲之徒所为的行为构成对公共安全的威胁，必须严加禁止。
除指令各下属机构依此行事外，本局特此通告公众逮捕为首者，他们将受到严厉惩处。”

Extract from the "Crystal", a mosquito paper, dated
September 18, 1932.

CENSORSHIP OF CHINESE NEWSPAPERS.

In view of the high tension existing amongst the
people in consequence of Japan's recognition of the puppet
"Manchukuo State" as also the manoeuvre indulged in by the
Japanese marines at various places, the Central Government
instructed the Municipality of Greater Shanghai the other
day to form a Publicity Department for the purpose of censoring
news items appearing in the newspapers.

At 4 p.m. September 15, the Municipality of Greater
Shanghai held a conference and invited the editors of the
various newspapers to attend for the purpose of discussing
the question of censorship. The newspaper delegates all
refused to countenance censorship on the bases of the law
granting freedom of speech. After a lengthy discussion,
the Municipality finally agreed to avoid the name of
censorship, but every night the newspaper delegates will
meet the Chief of the Publicity Department to examine all
news items. It was temporarily agreed that all news
concerning diplomatic and military affairs with Japan as
also those affecting the peace and order of the community
are to be scrutinized.

It is learned that this new ruling was officially
enforced on September 17.

摘录自1932年9月18日出版的小报《晶报》。

中文报纸的新闻审查。

鉴于日本承认傀儡“满洲国”以及日本海军陆战队在各地肆意挑衅，导致民众情绪高度紧张，中央政府日前指令大上海市政府成立宣传部，目的是审查报纸上刊登的新闻项目。

9月15日下午4时，大上海市政府召开会议，邀请各家报纸编辑参加，讨论审查问题。各报代表均以法律赋予言论自由为由，拒绝容忍审查。经过长时间讨论，市政府最终同意避免使用“审查”一词，但每晚各报代表将与宣传部主任会面，检查所有新闻项目。暂时商定，所有涉及对日外交和军事事务以及影响社区和平与秩序的新闻均须接受 scrutinized（审查/细查）。

据悉，这项新规定已于9月17日正式实施。

Date: Sept. 16, 1932.

Subject (in full)........................................Censorship of Chinese Newspapers........................................

Made by......Loh Sih Kya, C. A..........Forwarded by [签名]........................................

Sir,
    Recently the Municipality of Greater Shanghai received an order from Nanking directing it to devote attention to the publications made by local Chinese newspapers relating to the movements of the "Blood and Soul Corps for the Extermination of Traitors" which publications are considered provocative and likely to cause trouble.
    In view of the fact that the Provisional Constitution gives the newspapers the right of free expression, the Municipality of Greater Shanghai does not intend to enforce direct censorship on local newspapers. Chang Ting Yung (張廷榮), Chief of the Publicity Department of the Municipality, held a meeting on the afternoon of September 15 with the representatives of eight local daily newspapers to discuss the matter when it was resolved that each of these newspapers should appoint a member of their editorial staff to check over all news items before publication and any news of a suspicious nature should be reported by those persons entrusted with this work by telephone to Chang Ting Yung who will give instructions before the items are inserted in the newspapers.
    Mr. Chang has rented Room 601 of the Woo Kung (吳宮) Hotel at the corner of Fokien and Foochow Roads as his office where every night he will examine all news items supplied to newspapers by local news agencies and keep in touch with the various newspaper offices.
    There are three Sections under the control of the Publicity Department, one of which is the Newspaper Censorship Section. Chen Ko Zung (陳克成) (a Secretary of the Municipality) is the Chief of this Section, and will also be in Room 601 every night. He will be assisted in his work by three clerks.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Censorship of Chinese press-attached report by Mr.
Loh Sih-kya

Made by and Forwarded by Superintendent Robertson

This step on the part of the Chinese Authorities is
really an attempt to keep from publication any items bearing
on the activities of the Blood & Soul Corps and like organ-
izations which have for their aim the extermination of
"traitorous" merchants by drastic measures. The censorship
for the moment is mainly directed against advertisements
by shopkeepers who have received threatening letters accusing
them of dealing in Japanese goods and who fearing that the
next communication will be in the form of a bomb, attempt
to exonerate themselves through the columns of the press.
As a result of the censorship such advertisements no
longer appear in Chinese newspapers of any standing.

There has been no question as to what action the
Chinese Authorities will take in the event of their order
being defied, but the principal papers take it for granted
that disobedience will be followed by the withdrawal of
postal facilities, a very effective deterrent.

Jno Robertson

Subject (in full) Newspaper and Magazine Censorship Committee

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by Tho Robertson Supr

With reference to the Newspaper and Magazine
Committee, organized by the Municipality of Greater Shanghai
in December 1931, enquiries show that it has never actually
carried out censorship duties despite its announcement to this
effect. In short, this Committee is as yet only partially
organized as following the resignation of Mayor Chang Chun,
some members of this Committee also left their posts and
the arrangements made to fill the vacancies were further
delayed by the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese dispute on
January 28/29, 1932.

Enquiries at the local press and book companies
show that they have no knowledge of this Committee. According
to the Chinese newspaper offices they unanimously decided
not to submit to censorship of any kind and published a
declaration to this effect in the local newspapers on
December 12, 1931. This step is believed to be the outcome
of an attempt made by local students on and about December 9,
1931 to force the local press to publish full accounts of their
demands to the Mayor to enforce the execution of Col. Chen
Hsi-tseng, ex-Chief of the Public Safety Bureau for his
alleged oppression of the students' anti-Japanese movement.

The Newspaper Censorship Office established by the
Chinese Authorities on March 13, 1931 in the Wei Chung Hotel
(Room 24), 65 Shantung Road, was abolished on January 1, 1932.
in accordance with instructions issued by the 1st Plenary Session
recently held in Nanking.

Sih Tse Liang

关于大上海市政府于1931年12月组建的报刊杂志委员会，经查询，尽管其曾宣布履行审查职责，但实际上从未真正执行。简言之，该委员会迄今仅部分组建完成，因为在市长张群辞职后，该委员会部分成员亦离职，而填补空缺的安排又因1932年1月28/29日爆发的中日争端而进一步延误。

经向本地报业及书商查询，显示他们对这一委员会毫不知情。据中文报社称，他们一致决定不接受任何形式的审查，并于1931年12月12日在本地报纸上发表声明以此表态。据悉，此举是本地学生于1931年12月9日前后试图迫使本地媒体全面刊登其向市长提出的要求的结果，这些要求包括强制执行前公安局局长陈希曾（Chen Hsi-tseng，音译）上校死刑，因其被指压迫学生的抗日运动。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, January 5, 1932

Muzzling The Press In
The French Concession
(China Weekly Review)
An extraordinary situation has been created in the French Concession of Shanghai by an Ordinance promulgated by M. E. Koechlin, Consul General for France, and published in the Bulletin Municipal, the official organ of the French Concession, December 11.
The “teeth” in the ordinance are contained in the stipulation that no publication of any kind shall be published or sold in the French Concession of Shanghai without permission in writing from the French Consul General.
There are not a few subscribers of The Review in the French Concession and one of these days when something appears in these columns about vice conditions in the once ultra-respectable French Concession that the French Consul General doesn’t like he may even attempt to stop the postal employees from carrying this American journal to its subscribers.
Certainly he will, under the new ordinance, have power to stop the sale of the paper.
Undoubtedly the Ordinance is mainly aimed at the suppression of criticism in the French language, and rather strong attacks have been made on existing conditions by several local French journals of the “mosquito” type. It is unfortunate that some of these attacks are not made with the best of motives, but it is more unfortunate that conditions exist in the French Concession which warrant such attacks being made.
Certainly, in France itself no attempt to suppress the liberty of the press as is attempted by the French Consul General in Shanghai could succeed for a moment, but we are informed that the regulations which govern the French Concession go back to the days of the Empire, and that the liberal laws of the French Republic have not yet penetrated the benighted French Concession of Shanghai.
If the French Consul General can “get away with” anything of this sort it means that he can practically stifle all criticism of the existing regime, particularly in the French language, for practically the only clientele which a French journal can find in Shanghai is to be found in the French Concession.
That certainly would be unfortunate, for if there is one place in this world the administration of which is open to much criticism it certainly is the French Concession.
Luckily for the peace of mind of the ruling clique of the Concession, the Hangchow Conference this year was something of a fiasco or else the world would have been enlightened on French Concession conditions in a way that would have been startling.
page_data.zh:
2893。
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932年1月5日，星期二

在法租界钳制新闻
（《密勒氏评论报》）
法国驻沪总领事 E. 柯克林（E. Koechlin）先生颁布了一项法令，并于12月11日刊登在法租界官方刊物《市政公报》上，由此在上海法租界造成了一种非同寻常的局面。
该法令的“厉害之处”在于规定：未经法国总领事书面许可，不得在法租界出版或销售任何种类的出版物。
《评论报》在法租界有不少订户，总有一天，如果本栏目刊登了关于曾经极其体面的法租界内风化状况的内容，而法国总领事不喜欢，他甚至可能试图阻止邮政员工将这份美国期刊投递给其订户。
当然，根据新法令，他有权停止该报纸的销售。
毫无疑问，该法令主要针对压制法语批评，几家当地的“小报”类法文期刊对现状进行了相当激烈的抨击。不幸的是，其中一些抨击并非出于最好的动机，但更不幸的是，法租界确实存在招致此类抨击的状况。
诚然，在法国本土，像上海法国总领事所尝试的那种压制新闻自由的企图片刻都无法得逞，但我们获悉，管辖法租界的法规可追溯至帝国时代，法兰西共和国的自由法律尚未渗透进上海这个蒙昧的法租界。
如果法国总领事能“安然无恙”地推行此类措施，那意味着他实际上可以扼杀对现有政权的所有批评，特别是法语批评，因为法文期刊在上海几乎唯一的客户群就在法租界。
这确实是不幸的，因为如果世界上有一个地方的行政管理备受批评，那肯定是法租界。
幸运的是，为了租界统治集团的安心，今年的杭州会议 somewhat of a fiasco（有点失败/闹剧），否则世界将以一种令人震惊的方式了解法租界的状况。

总领事签署新法令

法国驻沪总领事柯希林（M. E. Koechlin）已颁布以下领事法令，并刊登在昨日的《法租界公报》上：——
（1）1926年5月17日第33号法令特此废止，并由下列条款取代：——
（2）未经法国总领事书面许可，不得在法租界内出版或销售任何期刊、报纸或评论。
未经法国总领事书面许可，不得设立任何出版或发行上述报刊的机构。
（3）为根据第二条获得许可，利害关系人应直接向法国总领事提出申请。该申请应清楚说明预期目标、许可受益人以及对许可使用负责的人员。
出版公司的章程（如有）应在提交申请时一并呈报，否则申请将被拒绝或许可将被撤销。
（4）若许可获准，任何报纸或评论在投入流通前，必须先向法国警察局和法国总领事馆各呈送一份样刊。
（5）若违反第二条第（1）款，编辑、销售者和发行者将受到起诉；若违反第二条第（2）款，该机构的董事或经理将由警察局及政治部（Surety Services）主管在对其有管辖权的法庭提起公诉。此外，总领事可宣布关闭该机构。
（6）第二条所规定的许可，不妨碍对任何违反公共和平与良好秩序的作品的许可持有人、作者以及（必要时）印刷者进行起诉。
（7）本法令自公布之日起生效。
（8）警察局及政治部主管负责执行本法令。

Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

Proposal to Introduce Regulations
to Check Subversive Activities.

It has been the policy of the Municipal Council for
many years to endeavour to keep the Settlement free from
activities likely to affect adversely the Republic of
China and other nations which contribute to its welfare.
The maintenance of this policy has become increasingly
difficult in recent years, and happenings during the
past two months have brought matters to something approach-
ing a crisis.

The disclosures in the Pan Pacific Trade Union
Secretariat Case (Noulens' case) showed that the Settlement
was being used as a base for activities aiming at causing
Communist upheavals in various parts of China, Japan, Korea,
Formosa, Hongkong, the Philippine Islands, Indo-China
and the Dutch East Indies, and other discoveries showed
that propaganda emanating from the Settlement was finding
its way to Europe and America. For some months previous
to the P.P.T.U. Secretariat case the Governments of the
countries mentioned were very concerned about intrigues
and propaganda originating in Shanghai and it is quite
conceivable that strong protests might have been made by
them either to the Chinese Government or Municipal Council
if means had not been found to check the undesirable
activities.

There is growing evidence that the "Reds" are rapidly
recovering from the check they received when their archives
were captured last Summer and that they will soon be

1932年1月26日。

警务处长。

先生：

关于引入规章以遏制颠覆活动的建议。

多年来，工部局的政策一直是努力确保租界内不发生可能对中华民国及其他对其福利有贡献的国家产生不利影响的活动。近年来，维持这一政策变得日益困难，过去两个月发生的事件使事态接近危机。

太平洋工会秘书处案（牛兰案）的披露表明，租界正被用作旨在引起中国各地、日本、朝鲜、台湾、香港、菲律宾群岛、印度支那和荷属东印度群岛共产党动乱的活动基地；其他发现也表明，源自租界的宣传品正流向欧洲和美国。在牛兰案发生前的几个月里，上述国家的政府对源于上海的阴谋和宣传深感忧虑，可以想象，如果找不到遏制这些不良手段的方法，他们很可能会向中国政府或工部局提出强烈抗议。

越来越多的证据表明，“赤色分子”正从去年夏天档案被缴获所受的挫折中迅速恢复，并且很快将

page_data.en:
- 2 -
bolder than ever before. "Red" handbills are already
on the increase and a "Red" newspaper in the English
language is appearing weekly.
It is true that subversive activities in
Shanghai can never be effectively checked without whole-
hearted and efficient co-operation from the Chinese
Government. However I suggest that everything possible
should be done to ensure that no allegation of negligence
in this matter can be made against the Municipal Council.
As a means to this end I recommend that the
Municipal Bye-Laws be altered to authorize the Municipal
Police to maintain in the Settlement effective control
over all political societies, labour unions, schools
and printed matter of all sorts.
The necessity for these bye-laws is evident from
the fact that such regulations are in force in the French
Concession and Chinese territory and that the Chinese
Authorities have in their efforts to maintain peace and
order among Chinese subjects in the Settlement found it
necessary on several occasions to endeavour to apply these
regulations in the jurisdiction of the Municipal Council.
I have recommended that the new regulations be
incorporated in the bye-laws in preference to any scheme for
the extension of bureaucratic laws to the Settlement for
the following reasons :-
1. The Chinese local Authorities and laws made by them
are liable to fail at critical times when their co-operation
and use is most needed.
2. The possibility of a Communist Government coming into
power, at least temporarily, in Nanking within the next
year has been suggested by some serious students of
Chinese politics.
page_data.zh:

比以往任何时候都更加大胆。“赤色”传单已经在增加，一份英文的“赤色”报纸每周都在出现。
诚然，如果没有中国政府全心全意且有效的合作，上海的颠覆活动永远无法得到有效遏制。然而，我建议应尽一切可能确保工部局不会在此事上受到失职的指责。
作为实现这一目标的手段，我建议修改《工部局附则》，授权工部局警务处对租界内所有政治团体、工会、学校和各类印刷品维持有效控制。
这些附则的必要性显而易见，因为此类规章已在法租界和华界实施，而且中国当局在努力维持租界内中国臣民的和平与秩序时，已多次发现有必要尝试在工部局管辖范围内应用这些规章。
我建议将新规章纳入附则，而不是采取任何将官僚法律延伸至租界的方案，理由如下：——
1. 中国地方当局及其制定的法律在最需要其合作和使用的关键时刻往往会失效。
2. 一些研究中国政治的严肃学者提出，明年之内南京政府有可能出现共产党执政的情况，至少是暂时的。

Consular Ordinance No. 45
(abolishing Ordinance No. 6 of Feb. 17, 1917.)
------------

I, Paul Emile Naggiar, Consul-General of France,
Chevalier of the Legion of Honour,

In consideration of Article XIII of the Regulations
of the Municipal Organization of the French Concession,
Order as follows:-

Article 1.--No meeting, bureau, association or group
of a political nature may be established in the French
Concession without the permission of the Consul-General
or his representatives.

Article 2.--Any person who desires to hold such a
meeting, to establish such a Bureau or to form such an
association or group must apply for permission to the
Chief of Police at least 48 hours beforehand. He must make
known the object of the meeting, the agenda of the sessions,
the character of the attendance and every information on
the statutes and objects of the associations or groups
and he must furnish a list of the names of the responsible
persons.

Article 3.--The present Ordinance annuls Ordinance No.6
of February 17, 1917.

Done at Shanghai May 3, 1927.

(Signed) Emile Naggiar.

RÈGLEMENT CONCERNANT LA PUBLICATION DES
PERIODIQUES—JOURNAUX—REVUES

(Ordonnance Consulaire No. 187 du 23 Novembre 1931).

Article I.—L'ordonnance No. 33 du 17 Mai 1926 est abrogée et remplacée par les dispositions suivantes.
Article II.—Aucun périodique, journal ou revue ne pourra être publié, distribué ou vendu sur la Concession Française sans l'autorisation écrite du Consul Général de France.
Aucun établissement ne pourra être fondé à l'effet de publier ou distribuer lesdits journaux ou revues sans l'autorisation écrite du Consul Général de France.
Article III.—A l'effet d'obtenir l'autorisation prévue à l'article II, une demande sera adressée directement par l'intéressé au Consul Général de France. Cette demande devra indiquer clairement le but poursuivi et la personne qui bénéficiera de l'autorisation et sera responsable de l'usage qui en sera fait.
Le dépôt des statuts de la Société de publication, s'il y a lieu, devra être fait en même temps que la demande, à peine de rejet de la demande ou de retrait de l'autorisation.
Article IV.—Si la demande est agréée aucun journal ou revue ne pourra être mis en circulation sans dépôt préalable d'un exemplaire à la Police française et au Consulat Général de France.
Article V.—En cas d'infraction à l'article II § 1 les éditeurs, vendeurs et distributeurs, et en cas d'infraction à l'article II § 2 les directeurs ou administrateurs de l'établissement seront poursuivis à la diligence du Directeur des Services de Police et de Sûreté, devant le Tribunal dont ils sont justiciables.
La fermeture de l'établissement pourra en outre être prononcée par le Consul Général.
Article VI.—L'autorisation prévue à l'article II ne fera pas obstacle aux poursuites exercées contre le bénéficiaire de l'autorisation, l'auteur et, le cas échéant, l'imprimeur d'un ouvrage contraire à la paix publique ou aux bonnes moeurs.
Article VII.—La présente ordonnance entrera en vigueur à la date de sa publication.
Article VIII.—Le Directeur des Services de Police et de Sûreté est chargé de l'exécution de la présente ordonnance.

Le Consul Général de France à Changhai.

关于出版期刊、日报、杂志的章程

（1931年11月23日第187号领事令）。

第一条.—1926年5月17日第33号令予以废止，并由下列规定取代。
第二条.—未经法国总领事书面许可，不得在法租界出版、分发或销售任何期刊、日报或杂志。
未经法国总领事书面许可，不得设立旨在出版或分发上述报纸或杂志的机构。
第三条.—为获得第二条规定的许可，申请人应直接向法国总领事提交申请。该申请须明确说明所追求的目的，并指明享有许可及对许可使用负责之人。
如有出版社团章程，应与申请同时备案，否则申请将被驳回或许可将被撤销。
第四条.—如申请获准，在向法国警务处和法国总领事馆各预先呈缴一份样本之前，任何报纸或杂志不得发行。
第五条.—如违反第二条第一款，发行人、销售人和分发人将受到追诉；如违反第二条第二款，该机构的负责人或管理人将受到追诉。上述追诉由警务与治安总监提请其所属管辖法院进行。
此外，法国总领事可下令封闭该机构。
第六条.—第二条规定的许可，不妨碍对许可持有人、作者以及在情况需要时对印刷商就危害公共安宁或风化之作品提起的诉讼。
第七条.—本令自公布之日起生效。
第八条.—警务与治安总监负责执行本令。

驻上海法国总领事

RULES GOVERNING THE HOLDING OF MEETINGS BY PUBLIC
BODIES IN SHANGHAI.

(I) Procedure Relating To The Holding Of Meetings
By Labour Unions.

The People's Training Department of the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, the Bureau of Social Affairs
and the Public Safety Bureau have issued a joint
proclamation announcing that in order to accord protection
to Labour Unions and to place restriction on illegal bodies,
the People's Training Department, the Bureau of Social
Affairs and the Public Safety Bureau held a conference
on January 24 this year (?) to discuss this matter and
the following decisions were reached:-

1) If a Labour Union, which is already in existence,
secures permission for continuance of its existence, and a
record of which permission is on file with the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, and for which permission to
register has been granted by the Bureau of Social Affairs,
propose to hold a meeting, it must apply to the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, five days prior to the date
fixed for the meeting, to appoint a deputy to give
directions. The Shanghai Special District Kuomintang
will communicate to this effect with the Bureau of Social
Affairs which will transmit the communication to the
Public Safety Bureau which will in turn order the Police
Station of the District concerned to detail the Police
Force to accord protection.

2) Unless the abovementioned procedure is observed,
the Public Safety Bureau may prohibit the holding of a
meeting, and arrest and punish any person who refuses to
comply with the order.

3) After their reorganization by the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, all Labour Unions should,
in accordance with the order issued by the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang, apply to the Bureau of
Social Affairs for registration. A small Labour Union
must complete the registration within two weeks, while
a large Labour Union must complete the registration
within three weeks. When a Labour Union fails to
complete the procedure within the time fixed, the Bureau
of Social Affairs shall communicate with the Public Safety
Bureau to arrange for its suppression.

4) From the date on which this proclamation is
issued, all Labour Unions which have already been
inaugurated shall, within two weeks, apply to the
Shanghai Special District Kuomintang for permission
to continue their existence, and to the Bureau of Social
Affairs for registration. Any Labour Union which fails
to comply with this procedure within the fixed time,
shall be closed by the Public Safety Bureau at the
instance of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang
through the Bureau of Social Affairs.

On May 1 the Bureau of Social Affairs, in a
letter, stated that in dealing with the case of the
Preparatory Office of the Chinese Cement Factory Workers'
Union for making preparations to hold a meeting, the Bureau
page_data.zh:
上海公共团体举行会议规则。

(一) 关于工会举行会议的程序。

上海特别区国民党民众训练部、社会局和公安局联合发布公告，宣布为了保护工会并限制非法团体，民众训练部、社会局和公安局于今年（？）1月24日召开会议讨论此事，并达成以下决定：-

1) 如果已存在的工会获得了继续存在的许可，且该许可记录在上海特别区国民党档案中，并已获得社会局颁发的注册许可，拟举行会议时，必须在预定会议日期前五日向上海特别区国民党申请，由其指派一名代表进行指导。上海特别区国民党将就此与社会局沟通，社会局再将函件转达公安局，公安局随后命令相关辖区警察分局派遣警力提供保护。

2) 除非遵守上述程序，否则公安局可禁止举行会议，并逮捕和惩罚任何拒绝服从命令的人。

3) 所有工会经上海特别区国民党改组后，应按照上海特别区国民党发布的命令，向社会局申请注册。小型工会必须在两周内完成注册，大型工会必须在三周内完成注册。如果工会未在规定期限内完成手续，社会局将与公安局联系，安排予以取缔。

4) 自本公告发布之日起，所有已成立的工会应在两周内向上海特别区国民党申请继续存在之许可，并向社会局申请注册。任何未能在规定期限内遵守此程序的工会，将由上海特别区国民党通过社会局提请公安局予以封闭。

5月1日，社会局在一封信中指出，在处理中国水泥厂工人工会筹备处准备举行会议一案时，该局

found itself in a dilemma because the preparatory
Labour Union meetings were different from meetings
held by Labour Unions. Should the procedure governing
the holding of meetings decided by our previous
joint conference be adopted or should separate rules
be drawn up? The letter was transmitted to the
People's Training Department of the Shanghai Special
District Kuomintang, with a request that the conference
be held on a fixed date and place. Subsequently
a reply from the People's Training Department was
received stating that as the various public bodies
have complained that the procedure governing the
holding of meetings is difficult to be complied with
and asked for its cancellation, the executive committee
of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang decided
at its 18th meeting that the rules, drawn up recently
governing the holding of meetings by the various public
bodies, be brought up at the informal conference of the
Shanghai Special District Kuomintang and the local
civil and military authorities for consideration, and
it was resolved that these rules be cancelled at once
and that the provisional regulations governing the
holding of meetings by the people's public bodies be
drawn up. Upon receipt of this notification, a letter
to this effect was sent to the Bureau of Social Affairs.

(II) Procedure Relating to the Holding of Meetings
by the Merchants Federation, Industrial or
Commercial Branch Associations, Charitable
Institutions, etc.

The following decisions have been reached by
a joint conference held by the Shanghai Special District
Kuomintang, the Bureau of Social Affairs, the Merchants'
Federation and the Public Safety Bureau:-

1) That if the Merchants Federation or any
one of the various industrial or commercial branch
associations, for which permission for its continued
existence has been granted and is on record with the
Shanghai Special District Kuomintang, and for which
permission for registration has been granted by the
Bureau of Social Affairs, propose to hold a general
meeting, it shall, five days prior to the date fixed
for the holding of the proposed meeting, submit a report
to this effect to the Shanghai Special District
Kuomintang which will communicate with the Bureau of
Social Affairs. The latter will notify the Public
Safety Bureau who will, in turn, direct the Police
Station of the District concerned to detail policemen
to accord protection.

2) That the Bureau of Social Affairs publish
a weekly list containing particulars of the Merchants'
Federation, the various industrial and commercial branch
associations, the Street Unions, the various Guilds,
public bodies, etc., for which registration has already
been granted by the Bureau of Social Affairs, and
send 43 copies of this list to the Public Safety Bureau
to be distributed to the various Police Stations to be
kept on record.

On April 26 the Bureau of Social Affairs,
in a letter, stated that it is in receipt of a petition
from the Merchants Federation stating that according
to a decision reached at a joint conference of the

感到进退两难，因为工会筹备会议与工会举行的会议不同。是应采用我们此前联席会议决定的会议举行程序，还是应另行制定规则？该信已转交上海特别区国民党民众训练部，请求在固定的日期和地点召开会议。随后收到民众训练部的回复，称由于各公共团体抱怨会议举行程序难以遵守并要求取消，上海特别区国民党执行委员会在第18次会议上决定，将最近制定的关于各公共团体举行会议的规则，提交至上海特别区国民党与当地军政当局的非正式会议审议，并决议立即取消这些规则，并起草关于人民公共团体举行会议的暂行条例。收到此通知后，已就此致函社会局。

(二) 关于商会、工业或商业同业公会、慈善机构等举行会议的程序。

上海特别区国民党、社会局、商会和公安局召开的联席会议达成了以下决定：-

1) 如果商会或任何工业或商业同业公会（其继续存在的许可已获批准并记录在上海特别区国民党档案中，且已获得社会局颁发的注册许可）拟举行全体会议，应在预定会议日期前五日向上海特别区国民党提交报告，上海特别区国民党将与社会局沟通。后者将通知公安局，公安局随后指示相关辖区警察分局派遣警察提供保护。

2) 社会局发布一份周报，列出已获社会局注册批准的商会、各工业和商业同业公会、街道联合会、各公所、公共团体等的详细信息，并将该名单副本43份送交公安局，分发给各警察分局存档。

4月26日，社会局在一封信中表示，收到商会的请愿书，称根据

page_data.en:
3

Shanghai Special District Kuomintang, the Bureau of
Social Affairs and the Public Safety Bureau, a petition
applying for permission to hold a meeting shall be
forwarded five days prior to the holding of the proposed
meeting and it shall be transmitted to four Government
organs. Should the transmission be delayed on account
of holidays or other causes, the holding of meetings
is to be prohibited. Furthermore, the industrial
or commercial branch associations often hold
extraordinary meetings of members in case some important
affair occurs. It is difficult for them to comply
with the procedure. This matter was brought up for
discussion at the 46th committee meeting of the Merchants'
Federation and it was resolved that if an industrial
or commercial branch association propose to hold a
meeting with its members, it shall, one week prior to
the date of holding the proposed meeting, submit a report
to this effect to the Federation, which will, in turn,
report same to the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang
and the Bureau of Social Affairs and will request the
Bureau of Social Affairs to ask the Public Safety Bureau
to detail the Police Force to accord protection. If an
extraordinary meeting be held, the Federation will,
owing to the pressure of time, send men to call at the
various aforesaid Government organs to make verbal
request.
Upon receipt of this letter, the Bureau of
Social Affairs which considers that this proposal is
contrary to the decisions of the joint conference,
communicated with the People's Training Department
of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang.
Subsequently a reply from the People's Training Department
was received stating that as the reasons given by the
Merchants Federation relating to the holding of
meetings are reasonable, concessions would be made in
the case of extraordinary meetings and that the Federation
should submit a report to the Department for instructions.
In addition, it should forward a report to the Bureau
of Social Affairs for purpose of record.

3) The following is the reason why a Labour
Union or public body shall observe the procedure when
holding a meeting:-
The inauguration, training and registration
of Labour Unions and Public Bodies are under the direction
management of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang
and the Bureau of Social Affairs. Thus they know clearly
the condition of the various labour unions and public
bodies. The direct connection between the Public Safety
Bureau and the various labour unions and public bodies
is very slight. Unless the Shanghai Special District
Kuomintang or the Bureau of Social Affairs send a despatch
to the Public Safety Bureau, the latter will find it
difficult to accord protection or on placing restrictions.
It is necessary for the three Government organs to work
in co-operation when dealing with the movements of the
masses and from this good results will be attained.

Translated by Leh Sih Kyia,
Clerk, Special Branch 3.5
Jan. 18, 1932.

上海特别区国民党、社会局和公安局联席会议的决定，申请举行会议的请愿书应在预定会议举行前五日递交，并需转送四个政府机关。如果因节假日或其他原因导致转送延误，则禁止举行会议。此外，工业或商业同业公会在发生重要事务时经常召开会员临时会议。它们很难遵守该程序。此事在商会第46次委员会议上提出讨论，并决议：如果工业或商业同业公会拟与其会员举行会议，应在预定会议日期前一周向商会提交报告，商会再向上海特别区国民党和社会局报告，并请社会局要求公安局派遣警力提供保护。如果举行临时会议，鉴于时间紧迫，商会将派人前往上述各政府机关进行口头请求。
社会局收到此信后，认为该提议与联席会议的决定相悖，遂与上海特别区国民党民众训练部沟通。随后收到民众训练部的回复，称鉴于商会提出的关于举行会议的理由合理，对于临时会议可作出让步，商会应向该部提交报告以请示指令。此外，还应向社局提交一份报告以备存档。

3) 工会或公共团体在举行会议时应遵守程序的原因如下：-
工会和公共团体的成立、培训和注册均在上海特别区国民党和社会局的指导管理之下。因此，它们清楚地了解各工会和公共团体的状况。公安局与各工会和公共团体之间的直接联系非常微弱。除非上海特别区国民党或社会局向公安局发出公文，否则公安局将难以提供保护或实施限制。三个政府机关在处理群众运动时必须协同合作，这样才能取得良好的效果。

译者：Leh Sih Kyia（音译），
特务科三等书记
1932年1月18日。

Regulations governing the censoring of mosquito papers by
the Education Bureau of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai.
Permission for the enforcement of these Regulations was given
on October 31 in the 16th Year of the Republic (1927). These
Regulations were revised on June 26 in the 18th Year (1929).

------------------

Article 1. All mosquito papers published or sold in
this locality must be registered at this Bureau. Copies of
every issue must be forwarded to this Bureau for examination.
Article 2. When applying for registration, every
mosquito paper must give detailed particulars of the address
and the name of the publisher and of the editor. If the
mosquito paper is a new one, a copy of the first issue of
the paper must be enclosed with the petition. If the paper
is an old one, three copies of the latest issue must be
enclosed.
Article 3. Registration will be granted by this
Bureau if, after examination, it is found that the mosquito
paper satisfies any one of the following objects:-
A) Propagating the doctrines of the Kuomintang and
guiding the masses to work for the people's revolution.
B) Conducting research into the problems of
livelihood, customs and habits of the masses and guiding
them in the abolition of old habits.
C) Advocating knowledge or education or social
utilities.
Article 4. This Bureau will issue a registration
certificate and will give permission for the sale of a
mosquito paper if the examination is found satisfactory.
Article 5. If a mosquito paper make any changes
or stop publication after registration, the publisher concerned
must forward a report to this Bureau to be kept on record.

大上海市政府教育局审查小报条例。
本条例于民国十六年（1927年）10月31日获准施行。本条例于民国十八年（1929年）6月26日修订。

------------------

第一条. 凡在本地区出版或销售之所有小报，均须向本局登记。每期样本须送交本局审查。
第二条. 申请登记时，每份小报须提供出版人及编辑之姓名与地址之详细资料。若该小报为新创办者，申请书须附首期报纸一份。若为旧有报纸，须附最新一期报纸三份。
第三条. 经审查，若发现该小报符合下列任一宗旨，本局将准予登记：-
A) 宣扬国民党主义，引导民众致力于国民革命。
B) 研究民众之生计、风俗习惯问题，并引导其革除旧习。
C) 提倡知识、教育或社会公益。
第四条. 若审查结果满意，本局将颁发登记证，并准许该小报销售。
第五条. 若已登记之小报有任何变更或停刊，相关出版人须向本局提交报告以备案。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Article 6. If the examination of a mosquito paper
is satisfactory and the paper has seldom made mistakes,
permission for publication on probation will be given by
this Bureau which will send a letter warning the publisher
to make certain changes.

Article 7. This Bureau will permit registration to
those mosquito papers which have made changes after securing
permission for publication on probation.

Article 8. No registration will be permitted if any
one of the following be found at the time of examination:-
A) articles Contrary to the Three Principles of the People.
B) Sedition, thereby menacing the peace and good
order.
C) Indecent literature liable to seduce youths.
D) Slander against the reputation of individuals.
E) Publication of false reports with a view to
extortion.

Article 9. The following punishment shall be imposed
on a mosquito paper which publishes without registration:-
A) This Bureau will request the Municipality
of Greater Shanghai to order either the Public Safety
Bureau or the Provisional Court to give instructions to
the paper in question to stop publication or to prohibit
its publication and sale.
B) This Bureau will request the Municipality
of Greater Shanghai to order either the Public Safety Bureau
or the Provisional Court to seal up the office of the paper
in question or to arrest the publisher and the editor if
the offense is serious.

Article 10. This Bureau will either give a warning
or withdraw the registration if an examination of every issue
shows that the management has not acted properly.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

第六条. 若对小报之审查结果满意，且该报鲜有失误，本局将给予试办出版许可，并发函警告出版人进行某些修改。

第七条. 对于在获得试办出版许可后已进行修改之小报，本局将准予登记。

第八条. 若在审查时发现有下列情形之一者，不予登记：-
A) 文章违背三民主义。
B) 煽动叛乱，从而危及和平与良好秩序。
C) 淫秽刊物，易诱坏青年。
D) 诽谤个人名誉。
E) 发布虚假报道以图敲诈勒索。

A) 本局将请求大上海市政府命令公安局或临时法院指令该报停止出版，或禁止其出版与销售。
B) 若情节严重，本局将请求大上海市政府命令公安局或临时法院查封该报馆，或逮捕出版人及编辑。

第十条. 若对每期之审查显示管理层行为不当，本局将予以警告或撤销登记。

January 18,1932.

Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

Political Meetings.

In view of the extraordinary conditions which
exist at the present time and the partial break down
of the control exercised by the Chinese Authorities
in the administrative affairs of the Settlement, the
ordinary laws, I suggest, are not sufficient authority
to enable the Police to maintain law and order.
I therefore recommend that the order regarding political
meetings be published in the Chinese and Foreign press
and that the Council be asked to authorize the police
to break up every meeting which is held in contravention
of its terms. The order regarding political meetings
was issued on May 21, 1926 and reads as follows :-

"Notice is hereby given that no meeting,
"parade, demonstration, or party of a political
"nature is allowed within the Settlement, without
"special permission of the Council first had and
"obtained.
"Any person or persons wishing to convene
"such meeting, parade, demonstration or party of
"a political nature, shall apply for the necessary
"permission at least forty eight hours in advance
"to the Commissioner of Police stating the object
"of the meeting and giving full information as to
"the attendance and subjects to be discussed"
(Please see Handbook of Municipal Information
issued in 1931, page 35).

Officer i/c Special Branch.

December 15, 1931.

FRENCH CONCESSION PRESS LAWS.

New Ordinance Signed by Consul General.

The following Consular Ordinance has been
promulgated by M. E. Koechlin, Consul-General for France,
and published in the Bulletin Municipal:-
(1) Ordinance of No.33, of May 17, 1926, is hereby abrogated
and replaced by the following provisions:-
(2) No periodical, journal nor review shall be published
or sold in the French Concession without permission
in writing from the French Consul-General.
No establishment shall be created for the publication
or distribution of the said journals without the
permission in writing of the French Consul-General.
(3) In order to obtain permission in accordance with
article II, a request shall be addressed directly by
the person interested, to the Consul-General for France.
This request shall indicate clearly the object in
view, the person who will benefit under the permit
and who will be responsible for the use made of it.
The Articles of the publishing firm, if there are
any, shall be deposited at the same time as the request
on pain of a rejection of the request, or withdrawal
of the permit.
(4) If the permit is granted no journal or review shall
be put into circulation unless a sample copy has been
first deposited with the French Police and the French
Consulate-General.
(5) In the event of an infringement of Art.II (1) the
editors, sellers and distributors, and in the event
of an infringement of Art.II (2) the directors or
managers of the establishment will be prosecuted by
the Directors of the Police and Surety Services in
the tribunals before which they are justiciable.
The closing of the establishment, in addition, may
be declared by the Consul-General.
(6) The permit contemplated by Article II shall prove no
obstacle to the prosecution of the holder of the permit,
the author and, if need be, the printer of any work
contrary to public peace and good order.
(7) The present ordinance will come into force on the date
of its publication.
(8) The Chief of the Police and Surety Services is entrusted
with the execution of this present ordinance.

法租界报业法规。

总领事签署之新条例。

以下领事条例已由法国总领事 M. E. Koechlin 颁布，并刊登于《市政公报》：-
(1) 1926年5月17日之第33号条例 hereby 废止，并由以下规定取代：-
(2) 未经法国总领事书面许可，不得在法租界出版或销售任何定期刊物、报纸或评论。未经法国总领事书面许可，不得设立用于出版或分发上述刊物之机构。
(3) 为根据第二条获得许可，利害关系人应直接向法国总领事提出申请。该申请应明确指明目的、受益人以及对许可使用负责之人。若有出版公司章程，须随申请一并提交，否则申请将被驳回或许可被撤销。
(4) 若获发许可，除非先将样本存放于法国巡捕房及法国总领事馆，否则任何报纸或评论不得发行。
(5) 若违反第二条第(1)款，编辑、销售商及分销商；若违反第二条第(2)款，机构之董事或经理，将由警务与保安服务处总监在其所属管辖法庭提起诉讼。此外，总领事可宣布关闭该机构。
(6) 第二条所述之许可不妨碍对许可证持有人、作者以及必要时印刷商就任何违背公共和平与良好秩序之作品提起诉讼。
(7) 本条例自公布之日起生效。
(8) 警务与保安服务处总监负责执行本条例。

October 6, 1941.

Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau - Despatch
No. 30 from the Police Bureau of the
Shanghai City Government

With reference to the attached despatch
dated September 30, 1941 to the Acting Commissioner
of Police from the Police Bureau of the Shanghai
City Government on the subject of the Shanghai Press
Censorship Bureau situated in the Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road, it has to be pointed out that this
Bureau was originally established jointly by the
Japanese Expeditionary Forces in Central China and
the local Japanese Consulate-General with the object
of exercising control over the local Chinese language
newspapers, both leading dailies and mosquito papers.
It was for this reason that a number of local Chinese
language pro-Chungking dailies have registered
their publications in the names of third Power
nationals whereby they have evaded censorship by
the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau. Later, on
December 16, 1940, the Bureau was officially handed
over to the Nanking Government and placed nominally
under the charge of one Lieu Zah-keh (刘石克),
the Chief Editor of the "Central China Daily News,"
the principal publicity organ in Shanghai of Wang
Ching-wei; in reality, however, it is still under
the control of the Japanese.

At the very beginning, i.e. at the time
when the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau was first
established, there were but few Chinese language
newspapers and news agencies in Shanghai. At that
time nearly all of them submitted to censorship of
the Shanghai Press Censorship Bureau. At present,

1941年10月6日。

上海新闻检查局 - 来自
伪上海市警察局之
第 30 号公函

关于所附1941年9月30日伪上海市警察局致代理警务处处长之公函，主题涉及位于南京路哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）之上海新闻检查局，需指出的是，该局最初由日本华中派遣军与当地日本总领事馆共同建立，旨在控制当地中文报纸，包括主要日报和小报。正因如此，一些当地亲重庆（Chungking）之中文日报以第三国国民名义登记其出版物，从而规避上海新闻检查局之审查。后来，于1940年12月16日，该局正式移交给南京政府，名义上由汪精卫在上海之主要宣传机构《中华日报》总编辑刘石克（Lieu Zah-keh）负责；然而实际上，它仍受日本人控制。

起初，即上海新闻检查局刚成立之时，上海之中文报纸及通讯社寥寥无几。当时，几乎所有报社均服从上海新闻检查局之审查。目前，

page_data.en:

however, only the proofs of pro-Nanking dailies
and mosquito papers are understood to be censored
before publication by the Shanghai Press Censorship
Bureau; however, the pro-Chungking dailies do not
submit proofs to the Shanghai Press Bureau for
censorship, but abide by the S.M.C. ruling.
As regards the complaints contained
in the attached despatch against the Ningpo Kung
Pao (寧波公報) and the Chung Kuo Shang Pao
(中國商報), it has to be pointed out that both
of these papers are of mosquito type and are not
censored by the S.M.P. So far as is known to this
office, the Ningpo Kung Pao has been run for some
considerable time and is devoted to the publication
of news on conditions in Ningpo for the information
of Ningpo residents in Shanghai, but the Chung Kuo
Shang Pao is believed to be receiving regular
subsidies from Shao Chih-chun (邵式軍),
Commissioner of the Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei
Consolidated Tax Bureau, No. 230 Kiukiang Road.
Whether or not these two papers are submitting their
proofs for censorship by the Shanghai Press Bureau
is a matter which does not affect the S.M.P.

Certified true copy.

然而，据知只有亲南京的日报和小报（mosquito papers）的校样在出版前由上海新闻检查局进行检查；然而，亲重庆的日报并不将校样提交给上海新闻检查局进行检查，而是遵守工部局的规定。
关于附件公文中对《宁波公报》和《中国商报》提出的投诉，必须指出的是，这两份报纸均属于小报类型，且不受工部局警务处检查。据本处所知，《宁波公报》已运营相当长一段时间，致力于发布宁波当地情况的消息，以供在上海的宁波居民了解；但据信，《中国商报》定期接受江苏浙江安徽统税局局长邵式军（Shao Chih-chun）的津贴，该局址位于九江路230号。
这两家报纸是否将其校样提交上海新闻检查局审查，是与工部局警务处无关的事项。

核证无误副本。
------------------

Sir,

In accordance with Instructional Order No. Wu 12135
of Shanghai Special Municipal Government it is stated:

" Communication No. Tao 124 has been received
from the Ministry of Propaganda to the follow-
ing effect:-
'With reference to various newspapers pub-
lished in Shanghai, a good number of them
send their draft articles to the Shanghai News
Censorship Office before publication in accord-
ance with the existing regulations while some
still have the objectionable parts already
deleted by the censor from the original draft
published thus constituting a breach of its in-
structions. According to recent reports of the
Shanghai News Censorship Office, "Ningpo Kung
Pao" and "Chung Kuo Shang Pao" in Shanghai
have repeatedly ignored the instructions of the
censor. In regard to news censorship, it is im-
portant propaganda policy. That the aforesaid
papers should disobey the instructions of the
censor is decidedly improper. Apart from warning
having been given to them we request that you
note and notify the police authorities under
your command to promptly render assistance and
establish liaison of some kind with the Shanghai
News Censorship Office with a view to facilitat-
ing news censorship. Please let us know in your
reply what action has been taken in this connec-
tion.'
In view of the above, you are directed to ap-
proach the Police Department of the S.M.C. for in-
structions to be issued to all newspapers within
its jurisdiction to submit to censorship."

In consequence of the foregoing, I may add that as
the matter concerns censorship administration the ins-
tructions of the censor should be strictly observed
and would request you to be good enough to render
assistance by notifying all the newspaper publishers

第30号公文

关于附件中1941年9月30日上海市政府警察局致代理警务处长的有关位于南京路哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）的上海新闻检查局的公文，必须指出的是，该局最初由日本华中派遣军和日本驻当地总领事馆联合成立，目的是控制当地的中文报纸，包括主要日报和小报。正是出于这个原因，一些当地的亲重庆中文日报以第三国国民的名义注册其出版物，从而逃避了上海新闻检查局的审查。后来，在1940年12月16日，该局正式移交给南京政府，名义上由汪精卫在上海的主要宣传机构《中华日报》主编刘石克（Lieu Zah-keh）负责；但实际上，它仍受日本人控制。

起初，即上海新闻检查局刚成立时，上海的中文报纸和通讯社寥寥无几。当时，几乎所有这些都服从上海新闻检查局的审查。目前，

关于附件公文中对《宁波公报》和《中国商报》提出的投诉，必须指出的是，这两份报纸均属于小报类型，且不受工部局警务处检查。据本处所知，《宁波公报》已运营相当长一段时间，致力于发布宁波当地情况的消息，以供在上海的宁波居民了解；但据信，《中国商报》定期接受江苏浙江安徽统税局局长邵式军（Shao Chih-chun）的津贴，该局址位于九江路230号。

这两家报纸是否将其校样提交上海新闻检查局审查，是与工部局警务处无关的事项。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.

Translation of Despatch No. le 30 from Police Bureau, S.S.M.G.
September 30, 1941.

Captain H.H. Smyth, O.B.E.,
Acting Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

In accordance with Instructional Order No. u 12135
of Shanghai Special Municipal Government it is stated:

"Communication No. Tao 124 has been received
from the Ministry of Propaganda to the follow-
ing effect:-
'With reference to various newspapers pub-
lished in Shanghai, a good number of them
send their draft articles to the Shanghai News
Censorship Office before publication in accord-
ance with the existing regulations while some
still have the objectionable parts already
deleted by the censor from the original draft
published thus constituting a breach of its in-
structions. According to recent reports of the
Shanghai News Censorship Office, "Ningpo Kung
Pao" and "Chung Kuo Shang Pao" in Shanghai
have repeatedly ignored the instructions of the
censor. In regard to news censorship, it is im-
portant propaganda policy. That the aforesaid
papers should disobey the instructions of the
censor is decidedly improper. Apart from warning
having been given to them we request that you
note and notify the police authorities under
your command to promptly render assistance and
establish liaison of some kind with the Shanghai
News Censorship Office with a view to facilitat-
ing news censorship. Please let us know in your
reply what action has been taken in this connec-
tion.'
In view of the above, you are directed to ap-
proach the Police Department of the S.M.C. for in-
structions to be issued to all newspapers within
its jurisdiction to submit to censorship."

根据上海特别市政府第 u 12135 号指令，内容如下：

“收到宣传部第 Tao 124 号公函，内容如下：
‘关于在上海出版的各类报纸，其中许多按照现行规定在出版前将稿件送交上海新闻检查所审查，而有些报纸仍将已被检查员从原稿中删除的可疑部分予以刊登，从而违反了其指令。根据上海新闻检查所的最近报告，上海的《宁波公报》和《中国商报》多次无视检查员的指令。新闻检查是重要的宣传政策。上述报纸不服从检查员指令的行为显然是不恰当的。除已向它们发出警告外，请贵方知悉并通知贵辖下的警察当局迅速提供协助，并与上海新闻检查所建立某种形式的联络，以促进新闻检查工作。请在回复中告知就此采取了何种行动。’
鉴于上述情况，现指示你方接洽工部局警务处，以便向其管辖范围内的所有报纸发布提交审查的指令。”

It might well be said that the publication of 
anti-Japanese articles by foreign registered Chinese 
language newspapers in the Settlement is prevalent because 
they enjoy neutrality and have the right to exercise 
impartiality in publishing every kind of news, no matter 
what consequences such publication may have. Actually, 
these papers are publishing anti-Japanese articles out of 
illewill and it is not a case of merely publishing any news 

that comes to their knowledge. In some cases, they publish 

anti-Japanese articles in order to increase circulation, 
but whatever their motive mey be, the publication of 
anti-Japanese articles tends to encourage and stimulate 
anti-Japanese feeling among the Chinese population of the 
Settlement. 

A close examination and analysis of the papers 
in question will disclose that they harbour strong anti- 
Japanese sentiments, and we fear that any leniency on 
the part of the Settlement authorities in dealing with such 
papers may be due to the fact that the authorities have 

failed to detect the anti-Japanese feeling harboured by 


the papers.

Settlement authorities@ over such papers is quite strong.

authorities have been sparing no efforts to restore peace 
and order in the Settlement, and we think that the 
Settlement authorities will recognize the fact that 
we, the Press Censorship Office, are also doing our bit 
in this respect through our work of censoring the 
Chinese newspapers. The foreign registered Chinese 
language newspapers, however, refuse to be censored by 
us and deliberately publish anti-Japanese articles that 
heve been prohibited publication by purely Chinese papers 
because they enjoy extraterritoriality. Their action 
tends to etitalete antieJapanese feeling among the 
Chinese population of the International Settlement; it also 
means that these foreign registered Chinese newspapers 
heave voluntarily abandoned their neutrality. If we 
reflect what conseauences the publication of anti-Japanese 
articles may have on the peace and order of the 
Settlement, we should not leave the matter neglected. 
Whatever efforts you may make to effect the arrest of 
the anti-Japanese terrorists, they will come to naught 
if you do not take action against anti-Japanese papers. 
Wé will not be far wrong if we say that the recent scts 
of terrorism were partly due to encdburagement and 
stimulation from anti-Japanese articles published by 
' foreign registered Chinese language newspapers. W#e think 
that the Police should take action against any paper 
the existence of which detrimental to the peace and order 
of the Settlement. We remember the case of the “China 


om 


Forum,” an American registered periodical, which was 
suppressed by your authority. we think -t is not 
impossible to suppress the existing anti-Japanese 
foreign registered Chinese language papers in a similar 
mannere 

We hereby request you to give consideration 
to this matter and to take adequate steps against the 


papers complained of. 


Yours sincerely, 


The Shanghai Press Censorship Office.

(From our Special Correspondent) 
Nanking, January 25. 
Yesterday morning the Central Political Council 
examinefione of the most interesting questians of the present 
time: the censorship of the press. - 
As the result of a petition submitted by the "Ta 
Kung Pao” ("The Impartial") of Tientsin and of the Mewspaper- 
men's Association of Shanghai, demanding greater freedom 
for the Chinese Press - a petition which was presented to 
the recent Plenary Congress of the members of the Kuomintang - 
the Central Political Council yesterday fixed the two 
following principles regarding the freedom of the Press:-~ 
1. The Press will henceforth be authorized t publish 
“mild criticiams" of joint acts of the Government and 
of the Party. 
They wil not be allowed to publish reports touching 
a@n military or diplomatic questions held to be secret 
or which may be. prejudicial to the national interests 
of China. ; 
2. Newspapers may not publish information relating to 
propaganda if such information is contrary to the Three 
Principles of the People.

It wuld be interesting, without doubt, to make 
a rapid survey of the manner dm which the varias censorship 
organs in the cities controlled by the Nanking Government carry 
out their work. 

At Nanking, every publication, under pain of 
being banned or confiscated, must be submitted to the

At Shenghai, apart from a so-called censa@ ship

had issued m appeal demanding ‘national unification", one

Readers will recollect that recently Hu Han Min,

an interview granted to this paper, declared that he had 
submit ted three conditions for his reconciliation with 
Nanking. The first of these conditions was the suppression 
of the censorship of the Press. 

Is it to appease the Opposition in Canton and to 
facilitate an alliance between the South-West and the 
Central Government that the Permanent Committee of the 
Central Executive Committee has taken this ‘etep, not to 
abolish the censorship but to define the principles on 
which thie censorship is based? - 

One section of the order reads: “all reports 
relating to the Party and to administrative affaires and 
all opinions expressed in good faith are allowed to be 7

published on the condition that they do not betray diplomatic 
and military secrets and they do not harm the policy of the 
Party er of the government. The newspapers must refrain 
trom expressing opinions that are contrary to those of the 
Kuomintang: 

In the first place, for an opinion on any affairs 
concerning the Kuomintang and the government to be prin ed 
in the Press, the anthor must be of good faith. This 
anxiety is ream nable. 

In the second place, no military or diplomtic 
secrets are to be disclosed. In principle, this prohibition 
need not trouble anybody for we do not believe that journalists 
possess as many secrets as tM dly informed people suppose they 
do. Most of the military or diplomatic information which 
they may possess wore furnished by the authorities themselves, 
consequently what they know is what the government wants them 
to know, especially so in China. Real diplomatic or military 
secrets are procured by spies and these people do not work for 
newspapers. 

In the third place, a newspaperman must not write 
anything that is harmful to the policy of the Kuomintang 
or the Government. This is something more severe and it 
will be interesting to learn if this will please the South- 
Weste 

As for us, we will confine ou selves to a criticism 
of the decision of the Central Executive Committee. In our 
opinion the question of the censorship of Chinese newspapers 
concerns the Chinese only. We would, however, like to make 
this remark: Most of the large Chinese newspapers in Shmghai 
and in North China are located in foreign settlements; they 
have submitted to government censorship because a very large 
number of their subscribers live outside the settlements as 
well as in the interior provinces. In order to be able 


reach them, it is necessary for papers to be in agreement 


Ne 


with the authorities. 

We would like to voice a strong protest against the 
illegal as well as absurd censorship which the Chinese 
lauthorities are exercising in an international settlement 
:on pelegrams which the corresponients of foreign newspapers 
-are daily sending to Europe and Americae 

This censorship is illegal on several counts. Above 
all it is being exercised in am international settlement 
when the right of censorship in the settlement belongs to 
the authorities of the settlement. In establishing their 
Sadincin pa miki VII, the Chinese Authorities have taken 
the place of the authorities of the International Settlement 
without having first consulted with them as well as without 
having been authorised to do so by @ Consular Body. 

The censorship of telegrams sent but by foreign 
newspaper correspomients to European and American rmwspapers, 
is, in our view, illegal because it is contrary to the 
principle of extraterritoriality, a right which most of 
the correspomients enjoy. 

The Chinese authorities realize fully that censorship 
is not defensible so much so that they are keeping it a secret. 
They have overlooked, however, that foreign newspapers are 
sent out to China and that each correspondent can easily 
ascertain whether his telegrams havebeen mutilated, delayed 
or even falsified. They also seem to have overlooked the 
fact that the editors of the newspapers in foreign countries 
will be surprised that a telegram sent from Shamghai at 1 am. 
on January 1 does not reach Paris until noon January 1, thaé 
is to say, much too late for the news to be uweful. The editors 
are also surprised to learn that a telegram handed in by the 
correspondent in Shmghai at 1 Am. Jemuary 1 is not despatched 
until 10 a.m. because the illegal censorship bureau had heli 
up the telegram for 9 hours. Perhaps the bureau had been

We have said that the censorship on foreign telegrams 
is illegal, we now add that it is absurd. It will be suffieient
